the plural: *El 62 % de los jóvenes se informa / se informan por redes sociales.* Both are
correct. (*Informarse* = to keep informed, to get the news.)

![A bar chart from an invented survey of young people about where they get their news: redes sociales 62 %, televisión 18 %, periódicos 13 %, radio 7 %.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Read the chart: *Según la encuesta, más de la mitad de los jóvenes (el 62 por ciento) se informa
por redes sociales. El 18 por ciento ve el noticiero en la tele, y solo el 7 por ciento escucha la
radio.* The survey is invented for this lesson.

## Pronunciation

- *Periodista*: four syllables, *pe-rio-DIS-ta*; the *io* glides together.
- *Millón, millones*: *ll* sounds like English *y* in most of Mexico: *mi-YÓN, mi-YO-nes*. The
  plural loses the written accent, because the stress stays on *-llo-* and the word now ends in
  *-s*.
- *Según* is stressed on the last syllable and ends in *n*, so it needs its accent: *se-GÚN*.
- *Encuesta*: *en-KWES-ta*.

## Common mistakes

- Dropping *que*: ~~*Dice está cansada*~~ → *Dice que está cansada.*
- Leaving out *si* in a yes/no question: ~~*Pregunta vienes*~~ → *Pregunta si vienes*. And no
  accent: *si* (whether), not *sí* (yes).
- Dropping the accent of the question word: ~~*Pregunta donde vives*~~ → *Pregunta dónde vives.*
- Keeping the speaker's person: *Ana dice que está cansada*, not ~~*Ana dice que estoy
  cansada*~~ (that means you are the tired one).
- Using the preterite for a state: ~~*Dijo que estuvo cansada*~~ (for "she said she was tired" at
  the time) → *Dijo que estaba cansada.*
- ~~*un millón personas*~~ → *un millón de personas*; ~~*los 40 por cientos*~~ → *el 40 por
  ciento*.

## Key points

- Reported speech now: *dice que* + the same tense. Change the person (*yo* → *él, ella*; *mi* →
  *su*), and never drop *que*.
- Yes/no questions: *pregunta si…* (no accent on *si*). Other questions keep the question word
  with its accent: *pregunta dónde, qué, cuándo…*
- In the past: *dijo que* + preterite for a finished event, + imperfect for a state or scene at
  the time (*Dijo que estaba cansada*).
- *Según* + source; headlines are short and often in the present.
- *un millón de personas, dos millones de pesos*; *el 40 por ciento de…*; Mexico writes *2.3
  millones*, Spain *2,3 millones*.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: What do you think? Opinions, reasons and the environment
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

In A1 you learned *creo que* for a simple opinion, and in lesson 06 *¿Qué te parece?* Now you'll
build a whole short argument: say what you think, ask what others think, agree or disagree
politely, give a reason and draw a conclusion. These are the moves of every conversation about
the news (lesson 21), and of the DELE A2 speaking and writing tasks (lessons 23 and 24). The theme
is the environment, recycling and animals, with a few facts about Mexico, each dated, since rules
like these change.

## Giving your opinion

| Phrase | Meaning |
|---|---|
| *Creo que…* | I think (that)… (the most common) |
| *Pienso que…* | I think… |
| *Me parece que…* | It seems to me that…, I think… |
| *Para mí,…* | For me,…, In my view,… |
| *En mi opinión,…* | In my opinion,… (a little more formal) |

After *creo que, pienso que* and *me parece que*, use the ordinary verb forms you know, the forms
of statements (grammars call them the indicative): *Creo que es importante. Me parece que
tienes razón. Pienso que el gobierno debe hacer más.*

*Creo que sí* (I think so) and *Creo que no* (I don't think so) answer a question without
repeating it: *¿Va a llover? — Creo que sí.*

### What about "no creo que"?

*No creo* alone is fine: *¿Viene Ana? — No creo.* (I don't think so.) But a full sentence after
*No creo que…* needs a new verb form that Spanish uses for doubt. It's taught at B1. For now,
put the *no* inside the sentence instead: *Creo que no es buena idea* (I don't think it's a good
idea). This is natural, everyday Spanish, not a workaround.

## Asking for an opinion

- *¿Qué opinas de…?* (*opinar* = to think, to have an opinion) — *¿Qué opinas de la nueva ley?* (What do you think of the new law?)
- *¿Qué piensas de…?* / *¿Qué piensa usted de…?*
- *¿Qué te parece…?* (lesson 06) — *¿Qué te parece la idea?*
- *¿Tú qué crees?* — What do you think? (an informal favorite: *tú* comes before *qué*.)
- *¿Estás de acuerdo?* — Do you agree?

Notice the two nouns: *la opinión* (plural *las opiniones*) and *la solución* (solution).

## Agreeing and disagreeing

*Estar de acuerdo* means "to agree"; it's a phrase with *estar*, so it changes for the person:
*Estoy de acuerdo, ¿estás de acuerdo?, no estamos de acuerdo.* Say who or what you agree with with
*con*: *Estoy de acuerdo contigo / con usted / con Ana / con eso.*

![A scale from full agreement to full disagreement. From left to right: Estoy totalmente de acuerdo; Tienes razón; Sí, pero…; Depende; Yo no lo veo así; No estoy de acuerdo.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

| Agree | In between | Disagree |
|---|---|---|
| *Estoy de acuerdo (contigo).* | *Sí, pero…* | *No estoy de acuerdo.* |
| *Tienes razón.* (You're right.) | *Depende.* (It depends.) | *Yo no lo veo así.* (I don't see it that way.) |
| *Claro. / ¡Exacto!* | *Puede ser.* (Maybe.) | *No tienes razón.* (blunt) |

*Totalmente* = completely. *Tener razón* (to be right) uses *tener*: *Tienes razón*, not ~~*Eres
correcto*~~ or ~~*Estás razón*~~. Disagreeing directly with *No tienes razón* can sound rude; *Yo no lo veo así* or
*Sí, pero…* is softer and more usual.

For short agreement, A1's *yo también / yo tampoco* and lesson 06's *a mí también / a mí tampoco*
still work: *Creo que hay demasiado plástico. — Yo también.*

## Giving a reason: *porque, como, por*

There are three ways to say why:

- *porque* (because) goes in the middle, after the result: *Reciclo porque hay demasiada
  basura.* It also answers *¿por qué?*: *¿Por qué no usas bolsas de plástico? — Porque
  contaminan.*
- *como* (since, as) goes at the start of the sentence, before the result:
  *Como hay demasiada basura, reciclo.* Don't start an answer to *¿por qué?* with *como*.
- *por* + a noun (lesson 14): *Cerraron la playa por la contaminación.* (They closed the beach
  because of the pollution.)

## Drawing a conclusion: *por eso, así que*

Both mean "so" or "that's why", and both come after the reason:

- *Hay mucho tráfico; por eso tomo la bici.* — There's a lot of traffic; that's why I take my bike.
  (*La bici* is short for *la bicicleta*.)
- *Mi edificio no tiene elevador, así que subo por la escalera.* — My building has no elevator,
  so I take the stairs.

*Por eso* (literally "for that") points back clearly at the reason, and can start a new sentence:
*La ciudad está creciendo. Por eso hay más contaminación.* *Así que* is more conversational and
usually joins two parts of the same sentence.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  accTitle: From a cause to a consequence
  accDescr: Three linked boxes. First, a cause: Usamos mucho plástico. An arrow labeled por eso leads to the consequence: Hay mucha basura en el mar. An arrow labeled así que leads to a decision: Llevo mi propia bolsa al mercado. A note at the side says that the same idea can start with como: Como usamos mucho plástico, hay mucha basura en el mar.
  A["Cause: Usamos mucho plástico."] -- "por eso" --> B["Consequence: Hay mucha basura en el mar."]
  B -- "así que" --> C["Decision: Llevo mi propia bolsa al mercado."]
  N["Or start with como: Como usamos mucho plástico, hay mucha basura en el mar."] -.- A
```

## *Es* + adjective + infinitive

To say what is good or necessary in general, without saying who should do it, use *es* + an
adjective + the infinitive:

- *Es importante reciclar.* — It's important to recycle.
- *Es mejor usar la bici.* — It's better to use a bike.
- *Es necesario proteger los bosques.* — It's necessary to protect the forests.
- *Es difícil cambiar las costumbres.* — It's hard to change habits.

There is no word for "it" in these sentences, and no *de* or *que* before the infinitive.
*Hay que* (A1) gives a general rule in the same way: *Hay que cuidar el agua.*

## The environment: words and some Mexican facts

*El medio ambiente* is the environment; *la contaminación* is pollution, and *contaminar* is to
pollute. People *reciclan* (recycle) and try to *proteger* (protect) and *cuidar* (look after) the
planet, while others *destruyen* (destroy) forests. *Proteger* is spelled with *j* before *o*:
*protejo*. *Destruir* adds a *y*: *destruyo, destruye, destruyen*; *destruyó, destruyeron*.

Other words: *el planeta* (masculine, like *el problema*), *la tierra* (earth, land, soil; with a
capital, *la Tierra* is the planet Earth), *el aire* (air), *la energía* (energy), *la botella*
(bottle), *el plástico*.

### Sorting the trash in Mexico City

*La basura* is trash or garbage, and you throw it in *el bote de basura* (Spain: *la papelera*
for a small one, *el cubo de la basura* in the kitchen). Since 1 January 2026, sorting household
waste is required in Mexico City. The city's campaign puts it into three main groups:
*orgánicos* (food scraps, garden waste), *inorgánicos reciclables* (paper, cardboard, plastic,
glass, cans) and *inorgánicos no reciclables* (for example, used toilet paper and diapers). The
organic waste is collected on some days of the week (Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday, as announced
in 2025) and the inorganic waste on the others, kept in separate bags. Rules and days can change,
so check the city's current information if you live there. Earlier, from 1 January 2020, stores in
the city stopped handing out single-use plastic bags.

![Three trash bins side by side, labeled Orgánicos, Inorgánicos reciclables and Inorgánicos no reciclables. The first, for organic waste, holds a banana peel, leaves and food scraps. The second, for recyclable inorganic waste, holds a plastic bottle, a can, a glass jar and a cardboard box. The third, for non-recyclable inorganic waste, holds a roll of toilet paper and a diaper.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

New words in passing: *la lata* (can), *el vidrio* (glass), *el cartón* (cardboard), *la
cáscara* (peel), *el pañal* (diaper).

### Animals

Six of the world's seven species of sea turtle (*la tortuga marina*) live in Mexican waters, and
Mexico has protected them with a total ban on catching them since 1990. Many beaches have camps
where volunteers protect the nests. Other words: *el pez* (a living fish; plural *los peces*; fish
you eat is *el pescado*, A1) and *la mascota* (pet).

*Cuidar* takes *a* before a person or a pet you look after: *Mi hermana cuida a mi perro cuando
viajo.* With things, no *a*: *Hay que cuidar el agua.*

## Dialogue: three bins in the kitchen

Sofía and Diego share an apartment in Mexico City.

> Diego: Sofía, ¿por qué hay tres botes de basura en la cocina?
>
> Sofía: Porque en la ciudad hay que separar la basura. Como no recogen la basura mezclada, la separamos en casa.
>
> Diego: Me parece mucho trabajo. ¿Tú crees que sirve para algo?
>
> Sofía: Creo que sí. Si separamos el plástico y el vidrio, se pueden reciclar.
>
> Diego: Bueno, tienes razón. ¿Y dónde pongo esta botella de jugo?
>
> Sofía: En el bote de reciclables. Y las cáscaras de plátano, en el de orgánicos.
>
> Diego: ¿Y este vaso de plástico? Tiene restos de comida.
>
> Sofía: Primero lo lavas y luego va con los reciclables.
>
> Diego: Está bien. Estoy de acuerdo contigo: es importante cuidar el planeta. Así que yo saco la basura orgánica los martes.
>
> Sofía: ¡Perfecto! Y yo, los jueves.

> Diego: Sofía, why are there three trash cans in the kitchen?
>
> Sofía: Because in the city you have to sort your trash. Since they don't pick up mixed trash, we sort it at home.
>
> Diego: It seems like a lot of work to me. Do you think it's any use?
>
> Sofía: I think so. If we separate the plastic and the glass, they can be recycled.
>
> Diego: OK, you're right. And where do I put this juice bottle?
>
> Sofía: In the recyclables can. And the banana peels in the organic one.
>
> Diego: And this plastic cup? It has food scraps in it.
>
> Sofía: First you wash it, and then it goes with the recyclables.
>
> Diego: All right. I agree with you: it's important to look after the planet. So I'll take out the organic trash on Tuesdays.
>
> Sofía: Perfect! And I'll do Thursdays.

*Separar* = to sort, to separate; *los restos* = scraps, leftovers. *El de orgánicos* = the one for
organic waste (the noun *bote* is understood).

## An opinion post

A reader writes to a newspaper's website.

> ¿Prohibir las botellas de plástico?
>
> En mi opinión, el gobierno debe prohibir las botellas de plástico pequeñas. Como casi nadie las
> recicla, terminan en la calle, en los ríos y en el mar, y destruyen la vida de los peces y las
> tortugas. Creo que la solución no es difícil: en muchas oficinas ya hay agua para todos, así que
> cada persona puede llevar su propia botella. Sé que para las empresas es un cambio grande, pero
> es necesario proteger el medio ambiente. Por eso estoy de acuerdo con la nueva propuesta.

> Banning plastic bottles?
>
> In my opinion, the government should ban small plastic bottles. Since almost nobody recycles
> them, they end up in the street, in rivers and in the sea, and they destroy the lives of fish
> and turtles. I think the solution isn't hard: many offices already have water for everyone, so
> each person can bring their own bottle. I know that for companies it's a big change, but it's
> necessary to protect the environment. That's why I agree with the new proposal.

*Prohibir* = to ban (*prohíbo, prohíbes*: written accent on the *í*); *casi* = almost;
*propio* = own; *la
propuesta* = proposal. The writer gives an opinion (*En mi opinión*), a reason (*Como…*), a
solution (*Creo que…, así que…*), admits the other side (*Sé que…, pero…*) and concludes (*Por
eso…*). That's a complete short argument, and a good model for the exam.

## Pronunciation

- *Medio ambiente*: in speech the two words run together, *me-dioam-BIEN-te*.
- *Contaminación*: five syllables, *con-ta-mi-na-CIÓN*; plural *contaminaciones* is rare.
- *Así que* is said as one unit, *a-SÍ-ke*; the *u* is silent.
- *Pez* ends in an *s* sound in Latin America (*pes*); the plural *peces* is *PE-ses*.

## Common mistakes

- ~~*Soy de acuerdo*~~ → *Estoy de acuerdo.* Agreement uses *estar*.
- ~~*Estoy de acuerdo a ti*~~ → *Estoy de acuerdo contigo.*
- ~~*Eres correcto*~~ for "you're right" → *Tienes razón.*
- Starting an answer to *¿Por qué?* with *como*: *¿Por qué reciclas? — Porque…*, not ~~*Como…*~~.
- ~~*Es importante de reciclar*~~ → *Es importante reciclar.*
- ~~*la planeta*~~ → *el planeta*: it's masculine, although it ends in *-a*.

## Key points

- Opinions: *creo que, pienso que, me parece que* + the ordinary forms; *para mí, en mi opinión*;
  *Creo que sí / Creo que no*. *No creo* alone; *No creo que* + a sentence is B1.
- Ask: *¿Qué opinas de…? ¿Qué te parece…? ¿Tú qué crees? ¿Estás de acuerdo?*
- Agree and disagree: *Estoy (no estoy) de acuerdo contigo; Tienes razón; Sí, pero…; Yo no lo veo
  así.*
- Reasons: *porque* in the middle, *como* at the start, *por* + noun. Results: *por eso, así que*.
- *Es importante / mejor / necesario* + infinitive.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Writing for real life: invitations, thanks, apologies and short texts
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

In A1 you wrote short messages of 30–40 words: a greeting, three or four sentences, a closing.
At A2 your messages get longer and do more: they invite, thank, apologize, congratulate, accept
and decline, and they tell what happened, with the past tenses of module 1 working together.
This lesson gives you the phrases for those jobs, the **[[connectors]]** that turn a list of
sentences into a text, and a method for writing to a word count, which is exactly what the DELE A2
writing test asks for. The theme is celebrations and social occasions in Mexico.

## What the exam asks you to write

The DELE A2 writing test (lesson 24 describes the whole exam) has two tasks, in general terms:

1. A reply to a message, an e-mail, a note or a letter that you read first, in about 60 to 70
   words. The task tells you what your reply must include: thank, answer a question, explain,
   suggest something.
2. A short text of about 70 to 80 words. You choose one of two options: one is usually about
   your own everyday life (an experience, a description, your habits), the other a short
   narrative or biography built from pictures or data that the task gives you.

Both are everyday writing. Practicing them is practicing real life.

## A method for short texts

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  accTitle: Five steps for writing a short text
  accDescr: A top-down chain of five steps. One, read the task and underline every point you must cover. Two, choose tú or usted, from who you are writing to. Three, write a short plan with one line per point. Four, write the text with connectors. Five, count the words and check verb endings, accents and tú or usted.
  A["1. Read the task. Underline every point."] --> B["2. tú or usted? Who are you writing to?"]
  B --> C["3. Plan: one line per point."]
  C --> D["4. Write, with connectors."]
  D --> E["5. Count the words. Check verbs, accents, tú or usted."]
```

- Cover every point. A missing point costs more than a small grammar mistake.
- Stay near the length. Very short texts can't cover the points; very long ones have more
  room for mistakes. Count roughly as you write: a line of handwriting is about 8 to 10 words.
- Write what you can say correctly. A simple, correct sentence beats an ambitious broken one.

## Register: *tú* or *usted*

**[[Register]]** is the level of formality you choose. Write to friends and family with *tú*; to a
landlord, a teacher you don't know well, a company or an official with *usted*. Then keep it the
same all the way through: *tu*, *te*, *-s* endings in one, *su*, *le*, *usted* forms in the other.

| | informal (*tú*) | formal (*usted*) |
|---|---|---|
| greeting (A1) | *Querida Ana:* / *Hola, Pablo:* | *Estimada señora Ruiz:* |
| first line | *¿Cómo estás? Te escribo para…* | *Le escribo para…* |
| closing | *Un abrazo, / Con cariño, / ¡Hasta pronto!* | *Atentamente, / Saludos cordiales,* |

- *Te escribo para…* (I'm writing to…) + an infinitive states your purpose at once: *Te escribo
  para darte las gracias. Le escribo para confirmar mi reservación.*
- *Con cariño* (with love, with affection) is warm, for family and close friends.
- *Hasta pronto* (see you soon) closes a friendly message or a conversation.
- *Espero que estés bien* (I hope you're well) is a common friendly opening. Learn it as a set
  phrase: its verb *estés* is a form you'll study at B1.

## Messages for occasions

| Job | Informal | Formal |
|---|---|---|
| thank | *¡Muchas gracias por el regalo! Te agradezco mucho la invitación.* | *Le agradezco su ayuda.* |
| apologize | *Perdón por no contestar antes. Lo siento mucho.* | *Le pido una disculpa por el retraso.* |
| congratulate | *¡Felicidades por tu graduación!* | *Lo felicito por su nuevo puesto.* / *La felicito…* |
| invite | *Te invito a mi casa el sábado. ¿Quieres venir?* | *Tenemos el gusto de invitarlo…* |
| accept | *¡Claro que voy! Te confirmo que voy con mi novio.* | *Confirmo mi asistencia.* |
| decline | *Lo siento, no puedo ir. Es que tengo un compromiso.* | *Lamento no poder asistir.* |

The formal phrases mean: *Le agradezco su ayuda* (thank you for your help), *Le pido una
disculpa por el retraso* (I apologize for the delay), *Lo felicito por su nuevo puesto*
(congratulations on your new job; *el puesto* here is a position), *Tenemos el gusto de
invitarlo* (we are pleased to invite you), *Confirmo mi asistencia* (I confirm that I'll attend)
and *Lamento no poder asistir* (I'm sorry I can't attend).

Notes on the verbs:

- *Disculparse* is to apologize (*me disculpo, te disculpas…*; *Te escribo para
  disculparme*), and *la disculpa* is an apology. In Mexico *pedir una disculpa* (literally
  "to ask for pardon") is a very common polite way to say "to apologize": *Te pido una disculpa.*
- *Felicitar* is to congratulate: *Te felicito* (informal), *Lo felicito / La felicito*
  (formal, to a man or a woman). The noun phrase *¡Felicidades!* is A1.
- *Asistir a* means "to attend", not "to assist": *Asistí a la boda de mi primo* (I attended
  my cousin's wedding). "To help" is *ayudar*. *La asistencia* is attendance.
- *Confirmar* is to confirm: *¿Puedes confirmar antes del viernes?*

## Connectors for a short text

| Job | Connectors | Example |
|---|---|---|
| sequence (A1) | *primero, luego, después, al final* | *Primero hubo una ceremonia y después, una fiesta.* |
| addition | *y, también, además* | *La comida estaba rica; además, había mariachi.* |
| contrast | *pero, aunque, sin embargo* | *Aunque llovió, la fiesta fue un éxito.* |
| cause (22) | *porque, como, por* + noun | *Como llegué tarde, no vi la ceremonia.* |
| consequence (22) | *por eso, así que* | *Estaba cansada, así que me fui temprano.* |

The three contrast words work differently:

- *pero* (but) joins two parts in the middle: *Quería ir, pero tenía que trabajar.*
- *aunque* (although, even though) can start the sentence or join the middle, and at this
  level it takes the ordinary verb forms: *Aunque estaba cansado, fui a la fiesta. Fui a la
  fiesta, aunque estaba cansado.* Don't add *pero* after an *aunque* part: ~~*Aunque estaba
  cansado, pero fui*~~.
- *sin embargo* (however) contrasts with the sentence before. It usually follows a period or
  a semicolon and is followed by a comma: *El salón era pequeño. Sin embargo, todos bailamos.*

*Un éxito* = a success (a false friend: "exit" is *la salida*).

## The past tenses together

A personal account usually mixes the three pasts you know:

- the **[[preterite]]** for the events, in order: *fuimos, hubo, comimos, bailamos*;
- the **[[imperfect]]** for the scene and the feelings: *había mucha gente, la música era buena,
  estaba nerviosa*;
- the **[[present perfect]]** for an experience up to now: *Nunca he bailado tanto.*

## Celebrations in Mexico

Family celebrations are big in much of Mexico, and many follow a typical pattern, though every
family does things its own way.

- *Los quince años* (also written *los XV años*) is a girl's fifteenth-birthday celebration,
  traditional in many Mexican families. It often starts with a religious ceremony and goes on
  with a party, a waltz with family members, dinner and dancing until late. The girl is *la
  quinceañera*.
- *El bautizo* is a baptism, usually followed by a meal with the family and the *padrinos*
  (godparents, A1).
- *La graduación* marks the end of school or university; *el aniversario* is an
  anniversary (of a wedding, of a company).
- *La despedida* is a farewell or a farewell party: *una despedida de soltera* is a
  bachelorette party. In a letter, the same word is the closing phrase (A1).

At any of these, *los invitados* (guests) thank *el anfitrión, la anfitriona* (the host,
the hostess); the hosts *adornan* (decorate) the room with *adornos* (decorations), there
is *un brindis* (a toast; plural *los brindis*) when everyone *brinda* (toasts) with
wine or *un refresco* (a soft drink), and of course *el pastel* (cake; Spain also says
*la tarta*). *El evento* and *la ceremonia* are the general words.

![An invitation card for Mariana's quince años. Labels point to los anfitriones (Rosa y Ernesto Díaz, at the top), la quinceañera (Mariana, in large letters), la fecha (Sábado 14 de marzo), la ceremonia (6:00 p. m., Parroquia de San José) and la dirección of the party hall (Av. Juárez 120, Puebla). A line at the bottom asks guests to confirm by 1 March.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The invitation ends with *Favor de confirmar tu asistencia*, a very Mexican formula ("please
confirm your attendance") that you'll see on invitations and forms. *La parroquia* is a parish
church, and *Con mucho cariño* at the top shows the warm tone of a family invitation.

## Three model texts

The word counts were checked by computer. Each text is original and written to the length of
the exam tasks.

### 1. A reply accepting an invitation (67 words)

Mariana has invited her cousin Lucía to her *quince años* and asked her to bring her parents.

> Querida Mariana:
>
> ¡Muchas gracias por la invitación a tus quince años! Claro que voy a asistir. Te confirmo que
> llegamos el sábado 14 en la mañana, mis papás y yo. Mi hermano no puede ir, porque tiene un
> examen el lunes. ¿Te ayudo con los adornos? Me encanta adornar mesas. Además, quiero llevarte
> un regalo especial: ¿qué te gustaría? Estoy muy emocionada. ¡Hasta pronto!
>
> Un abrazo,
> Lucía

*Emocionada* = excited. Lucía thanks, accepts, confirms who is coming, explains an absence, offers
help and asks a question: six moves, each in one or two short sentences.

### 2. Congratulations and an apology (65 words)

> Hola, Pablo:
>
> ¡Felicidades por tu graduación! Sé que trabajaste muchísimo y estoy muy orgulloso de ti. Te
> escribo para disculparme: el viernes no puedo ir a la ceremonia, porque tengo una junta
> importante en Monterrey. Lo siento mucho. Sin embargo, el sábado regreso, así que te invito a
> cenar. ¿Te parece bien el restaurante italiano del centro? Yo pago, claro.
>
> Con cariño,
> tu tío Arturo

*Orgulloso de ti* = proud of you. Notice the chain *porque* (reason) → *Sin embargo* (contrast)
→ *así que* (consequence).

### 3. A personal account (74 words)

> El año pasado fui a los quince años de mi prima Daniela, en Puebla. Primero hubo una
> ceremonia en la iglesia y después todos fuimos a un salón de fiestas enorme. Había más de
> doscientos invitados y la música era fantástica. Daniela llevaba un vestido azul y estaba muy
> contenta. Aunque yo no conocía a mucha gente, la pasé muy bien. Al final hubo un brindis y
> todos comimos pastel. ¡Nunca he bailado tanto!

> Last year I went to my cousin Daniela's quinceañera party in Puebla. First there was a
> ceremony in the church and then we all went to a huge party hall. There were more than two
> hundred guests and the music was fantastic. Daniela was wearing a blue dress and was very
> happy. Although I didn't know many people, I had a great time. At the end there was a toast
> and we all ate cake. I've never danced so much!

Events in the preterite (*fui, hubo, fuimos, comimos*), the scene in the imperfect (*había, era,
llevaba, estaba, conocía*), and one experience in the perfect (*nunca he bailado*). *El salón de
fiestas* is a party hall.

## Pronunciation

- *Bautizo*: *bau-TI-so*; *au* is one syllable, and *z* sounds like *s* in Latin America.
- *Quinceañera*: *kin-se-a-ÑE-ra*.
- *Anfitrión*: *an-fi-TRIÓN*; the plural *anfitriones* has no accent.
- *Aniversario*: *a-ni-ver-SA-rio*, five syllables.
- *Sin embargo* runs together in speech: *si-nem-BAR-go*.

## Common mistakes

- ~~*Voy a asistir mi amiga con la mudanza*~~ for "help" → *Voy a ayudar a mi amiga con la
  mudanza.* *Asistir a* is "to attend".
- ~~*Aunque llovió, pero fuimos*~~ → *Aunque llovió, fuimos.* (or *Llovió, pero fuimos.*)
- Starting formal and ending informal: ~~*Estimada señora Ruiz: … ¿Cómo estás? … Un beso*~~.
  Choose one register and keep it.
- Forgetting a point of the task, or writing 40 words when 70 are asked.
- ~~*Te escribo por darte las gracias*~~ → *Te escribo para darte las gracias* (purpose is *para*,
  lesson 14).
- ~~*los quinces años*~~ → *los quince años*: *quince* doesn't change here.

## Key points

- Exam writing in outline: a reply of about 60–70 words, and a short text of about 70–80 words
  on one of two options.
- Plan: underline every point, choose *tú* or *usted*, write, count, check.
- *Te escribo para…, Con cariño, Hasta pronto; Le escribo para…, Atentamente.*
- Thank (*gracias por, te agradezco*), apologize (*disculparse, pedir una disculpa*),
  congratulate (*felicitar*), confirm, *asistir a* (to attend).
- Contrast: *pero* in the middle, *aunque* + the ordinary forms (no *pero* after it), *sin
  embargo* after a period, with a comma.
- Personal accounts: preterite for events, imperfect for the scene, perfect for "ever, never".

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: The DELE A2 exam and review
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This is the last core lesson of Spanish A2. It explains what level A2 means, describes the
official A2 exam, the DELE A2 of the Instituto Cervantes, gives strategies for each of its four
tests and the words its instructions use, and reviews the grammar of the whole course with three
charts and pointers back to the lessons. The questions at the end cover the whole course: use them
as a final check.

You don't need to take the exam, but its free official model exam is a good way to check your
level.

## What A2 means

A2 is the second of the six levels of the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR), the
upper half of "basic user". The Instituto Cervantes describes each level in detail in its
curriculum, the *Plan curricular*. In plain words, at A2 you can:

- understand sentences and common expressions about things that matter in daily life: your
  family, shopping, work, your neighborhood, travel, health;
- handle simple, routine exchanges: buy a ticket, make an appointment, ask for and give
  directions, order, complain politely, arrange to meet;
- describe your background, your surroundings and your needs, and tell a short story or
  experience in the past;
- write short messages and simple texts: invitations, thanks, apologies, a short account of
  something that happened.

At A2 people still have to make allowances for you: you speak and write in short sentences, you
make mistakes, and you need the other person to slow down sometimes. That's normal for the level.

## The DELE A2

The DELE (*Diplomas de Español como Lengua Extranjera*) are official diplomas awarded by the
Instituto Cervantes on behalf of Spain's Ministry of Education, and they don't expire. The figures
below come from the official *Guía del examen DELE A2* (© 2022 Instituto Cervantes), in this
course's own words.

| Test | Time | Tasks | Points |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reading (*Comprensión de lectura*) | 60 minutes | 4 tasks, 25 questions | 25 |
| Listening (*Comprensión auditiva*) | 40 minutes | 4 tasks, 25 questions | 25 |
| Writing (*Expresión e interacción escritas*) | 45 minutes | 2 tasks | 25 |
| Speaking (*Expresión e interacción orales*) | 12 minutes, after 12 minutes to prepare | 3 tasks | 25 |

The 100 points are split into two groups of 50: group 1 is reading + writing, group 2 is
listening + speaking. You need at least 30 points in each group. The result is *Apto* (pass) or
*No apto* (fail). A strong group can't rescue a weak one: 46 points in group 1 and 29 in group 2
is *No apto*, although the total is 75.

![A diagram of the DELE A2. Four boxes: reading, 60 minutes; writing, 45 minutes; listening, 40 minutes; speaking, 12 minutes after 12 minutes of preparation; each worth 25 points. Reading and writing form group 1, listening and speaking form group 2, each of 50 points. Under each group: at least 30. At the bottom: 30 or more in both groups gives Apto.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

### What each test asks, in general terms

- Reading: a personal letter or e-mail; several short public texts such as ads, notices and
  blog posts; a few practical texts such as leaflets, recipes or job offers; and a longer
  narrative such as a biography, a diary or a news story. You choose answers from three options
  or match statements to texts. Wrong answers lose no points.
- Listening: short everyday conversations (you answer by choosing pictures), short radio items
  such as news and ads, a longer conversation, and short announcements and recorded phone
  messages. Each recording is played twice, with time before it to read the questions.
- Writing: a reply of about 60–70 words to a message you read, and a short text of about
  70–80 words, choosing one of two options: an everyday personal topic, or a short narrative or
  biography built from pictures or data (lesson 23 and honors 24h2).
- Speaking: a short talk on one of two topics, prepared in advance (2–3 minutes); a
  description of a photo of an everyday situation (2–3 minutes); and a conversation with the
  examiner based on that photo, as in a role play (3–4 minutes). You may make notes while you
  prepare and look at them during the test.

Which Spanish? The guide says the exam's texts draw on present-day Spanish from Spain, so you
will read and hear *vosotros*, *el ordenador*, *el móvil*, *la papelera* and *Hoy he comido*.
In your answers, any standard variety of Spanish is accepted as long as you use it consistently.
Answer in the Mexican Spanish of this course, and recognize Spain's words (the vocabulary notes
give them).

Formats, dates and fees can change, so check the official pages before you register:

- [DELE A2 exam guide (PDF, Instituto Cervantes)](https://agenda.cervantes.es/sites/default/files/DELE_A2_v2020_Gu%C3%ADa_de_examen_0.pdf)
- [Preparing for the DELE: free model exams with audio, transcripts and answers](https://agenda.cervantes.es/es/node/27166889)
- [DELE: the official page of the Instituto Cervantes](https://cervantes.org/es/examenes/dele)

## The words of exam and textbook instructions

Instructions in exams and textbooks usually address you as *usted*, with *usted* commands:

| Instruction | Meaning |
|---|---|
| *Lea las instrucciones.* | Read the instructions. |
| *Escuche la grabación dos veces.* | Listen to the recording twice. |
| *Marque la opción correcta.* | Mark the correct option. |
| *Indique si la frase es verdadera o falsa.* | Say whether the sentence is true or false. |
| *Escriba un texto de aproximadamente 70 palabras.* | Write a text of about 70 words. |
| *Describa la foto.* | Describe the photo. |
| *Revise su texto y corrija los errores.* | Check your text and correct the mistakes. |

- *Corregir* (to correct) changes *e* → *i* like *pedir* and spells the *g* sound as *j*
  before *o* and *a*: *corrijo, corriges, corrige, corregimos, corrigen*; preterite *corregí,
  corrigió, corrigieron*; gerund *corrigiendo*; commands *corrige* (*tú*), *corrija* (*usted*).
- *Revisar* is to check or look over (a text, your work, a car). For studying before an exam,
  use *repasar* (lesson 18).
- *La lectura* is reading, or a reading text; *la comprensión* is understanding (*la
  comprensión de lectura*, reading comprehension); *oral* means spoken (*la expresión oral*).
- *La frase* is a sentence or a phrase; *el párrafo* a paragraph; *el resumen* a
  summary.
- *El punto* is a point in a score (*Saqué 18 puntos*) and also a dot or a period.
- *El candidato, la candidata* is a candidate (in an exam or an election).

## Strategies for each test

Reading. Read the questions first, then look for the part of the text that answers them.
Wrong options often repeat a word from the text but change the meaning: *antes* / *después*,
*todos* / *algunos*, *siempre* / *ya no*. Small words matter: *no, nunca, nadie, ninguno,
tampoco, solo, todavía no*. Don't leave anything blank, since wrong answers cost nothing.

Listening. Use the time before each recording to predict: is the answer a time, a price, a
place, a person? Listen the first time for the general idea and the second time for the detail.
Watch for corrections and changes of plan: *Iba a venir el martes, pero al final viene el
jueves.* The final version counts.

Writing. Follow the method of lesson 23: underline every point in the task, choose *tú* or
*usted*, plan one line per point, write with connectors, count, check. Check especially past
forms (*fui, hice, tuve; estaba, había*), accents, agreement, and pronouns (*se lo di*).

Speaking. Prepare the talk with a simple plan: an opening, three or four ideas in present,
past and future, a closing. In the photo description, go from general to detail: *En la foto
hay…; En primer plano…; Al fondo…; A la izquierda un señor está leyendo…; Creo que es…* (lesson
09). In the conversation, react and ask: *¿Ah, sí? ¿Y cuánto cuesta? ¿Me podría dar…?* If you
don't understand, ask: *Perdón, ¿puede repetir? ¿Qué significa…?* Honors lesson 24h2 has full
models.

## Grammar review

### Which past?

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  accTitle: Which past tense?
  accDescr: A decision chart for Mexican Spanish. First question: is it an experience up to now, or something that hasn't happened yet? If yes, use the present perfect, for example Nunca he ido a Oaxaca, Todavía no he terminado. If no, second question: is it background, such as a description, a habit, an action in progress, the time or someone's age? If yes, use the imperfect, for example Llovía, De niño jugaba en el patio, Tenía ocho años. If no, it is a finished event: use the preterite, for example Ayer llegué tarde, Hoy comí en casa.
  A["Talking about the past"] --> B{"An experience up to now, or 'not yet'?"}
  B -- yes --> C["Present perfect: Nunca he ido a Oaxaca. Todavía no he terminado. (04)"]
  B -- no --> D{"Background: description, habit, action in progress, time, age?"}
  D -- yes --> E["Imperfect: Llovía. De niño jugaba en el patio. Tenía ocho años. (02, 03)"]
  D -- no --> F["Preterite: a finished event, even today in Mexico. Ayer llegué tarde. Hoy comí en casa. (01, 03)"]
```

This is a simplification of lessons 01–04: most of Spain uses the perfect for today (*Hoy he comido en
casa*), and a few verbs change meaning between the two pasts (*conocí* = I met, *conocía* = I
knew; lesson 03).

### Where the pronouns go

![A chart of pronoun order. A row of slots: no, then the indirect pronoun (me, te, se, nos), then the direct pronoun (lo, la, los, las), then the conjugated verb: No se lo di. Below, three verbs where the pronouns can attach at the end: an infinitive, voy a dártelo; a gerund, estoy leyéndolo; an affirmative command, dímelo. A note: le and les become se before lo, la, los, las.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

- Order: indirect before direct, both before a conjugated verb: *Te lo presto. No se las mandé.*
  (lessons 05–07)
- *le, les* + *lo, la, los, las* → *se lo, se la…* (lesson 07)
- With an infinitive or a gerund, before the helper verb or attached: *Te lo voy a dar / Voy a
  dártelo; Lo estoy leyendo / Estoy leyéndolo* (05, 09). With an affirmative command, always
  attached: *Dímelo, Póngaselo* (16).

### The future, *ir a* and the conditional

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  accTitle: Future, ir a, present or conditional?
  accDescr: A decision chart. First question: is it a polite request, a wish or advice? If yes, use the conditional, for example ¿Podría ayudarme?, Me gustaría ir, Deberías descansar. If no, second question: is it a fixed arrangement or timetable? If yes, use the present, for example Mañana salgo a las ocho. If no, third question: is it a plan or intention in conversation? If yes, use ir a plus infinitive, for example Voy a estudiar medicina. If no, use the future for predictions, forecasts and promises, for example Mañana lloverá, Te llamaré.
  A["Later, or politely?"] --> B{"A polite request, a wish or advice?"}
  B -- yes --> C["Conditional: ¿Podría ayudarme? Me gustaría ir. Deberías descansar. (19, 20)"]
  B -- no --> D{"A fixed arrangement or timetable?"}
  D -- yes --> E["Present: Mañana salgo a las ocho. (13)"]
  D -- no --> F{"A plan or intention, in conversation?"}
  F -- yes --> G["ir a + infinitive: Voy a estudiar medicina. (A1, 13)"]
  F -- no --> H["Future: predictions, forecasts, promises. Mañana lloverá. Te llamaré. (13)"]
```

The boundaries are soft: *Te voy a llamar* and *Te llamaré* can both be a promise. The chart
shows the most usual choice in Mexico.

### The rest of the course

| Topic | The core idea | Lessons |
|---|---|---|
| *estar* + gerund | *Estoy platicando; estaba lloviendo* | 09 |
| describing people | *Es alta y tiene el pelo rizado; lleva lentes* | 10 |
| comparing | *más de un millón, tanto como, el más grande del país, riquísimo* | 11 |
| indefinites | *No hay ningún problema; No vino nadie* | 12 |
| *por* and *para* | *para ti, para el lunes; por la lluvia, por 900 pesos* | 14 |
| verb + infinitive | *acabo de llegar, volví a llamar, dejé de fumar* | 15 |
| impersonal *se* | *Se busca mesero; Se venden casas* | 17 |
| relative words | *la escuela donde estudié; lo que dices* | 18 |
| reported speech | *Dice que llega mañana; Dijo que estaba cansada* | 21 |
| opinions, reasons | *Creo que…; Estoy de acuerdo; como…, por eso…* | 22 |
| connectors | *aunque, sin embargo, además, así que* | 23 |

## Dialogue: before the exam

Emma is taking the DELE A2 next week. Her friend Rodrigo helps her practice.

> Rodrigo: ¿Cómo vas con la preparación?
>
> Emma: Bien, creo. Ya hice dos exámenes de prueba. En la lectura saqué 21 puntos, pero en la comprensión auditiva solo 15.
>
> Rodrigo: ¿Qué es lo más difícil?
>
> Emma: Las grabaciones. Hablan muy rápido y usan "vosotros". Al principio no entendía nada.
>
> Rodrigo: ¿Y ahora?
>
> Emma: Ahora escucho la radio todos los días, y leo las preguntas antes de cada grabación. Me ayuda mucho.
>
> Rodrigo: ¿Y la expresión oral? ¿Ya preparaste el monólogo?
>
> Emma: Sí, pero cometo errores con el pretérito. Ayer dije "yo hací" en lugar de "yo hice".
>
> Rodrigo: Bueno, eso se corrige practicando. Descríbeme esta foto, y yo te corrijo.
>
> Emma: Va. En la foto hay una familia en un parque. En primer plano, una niña está jugando con un perro…

> Rodrigo: How's your preparation going?
>
> Emma: Well, I think. I've already done two practice exams. In reading I got 21 points, but in listening only 15.
>
> Rodrigo: What's the hardest part?
>
> Emma: The recordings. They talk very fast and use "vosotros". At first I didn't understand anything.
>
> Rodrigo: And now?
>
> Emma: Now I listen to the radio every day, and I read the questions before each recording. It helps a lot.
>
> Rodrigo: And speaking? Have you prepared your talk yet?
>
> Emma: Yes, but I make mistakes with the preterite. Yesterday I said "yo hací" instead of "yo hice".
>
> Rodrigo: Well, you fix that by practicing. Describe this photo for me, and I'll correct you.
>
> Emma: OK. In the photo there's a family in a park. In the foreground, a girl is playing with a dog…

*Un examen de prueba* is a practice exam; *cometer un error* is to make a mistake; *en lugar de* =
instead of; *¿Cómo vas con…?* = how's … going?; *al principio* = at first; *Va* (Mexico,
informal) = OK. *Hablan muy rápido* uses *rápido* as an adverb (fast). *Se corrige practicando*
uses the gerund for "by" doing something.

## What comes next

At B1 you'll meet the forms this course kept out: the present subjunctive (*Quiero que
vengas; No creo que llueva; No te preocupes* as a real form, not a chunk), the pluperfect (*Cuando
llegué, ya había empezado*, previewed in honors 04h2), conditional sentences such as *Si tuviera
tiempo, viajaría*, and longer texts with more connectors. Keep your vocabulary reviews going, read
the graded readers on the course's reading list, and listen to Spanish every day: the radio and
podcasts of honors lesson 93 are a good start.

## Pronunciation

- *Corregir, corrijo*: the *g* before *e* and the *j* sound the same, a soft breathy *h* in
  Mexico: *co-rre-HIR, co-RRI-ho*. The *rr* is trilled.
- *Grabación*: *gra-ba-SIÓN*; plural *grabaciones* without an accent.
- *Comprensión*: *com-pren-SIÓN*, with *s*, not the English *sh* of "comprehension".
- *Vocabulario*: *vo-ca-bu-LA-rio*, five syllables; *b* and *v* sound the same.

## Common mistakes

- ~~*Yo corrego*~~ → *Yo corrijo*: e → i, and *g* → *j* before *o*.
- ~~*hacer un error*~~ → *cometer un error* (to make a mistake).
- *Revisar* means to check: ~~*Voy a revisar para el examen*~~ (for studying) → *Voy a repasar
  para el examen.*
- Thinking the total decides the result: each group (reading + writing, listening + speaking)
  needs 30 points.
- Switching between Mexican and Spain's Spanish in the same answer. Recognize *vosotros*, but
  write *ustedes*.

## Key points

- A2: you can manage routine everyday situations, tell simple stories in the past and write short
  messages and texts.
- DELE A2: reading 60 min, listening 40 min, writing 45 min, speaking 12 min (plus 12 to
  prepare), 25 points each. Group 1 (reading + writing) and group 2 (listening + speaking) each
  need 30 of 50 for *Apto*. The diplomas don't expire.
- The exam's texts use Spain's Spanish; answers in Latin American Spanish are accepted.
- Instructions: *Lea, Escuche, Marque, Indique si es verdadero o falso, Revise, Corrija*.
- Which past: perfect for experiences and "not yet", imperfect for background, preterite for
  events. Pronouns: indirect + direct, *le* → *se*. Future for predictions and promises, *ir a*
  for plans, conditional for politeness.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson. ¡Felicidades! You have finished the core of Spanish A2.

lessons.title: Honors: She said she would come: reporting in the past
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

In lesson 21 you reported speech with *dice que* + the same tense, and with *dijo que* + the
preterite for a finished event or the imperfect for a state. That's enough for everyday
conversation. Written news, books and careful speech go further: when the report is in the past,
almost every tense moves one step back. *"Vendré"* becomes *Dijo que vendría*; *"He terminado"*
becomes *Dijo que había terminado*. This lesson shows the whole system, the verbs that make
reports precise (*anunciar, asegurar, negar, advertir…*), and how questions and commands are
reported. Some of the forms are B1, so the aim is to recognize them all and to produce the ones
you already know.

## The tense shifts

When the reporting verb is in the past (*dijo, contó, explicó*), each tense of the original moves
back in time. This is the **[[tense shift]]**, and English does nearly the same thing (*"I'm tired"*
→ she said she *was* tired).

| Original | Reported after *dijo que…* | Example |
|---|---|---|
| present | imperfect | *"Vivo en Mérida."* → *Dijo que vivía en Mérida.* |
| *ir a* (present) | *ir a* (imperfect: *iba a*) | *"Voy a votar."* → *Dijo que iba a votar.* |
| future | **[[conditional]]** | *"Te llamaré."* → *Dijo que me llamaría.* |
| present perfect | **[[pluperfect]]** | *"He terminado."* → *Dijo que había terminado.* |
| preterite | pluperfect, or the preterite | *"Perdí el vuelo."* → *Dijo que había perdido el vuelo* / *que perdió el vuelo.* |
| imperfect | no change | *"Estaba cansada."* → *Dijo que estaba cansada.* |
| conditional | no change | *"Me gustaría ir."* → *Dijo que le gustaría ir.* |

![A chart of tense shifts in reported speech. Five arrows, each from what someone said to how it is reported after dijo que: present (estoy) to imperfect (estaba); ir a (voy a) to iba a; future (vendré) to conditional (vendría); present perfect (he terminado) to pluperfect (había terminado); preterite (llegué) to pluperfect (había llegado) or, in speech, the preterite. A note: the imperfect and the conditional don't change.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Three notes on the forms:

- The conditional is the future stem + *-ía* (lesson 19): *vendría, tendría, haría, diría,
  podría, sabría*. So the irregular futures of lesson 13 give the irregular conditionals here.
- The pluperfect ("had done") is *había, habías, había, habíamos, habían* + the participle:
  *había terminado, habían salido*. It's a B1 form, previewed in honors lesson 04h2. Recognize
  it; you can use it in writing if you're sure.
- With the preterite, both versions are correct. Mexican speech very often keeps the preterite
  (*Dijo que perdió el vuelo*); careful writing and news prefer the pluperfect (*Dijo que había
  perdido el vuelo*), especially when the order of events matters.

And, as in lesson 21: when the reported fact is still true now, the present can stay. *Me dijo
que vive en Mérida* means she still lives there; *Me dijo que vivía en Mérida* just reports her
words.

### Example 1: shifting a statement step by step

Carlos said last week: *"Mañana voy a Monterrey. He comprado el boleto y volveré el viernes."*
Report it today.

1. Choose the frame: it was last week, so *Carlos dijo que…*
2. *voy a Monterrey*: present → imperfect. But *voy a* + a place is just *ir*, so *iba a
   Monterrey*.
3. *mañana*: his "tomorrow" is not ours → *al día siguiente* (the next day).
4. *He comprado*: present perfect → pluperfect, *había comprado*.
5. *volveré*: future → conditional, *volvería*.

Result: *Carlos dijo que al día siguiente iba a Monterrey, que había comprado el boleto y que
volvería el viernes.* Notice *que* repeated before each part: it keeps the report clear.

## Time and place words

The time and place change with the point of view, as you saw in lesson 21:

| Original | In a past report |
|---|---|
| *hoy* | *ese día* (that day) |
| *mañana* | *al día siguiente* (the next day) |
| *ayer* | *el día anterior* (the day before) |
| *la semana que viene* | *la semana siguiente* |
| *ahora* | *en ese momento* (lesson 03) |
| *aquí* | *allí, ahí* |
| *este, esta* | *ese, esa* |

*Venir* and *ir* can swap too, depending on where you are when you report: *"¿Vienes a mi
casa?"* can become *Me preguntó si iba a su casa*. Don't force these changes: if the time and place are the same for you and the speaker, keep the
original words. *Ana me dijo hace una hora que hoy no viene* (still today) is perfectly natural.

## Reporting verbs

*Decir* works everywhere, but news and careful writing vary it, and each verb adds meaning:

| Verb | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| *anunciar* | to announce | *El gobierno anunció que habría más trenes.* |
| *afirmar* | to state | *La directora afirmó que el proyecto era seguro.* |
| *asegurar* | to assure, to say for sure | *El técnico aseguró que lo arreglaría ese día.* |
| *negar* (*niego*) | to deny | *El vocero negó la noticia.* |
| *aclarar* | to clarify | *El vocero aclaró que la tienda seguía abierta.* |
| *advertir* (*advierto*) | to warn | *Los bomberos advirtieron que el humo era peligroso.* |
| *agregar* | to add (lesson 16) | *Agregó que no había heridos.* |
| *comentar, explicar, contar* | to remark, explain, tell | *Explicó que el vuelo salía tarde.* |
| *responder, contestar* | to reply, answer | *Respondió que no sabía nada.* |

*Negar* is an *e → ie* verb (*niego, niegas, niega, negamos, niegan*) with *gu* before *e* in the
preterite (*negué*). After *negar que*, Spanish normally uses the subjunctive, a B1 form, so at A2 use *negar* with a noun (*Negó la noticia*) or say *dijo que no…*: *Dijo que no era
verdad.* *Advertir* changes like *sentir*: *advierto, advierte*; *advirtió, advirtieron*;
*advirtiendo*.

News also has its own nouns: *la conferencia de prensa* (press conference; Spain also says *la
rueda de prensa*), *la declaración* (statement), *el vocero, la vocera* (spokesperson, the usual
word in Mexico; Spain *el portavoz*), *el reportaje* (a news feature or in-depth report, longer
than *una noticia*).

## Reported questions in the past

Questions shift like statements, and keep *si* or the question word:

- *"¿Vienes a la fiesta?"* → *Me preguntó si iba a la fiesta.* (present → imperfect, and
  *venir* → *ir* from my point of view now; *si venía* is also correct.)
- *"¿Dónde has dejado las llaves?"* → *Me preguntó dónde había dejado las llaves.*
- *"¿Qué harás en vacaciones?"* → *Me preguntó qué haría en vacaciones.*

### Example 2: three questions from a job interview

Paula had an interview yesterday. The interviewer asked: *"¿Cuántos años ha trabajado en
ventas? ¿Por qué quiere cambiar de empresa? ¿Podrá empezar el lunes?"* Paula tells a friend:

> *Me preguntó cuántos años había trabajado en ventas, por qué quería cambiar de empresa y si
> podría empezar el lunes.*

- *ha trabajado* → *había trabajado* (perfect → pluperfect); *quiere* → *quería* (present →
  imperfect); *podrá* → *podría* (future → conditional).
- The interviewer's *usted* becomes Paula's *yo*. In these tenses the *yo* and *usted* forms are
  the same (*había, quería, podría*), so only the tense changes.
- *Cuántos* and *por qué* keep their accents; the yes/no question gets *si*. *Las ventas* =
  sales.

## Reported commands: recognition only

A command is reported with *decir que* or *pedir que* + another new form, the past subjunctive
(B1):

- *"Llámame."* → *Me dijo que lo llamara.* (He told me to call him.)
- *"Traigan su identificación."* → *Nos pidieron que trajéramos la identificación.*
- *"No llegues tarde."* → *Me dijo que no llegara tarde.*

You don't need to produce *llamara, trajéramos, llegara* yet: recognize the *-ara, -iera* ending
as "a reported command or wish". To report a command with A2 grammar, use *tener que* or quote
the person directly:

- *Me dijo que tenía que llamarlo.* — He told me I had to call him.
- *Me dijo: "Llámame mañana".* — He told me: "Call me tomorrow."

## A news article retold

### Example 3: from quotes to a report

Here is an invented news item with direct quotes, the way a newspaper might print it after a press
conference:

> *En una conferencia de prensa, la directora del Museo de San Martín, Elena Ortiz, anunció:
> "El museo va a cerrar en enero. Abriremos otra vez en septiembre con tres salas nuevas. Ya
> hemos recibido dinero del gobierno del estado". Ortiz aseguró: "Las obras no causan
> problemas a los vecinos". El vocero del museo aclaró: "La tienda sigue abierta". También
> advirtió: "Hoy es el último día para comprar boletos con descuento".*

*La sala* here is a room in a museum (A1's *la sala* is a living room); *las obras* are building
works; *causar* = to cause; *el descuento* = discount. Notice that standard Spanish (RAE) puts
the period after the closing quotation mark: *…sigue abierta".*

A week later, a radio presenter retells it without quotes:

> *La directora del Museo de San Martín, Elena Ortiz, anunció en una conferencia de prensa que
> el museo iba a cerrar en enero y que abriría otra vez en septiembre con tres salas nuevas.
> Explicó que ya habían recibido dinero del gobierno del estado y aseguró que las obras no
> causaban problemas a los vecinos. El vocero del museo aclaró que la tienda seguía abierta, y
> advirtió que ese día era el último para comprar boletos con descuento.*

Line by line:

| Quote | Report | Shift |
|---|---|---|
| *va a cerrar* | *iba a cerrar* | *ir a*: present → imperfect |
| *Abriremos* | *abriría* | future → conditional; the subject is now *el museo* |
| *hemos recibido* | *habían recibido* | perfect → pluperfect |
| *no causan* | *no causaban* | present → imperfect |
| *sigue abierta* | *seguía abierta* | present → imperfect |
| *Hoy es el último día* | *ese día era el último* | *hoy* → *ese día*; present → imperfect |

*Abriremos* becomes *abriría* (singular, the museum) in this version; *abrirían* (plural, the
museum's staff) would also be correct, as *habían recibido* shows. Both are natural.

### Example 4: the same story, told quickly in speech

Ana heard the press conference on the radio news that morning and tells a friend the same
evening:

> *Oye, dijeron en la radio que el museo cierra en enero y que lo van a abrir otra vez en
> septiembre. ¡Y hoy es el último día para comprar boletos con descuento!*

Because it's still the same day and the plans are still in the future, Ana keeps the present and
*ir a*. Spoken Spanish shifts tenses only as far as the meaning needs; the full shifts belong to
reports of something that is over or far from now. *Oye* = listen, hey (A1's *oír*). *Dijeron*
with no subject = "they said", someone on the radio.

## Common mistakes

- Keeping the future for a plan that is now in the past: ~~*Dijo que vendrá al día siguiente*~~
  for "she said she would come the next day" → *Dijo que vendría al día siguiente.* (In speech
  you'll also hear *Dijo que venía al día siguiente*, from a present with future meaning, *"Vengo
  mañana"*; that is correct too.)
- Using the conditional for a past fact: ~~*Dijo que estaría cansada*~~ (she said she would be
  tired) when she said *"Estoy cansada"* → *Dijo que estaba cansada.*
- Forgetting *si* in a reported yes/no question: ~~*Me preguntó iba a la fiesta*~~ → *Me preguntó
  si iba a la fiesta.*
- Keeping the speaker's *yo* and *tú*: Pedro said to me *"Te ayudo"* → *Pedro dijo que me
  ayudaba / que me iba a ayudar*, not ~~*que te ayudo*~~.
- Writing *habia* without the accent: *había, habían*.

## Key points

- After a past reporting verb, tenses move back: present → imperfect, future → conditional
  (*vendría*), perfect → pluperfect (*había terminado*), preterite → pluperfect or preterite;
  imperfect and conditional stay.
- If the fact or the time is still current, the original tense and words can stay.
- Time and place change with the point of view: *mañana* → *al día siguiente*, *ayer* → *el día
  anterior*, *hoy* → *ese día*, *aquí* → *allí*.
- Reporting verbs: *anunciar, afirmar, asegurar, negar, aclarar, advertir, agregar, responder*.
- Reported commands use a B1 form (*Me dijo que lo llamara*): recognize it; produce *Me dijo que
  tenía que…* or quote directly.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Honors: DELE A2 writing and speaking in practice
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 23 gave you a method for short texts, and lesson 24 described the DELE A2. This lesson
puts both to work. You'll follow two writing tasks from the prompt to a finished text, with a
first draft, the corrections a teacher would mark, and a clean second version, all with checked
word counts. Then you'll plan and hear models for the three speaking tasks: a short talk, a
photo description and a conversation. Everything here is original practice material in the
general format of the exam, not copied from it; for the real thing, use the free official model
exam linked in lesson 24.

A few words you'll need first: *el borrador* (draft), *el esquema* (outline, plan), *la
ortografía* (spelling), *la tilde* (written accent, the mark itself), *la mayúscula* (capital
letter), *el examinador, la examinadora* (examiner), *el monólogo* (monologue, a talk by one
person).

## Writing task 1: a reply

### Example 1: Valeria's e-mail

*The prompt* (in the style of the exam): your friend Valeria sends you this e-mail. Reply in
60–70 words. Welcome her, recommend a neighborhood, answer her question about transport and
suggest a day to meet.

> *¡Hola! ¿Cómo estás? Te tengo una noticia: ¡el mes que viene me mudo a tu ciudad! Encontré
> trabajo en una empresa del centro. ¿Qué colonia me recomiendas para vivir? ¿Es fácil moverse
> en transporte público? Me encantaría verte el primer fin de semana. Un abrazo, Valeria*

*Moverse* = to get around; *el transporte público* = public transportation.

*Step 1: the plan.* One line per point, in note form, is enough: *bienvenida → colonia Las
Flores (tranquila, segura, cerca del centro) → metro, autobuses, hora pico → comer el sábado.*
Register: *tú* (a friend).

*Step 2: the first draft* (56 words):

> Querida Valeria:
>
> ¡Qué buena noticia! Bienvenido (1) a la ciudad. Te recomiendo la colonia Las Flores: es
> tranquila, segura y es (2) cerca del centro. Además, hay muchos parques. Moverse en transporte
> publico (3) es fácil: hay metro y autobuses, pero en la hora pico hay mucho (4) gente. ¿Qué le
> (5) parece si comemos juntas el sábado?
>
> Un abrazo,
> Sofía

*Step 3: the corrections.*

| | Draft | Correction | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | *Bienvenido* | *Bienvenida* | It agrees with Valeria, a woman. |
| 2 | *es cerca* | *está cerca* | Location takes *estar* (A1). |
| 3 | *publico* | *público* | Spelling: the tilde shows the stress (*PÚ-bli-co*). |
| 4 | *mucho gente* | *mucha gente* | *La gente* is feminine. |
| 5 | *¿Qué le parece…?* | *¿Qué te parece…?* | The register slipped from *tú* to *usted*. |

The draft also has a content problem: at 56 words it's short, and the invitation has no date or
place, so it hardly works as a plan.

*Step 4: the second draft* (68 words):

> Querida Valeria:
>
> ¡Qué buena noticia! Bienvenida a la ciudad. Te recomiendo la colonia Las Flores: es tranquila,
> segura y está cerca del centro. Además, hay muchos parques y restaurantes. Moverse en
> transporte público es fácil: hay metro y autobuses, pero en la hora pico hay mucha gente. ¿Qué
> te parece si comemos juntas el sábado 6? Conozco un lugar muy bueno cerca de mi casa.
>
> Un abrazo,
> Sofía

Every point is covered, the register is the same from start to end, and the text has a contrast
(*pero*), an addition (*Además*) and a suggestion (*¿Qué te parece si…?*, lesson 15). The
neighborhood is invented.

## Writing task 2: a short text

### Example 2: "Mi primer trabajo"

*The prompt*: write a text of 70–80 words about your first job. Say when it was, what you did,
what the people were like and what you learned.

*The plan.* Four points, and for each one the tense: *when* → preterite and age in the imperfect;
*what you did* (habits) → imperfect; *people* (description) → imperfect with *ser*; *what you
learned* (result) → preterite.

*The first draft* (66 words):

> Mi primer trabajo fue en una cafetería de mi barrio, cuando tuve (1) diecisiete años. Trabajaba
> los fines de semana, de ocho a tres. Preparaba café, limpiaba las mesas y atendía a las (2)
> clientes. Mis compañeros eran muy simpáticos y el dueño estaba (3) paciente. Al principio me
> equivocaba mucho con las cuentas, pero poco a poco aprendi (4). Gracias a ese trabajo, ahorré
> dinero por (5) mi primera computadora.

*The corrections.*

| | Draft | Correction | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | *cuando tuve diecisiete años* | *cuando tenía* | Age in the past is background: imperfect (lesson 02). |
| 2 | *a las clientes* | *a los clientes* | A mixed or unknown group takes the masculine. |
| 3 | *estaba paciente* | *era paciente* | A character trait takes *ser* (lesson 10). |
| 4 | *aprendi* | *aprendí* | The *yo* preterite of regular *-er* and *-ir* verbs has a tilde. |
| 5 | *por mi primera computadora* | *para* | Purpose, a goal ahead: *para* (lesson 14). |

There's also a missing point: the task asks what you learned, and the draft only says that the
writer stopped making mistakes with the bills. The second draft adds one sentence.

*The second draft* (75 words):

> Mi primer trabajo fue en una cafetería de mi barrio, cuando tenía diecisiete años. Trabajaba
> los fines de semana, de ocho a tres. Preparaba café, limpiaba las mesas y atendía a los
> clientes. Mis compañeros eran muy simpáticos y el dueño era paciente. Al principio me
> equivocaba mucho con las cuentas, pero poco a poco aprendí. Gracias a ese trabajo, ahorré
> dinero para mi primera computadora. Además, aprendí a hablar con todo tipo de gente.

*Equivocarse* = to make a mistake, to get something wrong; *poco a poco* = little by little;
*gracias a* = thanks to; *todo tipo de* = all kinds of. Notice the tenses: *fue* (the job as a
whole, finished), *tenía, trabajaba, preparaba, eran, era, me equivocaba* (background and
habits), *aprendí, ahorré* (results).

### Your own checklist

After the first draft, read it once for each of these, not all at once:

1. Content: every point of the task? About the right length?
2. Register: *tú* or *usted*, the same all the way?
3. Verbs: the right past (event or background), the right person, *ser* or *estar*.
4. Agreement: *el/la*, *-o/-a*, singular and plural.
5. Ortografía: tildes (*público, aprendí, está*), *¿ ¡* at the start, *mayúsculas* only for names
   and at the start of a sentence (not for days, months or nationalities: *el lunes, en mayo,
   mexicana*).

## Speaking task 1: the prepared talk

In the exam you choose one of two everyday topics and prepare it in the preparation time, with
notes.
Then you speak for about 2–3 minutes, and the examiner may ask a question or two. A clear
*esquema* (outline) is the secret:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  accTitle: An outline for a two-minute talk
  accDescr: A top-down chain of five boxes. One, open: say the topic. Two, the present: what you usually do. Three, the past: a memory or one experience. Four, the future: a plan or a wish. Five, close: your opinion and a final phrase such as Eso es todo.
  A["1. Open: Voy a hablar de…"] --> B["2. Now: what I usually do (present)"]
  B --> C["3. Before: a memory or experience (preterite, imperfect)"]
  C --> D["4. Later: a plan or wish (ir a, me gustaría)"]
  D --> E["5. Close: Para mí… Eso es todo."]
```

Moving through present, past and future shows the examiner the range of your grammar without
any risk: you choose what to say.

### Example 3: a model talk, "Mi tiempo libre"

> Bueno, voy a hablar de mi tiempo libre. Entre semana trabajo mucho, así que no tengo mucho
> tiempo, pero los fines de semana hago varias cosas. Los sábados en la mañana corro en el
> parque con una amiga; o sea, corremos un poco y platicamos mucho. Por la tarde, normalmente
> veo una serie o leo. En cuanto a los domingos, como con mi familia: mi mamá cocina y todos
> ayudamos.
>
> De niña tenía más tiempo libre. Jugaba en la calle con mis vecinos y en el verano íbamos a la
> playa. Ahora es diferente, pero me gusta mi vida.
>
> El mes pasado empecé una clase de baile, porque siempre quise aprender salsa. Es difícil, pero
> muy divertido. Por otro lado, quiero viajar más: el año que viene voy a ir a Oaxaca con mis
> primos. Para mí, el tiempo libre es muy importante, porque es el momento para descansar y
> estar con la gente que quiero. Eso es todo.

The talk has about 160 words, roughly two minutes at a calm pace with pauses. *Entre semana* =
on weekdays; *la clase de baile* = dance class.

The small linking phrases do a lot of work:

- *o sea* (I mean, in other words) rephrases what you just said; very common in Mexico, and
  informal;
- *es decir* (that is) does the same in a slightly more careful style;
- *en cuanto a* (as for, regarding) moves to a new point;
- *por otro lado* (on the other hand; also "besides, apart from that") adds a different idea.

*Bueno* and *pues* (well) give you a second to think. In Mexico you'll also hear *este…* as a
hesitation sound, like English "um". These fillers are *muletillas*: one now and then sounds
natural, but too many sound nervous.

## Speaking task 2: describing a photo

The exam gives you a photo of an everyday scene. Go from the general to the details, then guess
and react. Lesson 09 gave you the position words; here they are in a full model.

![A drawing of a bus terminal. On the left, a ticket window where a woman is selling tickets to a young man with a backpack. In the foreground, a mother and her daughter are sitting on a bench; the girl is eating an apple, the mother is looking at her phone, and a big suitcase is next to them. On the right, an older man is standing and reading a newspaper. At the back, a bus can be seen through a large window, and a clock on the wall shows a quarter past ten.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

### Example 4: a model description

> En la foto hay una terminal de autobuses. Creo que es por la mañana, porque el reloj dice las
> diez y cuarto. A la izquierda hay una ventanilla: una señora está vendiendo boletos y un joven
> con una mochila está comprando uno. En primer plano, en una banca, una mamá y su hija están
> sentadas. Junto a ellas hay una maleta grande, así que seguramente van a hacer un viaje largo.
> La niña está comiendo una manzana y la mamá está mirando su celular. A la derecha, un señor
> mayor está de pie y está leyendo el periódico. Al fondo se ve un autobús. Me parece que todos
> están esperando la salida.

The structure: the place (*En la foto hay…*), the time with a reason (*Creo que…, porque…*), the
parts of the picture (*A la izquierda, En primer plano, A la derecha, Al fondo*), what people are
doing (*estar* + gerund) and how they are placed (*están sentadas, está de pie*), and guesses
(*seguramente, Me parece que…*). The examiner may then ask about your own experience: *¿Usted
viaja mucho en autobús?* Answer, and add one detail.

## Speaking task 3: the conversation

The third task is a conversation with the examiner based on the photo's situation, a bit like a
role play: here, you could be buying a ticket at that window. The examiner plays the other part.

### Example 5: at the ticket window

> Examinadora: Buenos días. ¿En qué le puedo ayudar?
>
> Candidato: Buenos días. Quería un boleto para Puebla, por favor.
>
> Examinadora: ¿Para qué día?
>
> Candidato: Para hoy, si es posible. ¿A qué hora sale el próximo autobús?
>
> Examinadora: Hay uno a las once y otro a las doce y media.
>
> Candidato: Perdón, ¿puede repetir? ¿A las doce y media?
>
> Examinadora: Sí, a las doce y media. ¿Sencillo o de ida y vuelta?
>
> Candidato: Sencillo, para el de las once. ¿Cuánto cuesta?
>
> Examinadora: Son 280 pesos. ¿Va a pagar con tarjeta?
>
> Candidato: Sí, con tarjeta. ¿Me podría dar un asiento de ventanilla?
>
> Examinadora: Claro. Aquí tiene: asiento 14, sale del andén 3.
>
> Candidato: Muchas gracias. ¡Buen día!

The candidate uses the polite *quería* (lesson 19), asks for repetition when unsure, answers the
examiner's questions, and closes politely. *Sencillo* = one-way (lesson 14); *el andén* =
platform; *¡Buen día!* = have a good day. The fare is invented.

## Common mistakes

- Writing the first draft and stopping. The five-point checklist above takes a few minutes and
  catches most mistakes.
- Learning a talk word for word. Examiners notice, and one forgotten word stops you. Learn the
  outline and a few key phrases instead.
- Describing a photo with the simple present only (*La niña come una manzana*). It isn't wrong,
  but *está comiendo* is what Spanish uses for what is happening in the picture.
- Overusing *o sea*: once or twice in a talk is plenty.
- Answering the examiner in one word. Add a reason or a detail: *Sí, viajo mucho en autobús,
  porque es más barato que el avión.*

## Key points

- Writing: plan, first draft, check one thing at a time (content, register, verbs, agreement,
  spelling), second draft, count.
- In a personal text, pick the tense from the job: background and habits in the imperfect,
  events and results in the preterite.
- Talk: an outline in present, past and future; *o sea, es decir, en cuanto a, por otro lado*;
  close with *Eso es todo*.
- Photo: general → parts (*a la izquierda, en primer plano, al fondo*) → actions (*estar* +
  gerund) → guesses (*creo que, seguramente*).
- Conversation: polite openings (*Quería…, ¿Me podría…?*), ask for repetition, close politely.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

## What this lesson is for

In module 1 you learned to tell a story with two past tenses: the imperfect for the scene
(*era, tenía, había*) and the preterite for the events that move the story on (*llegó, abrió,
sonó*). Module 2 gave you the pronouns that keep a story from repeating itself (*la buscamos, se
lo llevó, me la dio*). This lesson puts it all together in one longer text, a *cuento* (short story)
written for this course: *El reloj de San Jacinto*, about a thousand words in five parts. San
Jacinto is an invented town in the mountains of Puebla.

You'll practice three reading strategies that make a long text possible at A2: using
**[[cognates]]**, guessing from context, and skipping. And you'll answer the question a good reader
asks: not only "what happened?" but "why?", which needs **[[inference]]**.

## Before you read: three strategies

1. Cognates. Many Spanish words look like their English relatives: *el mecanismo*
   (mechanism), *perfecta*, *exactamente* (exactly), *el hospital*. They're free vocabulary
   (patterns: *-ción* = -tion, *-mente* = -ly). Beware of false friends: *la librería* is a
   bookshop, not a library.
2. Guessing from context (*adivinar por el contexto*). Ask what kind of word it is (a thing? an
   action?), guess from the sentence and the situation, and read on. If the next sentences
   agree with your guess, keep it.
3. Skipping. If the sentence makes sense without the word, skip it. In *Unas palomas salieron
   volando*, "some ___ flew out" is enough (they're pigeons).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  accTitle: What to do with a new word while reading
  accDescr: When you meet a new word, first ask whether it looks like an English word. If it does, try the English meaning and check that it fits. If it doesn't, ask whether the sentence makes sense without it. If it does, skip the word and keep reading. If not, guess from the sentence and the situation, then read on and check the guess. Only if the guess still doesn't work, look the word up.
  A["A new word"] --> B{"Does it look like an English word?"}
  B -- yes --> C["Try the English meaning: does it fit?"]
  B -- no --> D{"Does the sentence make sense without it?"}
  D -- "yes: skip it" --> E["Keep reading"]
  D -- no --> F["Guess from the sentence and the situation"]
  C --> E
  F --> G{"Read on: does the guess still work?"}
  G -- yes --> E
  G -- no --> H["Look it up in the glosses or a dictionary"]
```

A fourth tool: the two pasts are a map. The imperfect paints the background (*había un reloj
enorme*); the preterite marks the events (*Toqué varias veces. Nadie abrió.*). If you get lost,
follow the preterites.

## El reloj de San Jacinto

The characters (*los personajes*): Mateo, the narrator; don Ernesto; his daughter Laura;
doña Chela, a neighbor; Sofía, Mateo's friend; and Father Tomás, the priest. Read each part once
without stopping, then again with the glosses below it (only words the course hasn't taught).

### 1. El relojero

> Cuando yo era niño, en San Jacinto todos conocían a don Ernesto. Tenía un taller pequeño en la plaza, junto a la iglesia, y allí arreglaba relojes, radios y, a veces, hasta bicicletas. Era un señor alto y delgado, de pelo blanco, y siempre llevaba los lentes en la punta de la nariz. Hablaba poco, pero sonreía mucho.
>
> Mi familia vivía enfrente del taller, y todos los sábados yo lo ayudaba. Él me enseñaba los nombres de las herramientas y yo limpiaba las piezas con un trapo. No me pagaba con dinero: me pagaba con un refresco y una historia.
>
> En la torre de la iglesia había un reloj enorme, pero no funcionaba. Sus manecillas marcaban siempre las cuatro y diez, de día y de noche. La campana tampoco sonaba. Nadie sabía por qué se paró, y a nadie le importaba mucho: todos tenían celular.
>
> Un sábado le pregunté:
>
> —Don Ernesto, usted arregla todo. ¿Por qué no arregla el reloj de la torre?
>
> Él miró la torre por la ventana un momento. Luego volvió a su trabajo y dijo en voz baja:
>
> —Algunas cosas no se arreglan con herramientas, Mateo.
>
> No entendí su respuesta, pero no le pregunté más.

Words: *hasta* (here: even), *la punta* (tip), *el trapo* (cloth, rag), *enorme* (huge),
*se paró* (it stopped), *en voz baja* (quietly, in a low voice).

In short: Mateo helps don Ernesto, the repairman, every Saturday; the church clock always says
4:10, and don Ernesto won't fix it.

### 2. La puerta cerrada

> Un sábado de marzo crucé la calle como siempre, pero la puerta del taller estaba cerrada. Toqué varias veces. Nadie abrió. Doña Chela, la señora de la tienda de al lado, salió con su escoba.
>
> —Don Ernesto no está, mijo. Anoche se sintió mal y su hija se lo llevó al hospital, a Puebla.
>
> Tuve mucho miedo. Durante semanas, el taller siguió cerrado. Todas las tardes, después de la escuela, yo miraba la puerta y esperaba. Un domingo llegó un carro gris. Era Laura, la hija de don Ernesto, que vivía en la ciudad. Abrió el taller y empezó a guardar las cosas en cajas.
>
> —¿Cómo está su papá? —le pregunté.
>
> —Mejor, gracias. Pero ya no puede vivir solo. Se va a vivir conmigo, y vamos a vender el taller.
>
> Sentí un hueco en el estómago. Laura me miró un momento y sacó del cajón una caja pequeña de madera.
>
> —Esto es para ti. Mi papá dice que tú vas a saber qué hacer con esto.

Words: *tocar* (here: to knock), *de al lado* (next door), *la escoba* (broom), *se lo llevó*
(she took him), *seguir cerrado* (to stay closed), *el hueco* (hole, empty
space), *el cajón* (drawer), *de madera* (wooden).

In short: don Ernesto falls ill; weeks later his daughter comes to sell the shop and gives Mateo
a wooden box from her father.

### 3. La caja de madera

> En mi cuarto abrí la caja. Adentro había tres cosas: una llave grande y vieja, un cuaderno con la tapa azul y una pieza de metal, pequeña y redonda, envuelta en un trapo.
>
> En la primera página del cuaderno, con la letra de don Ernesto, decía: «Para Mateo. Ya es hora.»
>
> El cuaderno estaba lleno de dibujos: ruedas, cadenas, la campana, las manecillas. Debajo de cada dibujo, don Ernesto escribió el nombre de la pieza y para qué servía. Eran los dibujos del reloj de la torre. En la última página había un dibujo de la pieza redonda, con una flecha y una sola palabra: «aquí».
>
> Me quedé sentado en la cama mucho tiempo. La pieza no era de un reloj cualquiera. Era del reloj de la torre. Y don Ernesto la tenía en su taller. ¿Desde cuándo? ¿Y por qué la escondió?
>
> Esa noche llamé a Sofía, mi mejor amiga. Sofía no le tenía miedo a nada, ni a las arañas ni a la oscuridad.
>
> —Mañana subimos a la torre —me dijo—. Yo llevo la linterna.

Words: *adentro* (inside), *la tapa* (cover, lid), *redondo* (round), *la letra* (here:
handwriting), *decía* (it said: a written text "says" in Spanish, in the imperfect), *el
dibujo* (drawing), *la rueda* (wheel), *la cadena* (chain), *para qué servía* (what it was
for), *un reloj cualquiera* (just any clock, an ordinary clock), *la flecha* (arrow), *la araña* (spider), *la oscuridad* (darkness).

In short: the box holds a key, a notebook of drawings and a small part from the tower clock.

### 4. En la torre

> El padre Tomás abrió mucho los ojos cuando vio la llave.
>
> —¡La llave de la torre! La buscamos durante años. ¿Dónde la encontraste?
>
> Le contamos todo, y nos dio permiso de subir. La escalera de la torre era estrecha y oscura, y todo estaba cubierto de polvo. Unas palomas salieron volando cuando abrimos la puerta de arriba. Sofía estornudó tres veces.
>
> Arriba estaba el mecanismo del reloj, exactamente como en los dibujos. Sofía sostenía la linterna y yo leía el cuaderno en voz alta. Encontramos el lugar de la flecha: había un hueco pequeño y redondo. Saqué la pieza del trapo y la puse en su lugar. Entró perfecta.
>
> Según el cuaderno, después teníamos que darle cuerda al reloj con una manivela. Le dimos cuerda entre los dos, hasta que nos dolieron los brazos. No pasó nada.
>
> —¿Y ahora? —preguntó Sofía.
>
> De repente oímos un «clac» y las ruedas empezaron a moverse. Despacio, muy despacio, las manecillas se movieron por primera vez en muchos años. Las pusimos en las doce, como decía el cuaderno, y la campana sonó: una, dos, tres… doce veces.
>
> Desde arriba vimos la plaza. La gente salía de las tiendas y miraba hacia la torre. Doña Chela tenía la escoba en la mano y lloraba.

Words: *el padre* (here: the priest, Father Tomás), *el permiso* (permission), *estrecho*
(narrow), *cubierto de* (covered in), *la paloma* (pigeon), *salir volando* (to fly out),
*estornudar* (to sneeze), *entró perfecta* (it went in perfectly: it fitted), *sostener* (to hold, like *tener*), *darle cuerda a* (to wind up), *la
manivela* (crank, handle), *despacio* (slowly), *hacia* (toward).
