questions.explanation: "Nadie" (nobody) takes a singular verb: "nadie se cayó". When nadie comes before the verb, no "no" is needed. "Afortunadamente" can start or end the sentence.

questions.stem: How would a Mexican friend usually ask "Have you eaten yet?"
questions.explanation: In Mexico "ya" goes with the preterite: "¿Ya comiste?" (Spain would often say "¿Ya has comido?"). "¿Todavía comes?" means "Do you still eat?", "¿Ya comías?" is the imperfect, and "¿Ya comerás?" is a future.

questions.stem: How do you say "I've been living here for three years"?
choices: He vivido aquí desde tres años.
Vivo aquí desde hace tres años.
questions.explanation: Something still true now takes the present, and a length of time needs "desde hace": "Vivo aquí desde hace tres años" (or "Hace tres años que vivo aquí"). "Desde" alone needs a starting point (desde 2023), and "Viví aquí hace tres años" means "I lived here three years ago".

questions.stem: Estudio español ___ enero.
questions.explanation: "Enero" is a starting point, so use "desde" alone: "Estudio español desde enero" (I've been studying Spanish since January). "Desde hace" needs a length of time (desde hace tres meses).

questions.stem: What does "Hace dos años que no veo a mi hermano" mean?
choices: I'm going to see my brother in two years.
I see my brother every two years.
My brother has been away for two days.
I haven't seen my brother for two years.
questions.explanation: "Hace + time + que + present" describes a situation that has lasted up to now; with "no" it's how long something hasn't happened: "I haven't seen my brother for two years."

questions.stem: What does "Actualmente trabajo en un banco" mean?
choices: Actually, I work at a bank.
I currently work at a bank.
I used to work at a bank.
I really want to work at a bank.
questions.explanation: "Actualmente" is a false friend: it means "currently, at present". "Actually" is "en realidad".

questions.stem: Which past form does Mexican Spanish usually use for a life experience with no time given, as in "Have you ever been to Oaxaca?"
choices: the present perfect: ¿Has estado en Oaxaca?
the preterite with ayer: ¿Estuviste ayer en Oaxaca?
questions.explanation: Experiences up to now take the present perfect in Mexico as in Spain: "¿Has estado en Oaxaca?" The preterite is for finished events at a finished time, and the imperfect for descriptions and habits.

questions.stem: Read: "Me llamo Inés. Soy de Colombia y vivo en Monterrey desde 2022. Al principio extrañaba mucho a mi familia, pero ya me acostumbré. Mi meta es abrir una cafetería." Today is 2026. How long has Inés lived in Monterrey?
questions.explanation: "Vivo en Monterrey desde 2022": from 2022 to 2026 is about four years. She is from Colombia, so not since birth.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: No he visto jamás la nieve.
Jamás no he visto la nieve.
No jamás he visto la nieve.
He no visto jamás la nieve.
questions.explanation: "Jamás" works like "nunca": before the verb alone (Jamás he visto…) or after it with "no" in front (No he visto jamás…). "Jamás no" is a double negative in the wrong order, and nothing goes between "he" and the participle.

questions.stem: Which sentences mean "I've been studying Spanish for six months"? Select all that apply.
choices: Estudio español desde hace seis meses.
Hace seis meses que estudio español.
questions.explanation: "Desde hace + time" and "Hace + time + que + present" both describe something still going on. "Estudié español hace seis meses" means "I studied Spanish six months ago" (finished), and "desde seis meses" is missing "hace".

questions.stem: Complete the question (Since when have you lived in Mexico?): ¿Desde ___ vives en México?
questions.explanation: "¿Desde cuándo…?" asks for the starting point; question words carry a written accent: "cuándo". The answer uses "desde": "Desde 2023".

questions.stem: Match each expression with its meaning.
questions.explanation: "Hace poco" points to a recent finished moment, "últimamente" to what has been happening lately, "hoy en día" to the present in general, "por primera vez" to a first time, and "aún" is a synonym of "todavía". None of them means "actually" (en realidad).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: How long have you been living here?
questions.explanation: "¿Cuánto tiempo hace que…?" + the present asks how long something has been going on: "¿Cuánto tiempo hace que vives aquí?" "Viviste" (preterite) would talk about a finished stay.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I miss my family a lot.
questions.explanation: "Extrañar" (to miss) takes the personal a before people: "Extraño mucho a mi familia" or "Extraño a mi familia mucho". Without "a" the sentence isn't standard.

questions.stem: Put these times in order, from the furthest in the past to now.
questions.explanation: "En 2010" is the oldest point, "hace cinco años" (five years ago) is more recent, then "el año pasado" (last year), "la semana pasada" (last week) and "hoy" (today). All of them except "hoy" mark finished time, so in Mexico they go with the preterite; "hoy" does too for a finished event (Hoy comí tarde).

questions.stem: According to tradition, when was Tenochtitlan founded?
questions.explanation: The traditional founding date is 1325. 1519 is when the Spanish arrived, 1521 when the city fell, and 1810 when the War of Independence began.

questions.stem: Why is "era" (imperfect) used in "Tenochtitlan era la capital de un imperio muy grande"?
choices: It is a single event with a date.
It is something still true today.
It is a plan for the future.
questions.explanation: The sentence describes what the city was like at the time: background, so the imperfect. Dated events in the same text (llegaron, se rindió) take the preterite.

questions.stem: El 13 de agosto de 1521, Cuauhtémoc ___. (rendirse)
questions.explanation: A single dated event takes the preterite. "Rendirse" changes like "pedir": e → i in the él form, "se rindió". "Se rendió" misses the change, and "se rendía" (and the misspelled "se rindía") are imperfect.

questions.stem: What was the Grito de Dolores?
choices: The end of the War of Independence in 1821
Miguel Hidalgo's call in 1810 to fight against the Spanish government
The start of the Revolution in 1910
questions.explanation: On 16 September 1810, in Dolores, the priest Miguel Hidalgo called the people to fight against the Spanish government. The war ended in 1821; the Revolution began in 1910.

questions.stem: How is "el siglo XVI" usually read in everyday speech?
questions.explanation: Centuries are written in Roman numerals and read as ordinary numbers: XVI = dieciséis, the sixteenth century (the 1500s). "Sexto" is VI, and "mil seiscientos" is the year 1600.

questions.stem: Why does the text say "Díaz renunció en mayo de 1911" and not "renunciaba"?
choices: It describes what Díaz was like.
It is a single event at a specific time.
questions.explanation: Díaz's resignation is one event with a date (May 1911), so it takes the preterite. "Renunciaba" would describe something repeated or in progress.

questions.stem: On which date does Mexico celebrate its Independence Day?
questions.explanation: Mexico celebrates 16 September, the anniversary of the Grito de Dolores in 1810, with the Grito repeated on the night of the 15th. 27 September 1821 is when the war ended, 20 November recalls the start of the Revolution, and 5 February the 1917 Constitution.

questions.stem: According to the lesson's text, what did Emiliano Zapata fight for in the south?
questions.explanation: "Emiliano Zapata luchó en el sur por la tierra de los campesinos": he fought for the peasants' land. Land was a central issue because very few families owned a large part of it.

questions.stem: Which of these sentences report single dated events, and so use the preterite? Select all that apply.
choices: Cortés y Moctezuma se encontraron el 8 de noviembre de 1519.
Hidalgo llamó a la gente a luchar en 1810.
questions.explanation: "Se encontraron", "llamó" and "renunció" are events with dates (preterite). "Era muy desigual" and "Había mercados y canales" describe the situation (imperfect).

questions.stem: Put these events in chronological order, starting with the earliest.
choices: Cortés llegó a la costa del golfo de México.
Hidalgo dio el Grito de Dolores.
El ejército de Iturbide y Guerrero entró a la Ciudad de México.
Madero llamó a la gente a levantarse en armas.
questions.explanation: 1325 (traditional founding), 1519 (the Spanish arrive), 1521 (Cuauhtémoc surrenders), 1810 (the Grito), 1821 (the army enters Mexico City), 1910 (Madero's call to arms).

questions.stem: Match each year with the event, as the lesson tells it.
questions.explanation: These five dates frame the lesson's story. Díaz resigned in May 1911, which isn't one of the years listed.

questions.stem: Some captions on this timeline are missing. Choose the caption for each numbered point.

image.alt: A timeline of Mexican history with seven years: 1325, 1519, 1521, 1810, 1821, 1910 and 1917. Only 1519 (llegan los españoles) and 1917 (nueva Constitución) have captions; the other five captions are numbered blanks. Below are bars for la Nueva España (1521–1821) and México independiente.

questions.explanation: 1325: Tenochtitlan is founded; 1521: it falls; 1810: the Grito de Dolores; 1821: the War of Independence ends; 1910: the Revolution begins. Hidalgo died in 1811 and Díaz resigned in 1911, neither of which is on the timeline. Like many timelines, this one uses the present (cae, empieza) for past events.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: When did the Revolution begin?
questions.explanation: A single event takes the preterite: "empezó". After a question word the verb comes next and the subject follows: "¿Cuándo empezó la Revolución?" (In conversation you'll also hear the topic first: "¿La Revolución cuándo empezó?")

questions.stem: Cuando llegamos, la tienda ya ___. (cerrar)
questions.explanation: The shop closed before we arrived, so the pluperfect: "había cerrado". The subject is "la tienda" (singular), the participle never agrees ("cerrada" is wrong here), and "ha cerrado" is the present perfect.

questions.stem: What does "Nunca había visto el mar" mean?
choices: I have never seen the sea.
I had never seen the sea.
I will never see the sea.
questions.explanation: "Había visto" is the pluperfect: "had seen". With "nunca": "I had never seen the sea" (before some moment in the past). "I have never seen" would be "Nunca he visto".

questions.stem: Para entonces, mis amigos ya ___ la cena. (hacer)
questions.explanation: "Mis amigos" is plural, so "habían", and "hacer" has the irregular participle "hecho", which never takes a plural ending: "habían hecho".

questions.stem: Which sentence means that the film started after you arrived?
choices: Cuando llegué, la película ya había empezado.
Cuando llegué, la película ya había terminado.
La película había empezado antes de las ocho.
questions.explanation: With two preterites, the events follow each other: I arrived, then the film started. "Ya había empezado" means it had already started before I arrived.

questions.stem: In the story, why is "se había acostado muy tarde" in the pluperfect?
choices: It happened after the alarm clock.
It happened the night before the moment being told.
questions.explanation: The story is told from Friday morning; going to bed late happened earlier, the night before ("la noche anterior"), so it steps back with the pluperfect.

questions.stem: In the story, why did Diego miss his flight?
choices: He got to the gate after the plane had taken off.
questions.explanation: "Cuando por fin llegó a la puerta, el avión ya había despegado": the plane had already taken off. He got lost downtown later, with Paty.

questions.stem: Choose the right form: Me enteré de que mi prima ___.
questions.explanation: The pronoun goes before "había", the verb agrees with "mi prima" (singular), and the participle doesn't change: "se había casado".

questions.stem: In the story, why had Paty kept Diego out of the house all day?
choices: She wanted to see a movie.
Their mom had asked her to, because of the surprise party.
questions.explanation: "Su mamá le había pedido tener a Diego fuera de casa todo el día": their mom had asked her, so the family could prepare the surprise party.

questions.stem: Which of these are pluperfect forms? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The pluperfect is "había" (imperfect of haber) + a participle: habíamos visto, había dicho, habían salido. "Hubo" is the preterite of hay (there was), and "he comido" is the present perfect.

questions.stem: Write the pluperfect of "salir" (ellos): Cuando llegué, mis amigos ya ___.
questions.explanation: "Habían" (ellos) + the regular participle "salido": "habían salido". They left before I arrived.

questions.stem: Match each verb with its past participle.
questions.explanation: All five participles are irregular. "Hacido" and "descubrido" are made by the regular rule, which these verbs don't follow.

questions.stem: Put the events of Diego's day in the order they happened.
choices: Diego y Paty se perdieron en el centro.
Diego abrió la puerta y vio a su familia.
questions.explanation: The story tells some of these with the pluperfect, but in real time the order is: the late night, the silent alarm, the plane leaving, getting lost downtown, and the surprise at home.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: When I arrived, everyone had left.
questions.explanation: "Todos" is plural, so "se habían ido" (pluperfect of irse: they had left before I arrived). The "cuando" clause can come first or last, and "todos" can go before or after the verb.

questions.stem: "¿Tienes la contraseña del wifi?" — "Sí, ___ tengo."
questions.explanation: "La contraseña" is feminine singular, so "it" is "la": "Sí, la tengo." "Lo" would be for a masculine noun, "las" for several, and "le" is the indirect pronoun ("to him / to her").

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I bought it yesterday" (el cargador)?
questions.explanation: With a conjugated verb such as "compré", the pronoun goes right before it: "Lo compré ayer." English puts "it" after the verb, but Spanish never does with a conjugated verb, and nothing can come between the pronoun and the verb.

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT correct Spanish?
questions.explanation: With "ir a" + infinitive the pronoun goes before the conjugated verb ("Lo voy a descargar", "No lo voy a descargar") or on the end of the infinitive ("Voy a descargarlo"). It can never go between the two verbs, so "Voy a lo descargar" is wrong.

questions.stem: Which sentence needs the personal "a" in the blank?
questions.explanation: The personal "a" goes before a direct object that is a specific person (or a pet): "Busco a mi hermana." Things take no "a": "Busco mi cargador", "Descargué la aplicación", "Prendí la computadora."

questions.stem: A sales assistant offers to help an older woman. Complete: "¿___ ayudo, señora?"
questions.explanation: "Usted" is grammatically third person, so "you" as a direct object is "lo" for a man and "la" for a woman: "¿La ayudo, señora?" "Te" is for "tú", which would be too familiar here, and "los" is plural. (You may also hear "le" in shops: honors 08h1.)

questions.stem: "¿Sabes que Marta se casa en junio?" — "Sí, ya ___ sé."
questions.explanation: "Lo" can stand for a whole idea, here "that Marta is getting married". It is always "lo" for an idea, never "la", even though Marta is a woman: "Ya lo sé" (I already know).

questions.stem: Your friend's phone is almost dead. Which is the correct way to say "Charge it!" (el celular, tú)?
questions.explanation: With an affirmative command the pronoun is joined to the end. "Carga" is stressed on CAR; adding "lo" puts that stress three syllables from the end, so it needs a written accent: "cárgalo". "¡Lo carga!" is a statement (he charges it), and "carga lo" splits the word.

questions.stem: Inés sends a message: "Beto, te mando el enlace de la página web. Ábrelo en la laptop y descarga los archivos. Después imprímelos, por favor; la impresora de la oficina ya funciona." What does Inés ask Beto to print?
questions.explanation: "Imprímelos" (print them) uses "los", masculine plural, and the only masculine plural noun in the message is "los archivos". "Ábrelo" (open it) is about the link, "el enlace"; "la página web" and "la laptop" would need "la".

questions.stem: Which sentences correctly say "I can't delete them" (los videos)? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: With "poder" + infinitive, the pronoun goes before the conjugated verb (after "no": "No los puedo borrar") or on the end of the infinitive ("No puedo borrarlos"). It can't go between the verbs or before "no". "Borrarlas" has the wrong gender: "los videos" is masculine.

questions.stem: Answer with a pronoun and the verb (preterite): "¿Ya imprimiste los boletos?" — "Sí, ya ___."
questions.explanation: "Los boletos" is masculine plural, so "los", before the verb: "Sí, ya los imprimí." The present perfect "ya los he impreso" (or "imprimido") is also correct; in Mexico the preterite is the usual choice.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts.

image.alt: A smartphone with a cable and plug, a laptop and a pair of headphones, with five numbered markers on the parts.

questions.explanation: 1 is the laptop's screen, "la pantalla"; 2 the battery symbol, "la batería"; 3 the plug at the end of the cable, "el cargador"; 4 the keys, "el teclado"; 5 the headphones, "los audífonos". A printer ("la impresora") and a password ("la contraseña") aren't shown.

questions.stem: Match each direct object to the pronoun that replaces it.
questions.explanation: Direct object pronouns copy the gender and number of the noun: masculine "el cargador" → "lo", feminine "la pantalla" → "la", "los audífonos" → "los", "las fotos" → "las". "Le" is the indirect object pronoun (lesson 06).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'm going to turn it off. (it = la computadora)
questions.explanation: "La computadora" is feminine, so "la". With "ir a" + infinitive the pronoun goes before "voy" ("La voy a apagar") or on the end of the infinitive ("Voy a apagarla"); both are accepted. "Lo" has the wrong gender, and the pronoun can't appear twice.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I didn't download it yesterday. (it = la aplicación)
questions.explanation: "No" comes first, then the pronoun, then the conjugated verb: "no la descargué". "Ayer" can open or close the sentence: "Ayer no la descargué" or "No la descargué ayer". "La aplicación" is feminine, so "lo" is wrong.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ di el regalo a mi papá."
questions.explanation: Your dad receives the gift, so he is the indirect object: "le", doubled with "a mi papá". "Lo" and "la" are direct object pronouns, and "se" only replaces "le" when "lo, la, los, las" follows ("Se lo di").

questions.stem: Complete: "A mis papás les ___ los precios." (preocupar)
questions.explanation: Like "gustar", "preocupar" agrees with the thing that worries, not with the person. "Los precios" is plural, so "preocupan". "Les" shows who is worried (my parents).

questions.stem: How do you say "I'm ten pesos short"?
questions.explanation: With "faltar" the missing thing is the subject: "diez pesos" is plural, so "faltan", and "me" shows who is short. "Me falta diez pesos" doesn't agree, "falto" makes you the missing thing, and "faltas" means "you are missing".

questions.stem: You want to borrow your friend's charger. What do you ask?
questions.explanation: Spanish asks the owner to lend: "¿Me prestas…?" (Do you lend me…?). "¿Te presto…?" offers to lend to them, "pedir prestado" is for talking about borrowing (Le pedí prestado…), not for asking, and "¿Me regalas…?" asks for it as a gift.

questions.stem: A friend in Mexico says: "Me da pena cantar enfrente de todos." What does she mean?
choices: She's embarrassed to sing in front of everyone.
She doesn't mind singing in front of everyone.
She loves singing in front of everyone.
Singing in front of everyone makes her angry.
questions.explanation: In Mexico "me da pena" usually means "I feel embarrassed / shy". "I don't mind" would be "me da igual", and "I love it" "me encanta" or "me fascina". (Elsewhere "pena" can also mean sadness or pity.)

questions.stem: "No me importa el precio." Agree with your friend: "A mí ___."
questions.explanation: The friend's sentence is negative ("No me importa"), so you agree with "A mí tampoco" (me neither). "A mí también" agrees with a positive sentence, "A mí sí" disagrees ("it does matter to me"), and "también no" isn't Spanish (an English-style "also not").

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Lo di el regalo a ella.
Le di el regalo a ella.
Les di el regalo a ella.
questions.explanation: With "a ella" (a stressed pronoun), the short pronoun "le" is required: "Le di el regalo a ella." "Lo" is a direct object pronoun, and "les" is plural, but "ella" is one person.

questions.stem: Read: "Querida Ana: ¡Gracias por el perfume! Me fascina. Mi hermano me regaló un anillo y mis papás me dieron una caja de chocolates. Me sobraron muchos, y mañana te llevo unos." Who gave the writer a ring?
questions.explanation: "Mi hermano me regaló un anillo": the writer's brother gave the ring. Ana gave the perfume, and the writer's parents gave the box of chocolates ("una caja de chocolates"), some of which are left over ("me sobraron").

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: A Luis le faltan dos pesos.
questions.explanation: Verbs like "gustar" agree with the thing and show the person with a pronoun: "Me interesan los museos" (plural), "A Luis le faltan dos pesos", "¿Te parece bien el plan?" "Yo intereso la historia" makes you the subject, and "Nos preocupa los exámenes" needs the plural "preocupan".

questions.stem: Write the missing pronoun: "A mi hermana ___ fascinan los perros."
questions.explanation: "A mi hermana" is one person, third person, so the indirect pronoun is "le": "A mi hermana le fascinan los perros." The verb is plural because "los perros" is the subject.

questions.stem: Match each Spanish verb to its meaning.
questions.explanation: "Regalar" is only for gifts; "prestar" is to lend; "pedir prestado" is to borrow (ask to be lent); "devolver" is to give something back; "agradecer" is to thank. "To go back" is "volver" or "regresar".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I gave my mom a necklace.
questions.explanation: Your mom receives the necklace, so "le", doubled with "a mi mamá": "Le di un collar a mi mamá." The person can also come right after the verb ("Le di a mi mamá un collar") or first, for emphasis ("A mi mamá le di un collar"). "Di un collar a mi mamá", without "le", is also accepted: with a noun the "le" is grammatically optional, though Mexicans usually say it. "Lo" is the direct pronoun and can't stand for the receiver.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: We have two tickets left over.
questions.explanation: "Sobrar" works like "gustar": the tickets are the subject, so the verb is plural ("sobran") and "nos" shows who has them: "Nos sobran dos boletos." "Sobramos" would mean "we are left over". Putting "dos boletos" first is possible but less usual.

questions.stem: "¿Qué te parece mi idea?" Which answer is correct?
questions.explanation: "Parecer" for opinions works like "gustar": the idea "seems" good to me, "Me parece muy buena." "Parezco" means "I seem", "me parezco" is "I look like" (parecerse), and "te parece" would be about the other person's opinion.

questions.stem: "¿Me prestas tu gorra?" — "Sí, ___ presto."
questions.explanation: The person (you, "te") comes first and the thing ("la gorra" → "la") second: "Sí, te la presto." "Te lo" has the wrong gender, and "se" would mean "to him, her, you (usted), them".

questions.stem: Replace "el regalo" with a pronoun: "Le di el regalo." →
questions.explanation: Two pronouns: person first ("le"), thing second ("lo"). But "le" becomes "se" before "lo, la, los, las", so "Se lo di." Spanish never says "le lo".

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT correct?
questions.explanation: The two pronouns always travel together: both before the conjugated verb ("Te lo voy a envolver", "¿Te lo envuelvo?") or both on the end of the infinitive ("Voy a envolvértelo"). "Te voy a envolverlo" splits the pair.

questions.stem: How do you write "Give it to me!" (el libro, tú)?
questions.explanation: Both pronouns are joined to the end of the command "da", person first: "dá-me-lo". The stress is now three syllables from the end, so it needs an accent: "¡Dámelo!" "¡Me lo das!" is a statement ("You give it to me!").

questions.stem: How do you say "These jeans are tight on me"?
questions.explanation: "Quedar" (to fit) works like "gustar": the clothes are the subject, so "quedan" for "estos jeans", and the adjective agrees too: "apretados". "Flojos" means loose.

questions.stem: As you walk into a store in Mexico, the assistant says: "¿Ya la atienden?" What does she mean?
choices: Shall I wrap it for you?
questions.explanation: "Atender" is to serve or attend to a customer, and "la" is "you" (usted, a woman): "Is someone already helping you?" A polite answer is "No, gracias, solo estoy viendo" or "Sí, gracias".

questions.stem: "Se lo di." Which of these is NOT a possible meaning?
questions.explanation: "Se" here is "le" or "les" in disguise: to him, to her, to you (usted), to them, to you all. "Di" is "I gave". "He gave it to me" would be "Me lo dio". Add "a él, a ella, a ellos" to make "se" clear.

questions.stem: A customer says: "Buenas tardes. Quiero devolver esta blusa. Me queda grande y no tienen talla chica. Aquí está el ticket." Why does she want to return the blouse?
choices: It's too big, and there's no smaller size.
It's too small, and there's no bigger size.
questions.explanation: "Me queda grande" = it's too big on me; "no tienen talla chica" = you don't have a small. She has the receipt ("Aquí está el ticket").

questions.stem: Which are correct ways to ask "Can I try them on?" (los jeans)? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The pair "me los" (reflexive "me" of probarse, then "los") goes before "puedo" or on the end of the infinitive, with an accent: "probármelos". It can't be split ("Me puedo probarlos"), go between the verbs, or change order ("los me").

questions.stem: Replace both objects with pronouns: "Le mandé las fotos a Laura." → "___ mandé."
questions.explanation: The thing is "las fotos" → "las"; the person is "le" (a Laura). Person first, and "le" becomes "se" before "las": "Se las mandé." You can add "a Laura" or "a ella" to make "se" clear.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in the store.

image.alt: Inside a clothing store: a shop window with a mannequin, a clothes rack with a hanging tag, two fitting booths with curtains, a customer with a bag and a counter with a cash register. Five numbered markers.

questions.explanation: 1 is the shop window, "el aparador" (Spain: el escaparate); 2 the size tag (M), "la talla"; 3 the fitting rooms, "el probador"; 4 the counter with the register, "la caja"; 5 the shopper, "el cliente". The window's sign says "OFERTA", but the marker is on the window itself.

questions.stem: Name the numbered pieces of clothing.

image.alt: Six pieces of clothing in a grid, each with a numbered marker: a shirt with a collar and buttons, a blouse, a long coat, a striped scarf, a baseball cap and a belt with a buckle.

questions.explanation: 1 "la camisa" (a shirt with buttons and a collar), 2 "la blusa", 3 "el abrigo" (a long coat), 4 "la bufanda", 5 "la gorra" (a cap; "el sombrero" has a brim all the way around), 6 "el cinturón".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'm going to wrap it for you. (it = la camisa; you = tú)
questions.explanation: Person first, thing second: "te la". The pair goes before "voy" ("Te la voy a envolver") or joined to the infinitive with an accent ("Voy a envolvértela"). Both are accepted.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I gave it to her. (it = el anillo)
questions.explanation: "Le" + "lo" becomes "se lo", and "a ella" makes clear who "se" is: "Se lo di a ella." "A ella" can also come first for emphasis ("A ella se lo di"), and "Se lo di" alone is correct when the context shows who she is. The tile "le" can't be used: "le lo" is never correct.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ana ___ el abrigo porque hacía frío."
questions.explanation: The coat goes onto Ana herself, so the reflexive "ponerse" (to put on): "se puso". "Puso el abrigo" would need a place ("en la silla"). "Pusó" isn't a form: the strong preterite "puso" has no accent.

questions.stem: Complete: "No me acuerdo ___ su nombre."
questions.explanation: "Acordarse" always takes "de": "No me acuerdo de su nombre." (A1's "recordar" takes no preposition: "No recuerdo su nombre".)

questions.stem: What does "Nos conocimos en 2019" mean?
questions.explanation: With a plural subject, "nos" can mean "each other": "We met (each other) in 2019." In the preterite, "conocer" means "to meet for the first time" (lesson 03).

questions.stem: Complete: "Paola se enojó ___ Andrés."
questions.explanation: "Enojarse con alguien" = to get angry with someone. "De" goes with "quejarse" and "enamorarse"; "en" with "confiar".

questions.stem: How do you say "I fell asleep at the movies"?
questions.explanation: "Dormirse" (with se) is to fall asleep; "dormir" is to sleep. "Dormí en el cine" means "I slept at the movies". The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb, never after it.

questions.stem: Which is the correct way to write "I trust you"?
questions.explanation: "Confiar" takes "en", and its present stresses the "í", which needs a written accent: "confío" (con-FÍ-o). Without the accent, "confio" would be read with a different stress.

questions.stem: It's late and you want to leave the party. What do you say?
questions.explanation: "Irse" is to leave: "Me voy" (I'm leaving). "Ir" without "se" needs a destination ("Voy a casa"). "Me va" and "se voy" mix up the persons.

questions.stem: Read: "Martín y Clara se conocieron en el trabajo en 2020. Al principio no se llevaban bien: se peleaban por todo. En 2022 hicieron un viaje juntos y se enamoraron. Hoy están comprometidos." How did they get along at first?
choices: Very well: they fell in love at once.
questions.explanation: "No se llevaban bien: se peleaban por todo" = they didn't get along: they fought about everything. They fell in love in 2022 and are engaged now ("Hoy están comprometidos").

questions.stem: Which sentences mean "each other"? Select all that apply.
choices: Paola y Andrés se escriben todos los días.
Mi hermana y yo nos abrazamos en el aeropuerto.
Los novios se besaron en la plaza.
questions.explanation: Reciprocal "nos" and "se" need a plural subject: they write to each other, we hugged each other, the couple kissed each other. "Andrés se lava las manos" is reflexive (one person, himself), and "Me acuerdo de ti" is a pronominal verb.

questions.stem: Complete with the preterite of "sentirse" (yo): "Ayer ___ muy cansada."
questions.explanation: "Sentirse" + an adjective = to feel. The yo preterite is "me sentí", with the pronoun before the verb. (The e → i change appears only in the third person: "se sintió, se sintieron".)

questions.stem: Match each verb, in the meaning given, to the preposition it takes.
left: enamorarse (to fall in love with someone)
questions.explanation: "Quejarse de" (to complain about), "enojarse con" (to get angry with), "enamorarse de" (to fall in love with), "comprometerse con" (to get engaged to), "confiar en" (to trust). Other meanings take other prepositions: "quejarse con el gerente" (to complain to the manager), "comprometerse a llegar temprano" (to commit to arriving early).

questions.stem: This timeline tells a couple's story. Match each numbered point to what happened.

image.alt: A timeline with five years and a numbered picture above each: 2019, a speech bubble saying Mucho gusto; 2020, two cups of coffee on a table; 2021, a heart; 2023, a ring with a stone; 2024, two linked rings.

questions.explanation: 1 "Mucho gusto": they met, "se conocieron". 2 coffee for two: "salieron por primera vez". 3 a heart: "se enamoraron". 4 a ring with a stone: "se comprometieron". 5 two wedding rings: "se casaron".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: We're going to get married in June.
questions.explanation: The reflexive pronoun of "casarse" goes before "vamos" ("Nos vamos a casar") or on the end of the infinitive ("Vamos a casarnos"). "En junio" can go at the start or the end.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: They said goodbye (to each other) at the station.
questions.explanation: "Despedirse" changes e → i in the third-person preterite: "se despidieron". The place can go first or last: "Se despidieron en la estación" / "En la estación se despidieron".

questions.stem: A friend from Madrid says about your cousin Pablo: "Le vi ayer en el metro." How would a Mexican usually say it?
choices: La vi ayer en el metro.
Lo vi ayer en el metro.
Les vi ayer en el metro.
Se vi ayer en el metro.
questions.explanation: Using "le" for a man as direct object is Spain's leísmo. Mexico and most of Latin America use "lo": "Lo vi ayer." Both are accepted for one male person.

questions.stem: Which use of "le" does the RAE NOT accept as standard?
choices: El libro le compré ayer. (le = the book)
Le di el libro. (le = to Juan)
questions.explanation: The RAE accepts "le" for one male person (Spain's leísmo) and the courtesy "le" for usted, and "le" as an indirect object is standard everywhere. "Le" for a thing ("el libro le compré") is not accepted: it should be "lo".

questions.stem: In Mexico you hear: "—¿Ya saben tus papás? —Sí, ya se los dije." What does "los" show here?
choices: That the speaker is a man
That several people (the parents) were told
questions.explanation: What was told is one piece of news, so "los" isn't the thing. In much of Latin America the plural of the receivers moves onto the direct pronoun: "se los dije" = I told them. Careful standard: "Se lo dije (a ellos)".

questions.stem: Which is the careful standard way to write "I told them (it)"?
questions.explanation: "Les" + "lo" becomes "se lo". The DPD recommends "Se lo dije (a ellos)" in careful speech and writing, even though "se los dije" is very common in Latin American conversation. "Se les dije" is not standard (the grammar calls it false leísmo), and "les lo" never occurs.

questions.stem: "—¿Y los boletos? —Se los di a Marta." What does "los" refer to?
questions.explanation: Here the thing is plural ("los boletos"), so "los" is simply the direct object, as in lesson 07: "I gave them to Marta." Always check whether the thing is plural before reading "los" as "them (the people)".

questions.stem: An Argentine friend uses "vos". Which question would she ask?
questions.explanation: Voseo changes the subject pronoun and some verb forms, but the object pronoun stays "te": "¿Te llamo mañana?" "Os" belongs to Spain's vosotros; "le" would be usted.

questions.stem: In a café in Bogotá you hear: "¿Me regala un tinto, por favor?" What is the customer doing?
choices: Asking for a free coffee as a present
Asking for a glass of red wine
Offering to buy the waiter a coffee
Ordering a black coffee that he will pay for
questions.explanation: In Colombia "¿Me regala…?" is simply a polite way to ask for something, even when you pay. "Un tinto" there is a small black coffee.

questions.stem: Which request is the usual one in a Mexican café?
questions.explanation: "¿Me da…?" is the everyday polite request in Mexico (A1). "¿Me pone…?" is typical of bars in Spain, "¿Me regala…?" of Colombia, and a bare "Dame" can sound abrupt to a stranger.

questions.stem: Which are correctly written vos commands with pronouns? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Vos commands are stressed on the last syllable (contá, pasá, decí). With one pronoun the stress is second-to-last, so no accent: "contame", "decime". With two pronouns it's third-to-last, so the accent is needed: "pasámelo". "Contáme" has an unneeded accent, and "pasamelo" is missing one.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to where you're most likely to hear it.
left: Ya se los dije. (= to them)
choices: Mexico and much of Latin America
questions.explanation: Leísmo ("le vi") and bar orders with "poner" are typical of Spain; "¿Me regala…?" of Colombia; vos commands and "che" of Argentina; "se los dije" for "I told them" is very common in the speech of Mexico and much of Latin America (Argentina included). Each one is real usage somewhere.

questions.stem: Rewrite the Spain-style sentence with the pronoun Mexicans use: "A tu hermano le conozco desde niño." → "A tu hermano ___ conozco desde niño."
questions.explanation: "Conocer" takes a direct object, and your brother is a man: Mexico uses "lo": "A tu hermano lo conozco desde niño." "Le" here is Spain's leísmo.

questions.stem: You hear "Le dije la verdad a mis papás." How should it be written in a formal text?
choices: Le dije la verdad a mis papás.
Les dije la verdad a mis papás.
Se dije la verdad a mis papás.
Los dije la verdad a mis papás.
questions.explanation: Singular "le" for a plural person is common in speech, but careful writing matches the number: "les", for "mis papás". "Los" is a direct pronoun, and "se" only appears before "lo, la, los, las".

questions.stem: Build the shop assistant's question in Spanish.
questions.prompt: How can I help you? (usted)
questions.explanation: This courtesy "le" for usted is very common in Latin American service talk. Like any pronoun with an infinitive, it goes before "puedo" ("¿En qué le puedo ayudar?") or on the end of the infinitive ("¿En qué puedo ayudarle?").

questions.stem: What does "Esa frase me suena rara" mean?
choices: I hear that sentence a lot.
That sentence sounds strange to me.
questions.explanation: "Sonar" (to sound) works like "gustar" here: the sentence "sounds" strange to me. "Raro" means strange or odd (and also rare). "Me suena" alone would mean "it rings a bell".

questions.stem: An Argentine says "Contame" (tell me). Write the tú command a Mexican would use.
questions.explanation: The tú command of "contar" is "cuenta" (o → ue), plus "me": "cuéntame", with an accent because the stress is three syllables from the end. The vos form "contame" has no stem change and no accent.

questions.stem: How do you say "I dropped my keys"?
questions.explanation: The keys are the subject, so the verb is plural: "cayeron". "Se" always comes first, then the person: "se me". "Caí" would make "I" the one who fell.

questions.stem: What does "A Pablo se le olvidó la tarea" mean?
questions.explanation: "Se le olvidó" is the no-fault "se" with "le" = Pablo (doubled by "a Pablo"): the homework slipped his mind. "La tarea" (A1) is the subject.

questions.stem: Complete: "A nosotros se ___ acabó la leche."
questions.explanation: The person is "a nosotros", so the indirect pronoun is "nos": "Se nos acabó la leche" (we ran out of milk). The verb is singular because "la leche" is one thing.

questions.stem: Which sentence presents breaking the plate as an accident?
questions.explanation: The no-fault "se" says the plate broke "on me": "Se me rompió el plato." The other sentences use the active verb, which states what you did; "a propósito" even says it was on purpose.

questions.stem: When would you say "¡Perdón, se me hizo tarde!"?
choices: When you ask someone the time
questions.explanation: "Se me hizo tarde" (it got late on me) is a very common Mexican way to apologize for being late or say you lost track of time.

questions.stem: In Mexico, what does "Se me descompuso el carro" mean?
questions.explanation: "Descomponerse" is the everyday Mexican verb for a machine that stops working. "Lost" would be "se me perdió", and "crashed" "choqué" (lesson 03).

questions.stem: Your friend is leaving and you suddenly remember something: "¡Ah, se me olvidaba! Te traje un detalle." What does "se me olvidaba" mean here?
questions.explanation: In the imperfect, "¡Se me olvidaba!" is a fixed phrase for "I almost forgot!", said just before you mention the thing.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: A Luis se le perdió la cartera.
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the thing (olvidó + el paraguas, olvidaron + los boletos, perdió + la cartera) and "se" comes first. "Se me olvidé" puts the verb in the yo form, and "me se" has the wrong order.

questions.stem: Complete with the preterite of "caerse": "Se nos ___ los platos."
questions.explanation: The plates are the subject (plural), so the third-person plural preterite: "Se nos cayeron los platos" (we dropped the plates). "Caer" spells its third person with y: "cayó, cayeron".

questions.stem: Match each numbered panel to what happened.

image.alt: Four comic panels with numbered markers: coffee spilling from a tipping cup onto a laptop; a cracked phone on the ground under a bus-stop sign; a man outside a closed door thinking of keys on a table; a car stopped on a road with a fuel gauge on empty.

questions.explanation: 1 coffee on the laptop: "Se me derramó el café." 2 the phone on the ground: "Se me cayó el celular." 3 the keys left inside: "Se me olvidaron las llaves." 4 the empty fuel gauge: "Se nos acabó la gasolina." No dog or milk appears.

questions.stem: Match each phrase to its meaning.
questions.explanation: All five use the no-fault "se": things slip your mind (olvidarse), fall (caerse), run out (acabarse), get lost (perderse), or, without any accident, an idea occurs to you (ocurrirse). Something done on purpose uses the active verb: "Lo rompí a propósito."

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: We ran out of gas.
questions.explanation: "Se" first, then the person ("nos"), then the verb agreeing with the thing: "Se nos acabó la gasolina." The thing can also come first: "La gasolina se nos acabó." "Acabamos" would make "we" the subject ("we finished").

questions.stem: In the text "Un lunes terrible", why did the narrator have to wait for his neighbor?
choices: He had left his keys inside the house.
His brother forgot to fill the tank.
questions.explanation: "¡Se me olvidaron las llaves adentro! Tuve que esperar a mi vecina, que tiene una copia." He had left his keys inside, and the neighbor has a spare copy.

questions.stem: In an apology, what does "Fue un descuido, no lo hice a propósito" mean?
choices: It was a gift; I did it on purpose.
It was nobody's fault; it just happened.
It was careful; I did it slowly.
It was a slip; I didn't do it on purpose.
questions.explanation: "Un descuido" is a moment of carelessness, and "a propósito" means on purpose, the opposite of "sin querer" (lesson 03).

questions.stem: What is the gerund of "pedir"?
questions.explanation: "Pedir" is an -ir verb that changes e to i (pido, pidió), and the gerund changes too: "pidiendo". "Pediendo" forgets the change; "pidendo" drops the i of -iendo, and "pedindo" both forgets the change and drops the e.

questions.stem: What is the gerund of "leer"?
questions.explanation: The stem "le-" ends in a vowel, and Spanish doesn't let an unstressed i sit between two vowels, so -iendo is spelled -yendo: "leyendo" (like "oyendo", "trayendo").

questions.stem: A woman is on a park bench, reading. How do you say "She's sitting on the bench"?
questions.explanation: A position takes estar + the adjective "sentado", which agrees: "Está sentada". "Está sentando" doesn't work here (without an object, "sentar" needs "se"), "se está sentando" would mean she's sitting down right now, "Se sienta" describes a habit or the action of sitting down, and "ser" is never used for positions.

questions.stem: How do you say "I'm leaving tomorrow at eight"?
choices: Estoy saliendo mañana a las ocho.
Estoy a salir mañana a las ocho.
Estoy salido mañana a las ocho.
questions.explanation: Spanish doesn't use estar + gerund for plans. Use the present for a fixed arrangement, "Salgo mañana a las ocho", or ir a: "Voy a salir mañana". "Estoy saliendo" would mean you're walking out the door right now.

questions.stem: Complete: "¿Sigues ___ en Puebla?" (Are you still living in Puebla?)
questions.explanation: "Seguir" + gerund means "to still be doing": "¿Sigues viviendo en Puebla?" The infinitive, the present and the participle don't follow "seguir" with this meaning.

questions.stem: Look at the picture of the plaza. Who is lying on the grass?

image.alt: A plaza on a Sunday: a church in the background, a fountain in the middle with children running around it, an older man and a woman on a bench under a tree on the left, a young man lying on the grass in front of them, a girl with a red balloon and her father on the right, two women chatting further back, and a boy throwing a ball to a dog.

questions.explanation: "Un joven está acostado en el pasto": the young man in the foreground, in front of the bench. The older man is sitting on the bench, the girl is standing with her balloon, and the dog is running.

questions.stem: What does "Estaba lloviendo cuando salí" mean?
choices: It was raining when I left.
It had stopped raining when I left.
questions.explanation: "Estaba" + gerund is an action in progress in the past (it was raining), and the preterite "salí" is the event that happened during it (I left).

questions.stem: Which sentences correctly say "I'm reading it" about a book (el libro)? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The pronoun goes before "estar" ("Lo estoy leyendo") or is attached to the gerund, which then needs a written accent to keep its stress ("leyéndolo"). It never goes between "estar" and the gerund, and "leyendolo" without the accent is misspelled.

questions.stem: Type the gerund of "dormir".
questions.explanation: "Dormir" changes o to u in the gerund, like its él preterite "durmió": "durmiendo" (estoy durmiendo = I'm sleeping).

questions.stem: Complete with estar + the gerund of "correr": "Los niños ___ alrededor de la fuente." (The children are running around the fountain.)
questions.explanation: "Los niños" is ellos, so "están", and the gerund of the -er verb "correr" is "corriendo": "Los niños están corriendo alrededor de la fuente."

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in the plaza.

image.alt: The plaza picture without words, with five numbered markers: on the big tree on the left, on the bench, on the fountain in the middle, on the red balloon on the right and on the church in the background.

questions.explanation: 1 el árbol (tree), 2 la banca (bench; Spain says el banco), 3 la fuente (fountain), 4 el globo (balloon), 5 la iglesia (church, in the background). There is no bridge or traffic light in the picture.

questions.stem: Match each position phrase to its meaning.
questions.explanation: "Al fondo" is the back of the picture and "en primer plano" the front. "Junto a" is right beside, "alrededor de" around, and "en medio de" in the middle of. "Behind" is "detrás de", which isn't in the list.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'm chatting with my sister.
questions.explanation: estar + gerund: "Estoy platicando con mi hermana." "Estoy con mi hermana platicando" and, with emphasis on the person, "Con mi hermana estoy platicando" are also correct. "Soy" can't make the progressive, and "platicar" is the infinitive.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'm reading it (the book).
questions.explanation: "El libro" is masculine, so the pronoun is "lo", and it goes before "estar": "Lo estoy leyendo." (With these tiles, the attached form "Estoy leyéndolo" isn't possible, but it's also correct.) "La" would be for a feminine noun.

questions.stem: How do you say "She has straight hair"?
questions.explanation: Spanish uses tener + the article + the noun + the adjective: "Tiene el pelo lacio." The adjective agrees with "pelo", so it stays "lacio"; "ser" and "estar" don't work here, and Spanish uses "el", not "su", with parts of the body.

questions.stem: Your Mexican host says "Tus hijos son muy educados." What does she mean?
choices: Your children are very well educated.
questions.explanation: "Educado" is a false friend: it means polite, well-mannered. "Well educated" is "con estudios" or "culto"; "rude" is "grosero".

questions.stem: Complete: "Después de las vacaciones, mi papá ___ más delgado."
questions.explanation: A change ("after the vacation") takes "estar": "está más delgado" (he's thinner than before). "Es delgado" would describe what he's like in general.

questions.stem: How do you say "I look like my dad"?
questions.explanation: "To look like" is the reflexive "parecerse a": "Me parezco a mi papá." Without "me" it means "to seem", and the "a" before the person is needed.

questions.stem: Someone asks "¿Cuánto mides?" Which is a correct answer?
questions.explanation: "¿Cuánto mides?" asks your height, and the answer uses "medir" (mido): "Mido un metro setenta" (1.70 m). Weight is "pesar": "Peso setenta kilos."

questions.stem: Which is the kindest way to say that a friend's uncle is a bit overweight?
questions.explanation: "Un poco" and the soft word "llenito" (a bit plump) make it gentle. "Gordo", said directly about a person, can be rude, "muy gordo" even more so, and "feo" (ugly) isn't about weight at all.

questions.stem: In Mexico, what does "güero" usually describe?
questions.explanation: "Güero" (güera) is the everyday Mexican word for blond or fair; vendors also use it as a friendly way to call customers. Bald is "calvo" or "pelón", curly is "chino" or "rizado", and short is "bajo".

questions.stem: Read: "Daniela es alta, mide como un metro setenta y cinco. Antes tenía el pelo chino, pero ahora lo tiene lacio. Usa lentes." What does Daniela look like now?
choices: tall, with straight hair and glasses
tall, with curly hair and no glasses
short, with straight hair and glasses
questions.explanation: "Alta" is tall, "ahora lo tiene lacio" means her hair is straight now (it used to be "chino", curly), and "usa lentes" means she wears glasses.

questions.stem: Name the numbered features.

image.alt: Four faces with five numbered markers: on the first man's black beard, on the second man's gray mustache, on the top of the second man's head, on the third woman's curly brown hair, and on the fourth woman's long straight blond hair.

questions.explanation: 1 la barba (Raúl's beard), 2 el bigote (don Ernesto's mustache), 3 calvo (don Ernesto is bald on top), 4 el pelo rizado (Lucía's curly hair; chino in Mexico), 5 el pelo lacio (Sofía's straight hair). Nobody in the picture wears glasses, and no marker is on a nose.

questions.stem: Match each adjective to its meaning.
questions.explanation: amable = kind, tímido = shy, perezoso = lazy (Mexico also flojo), grosero = rude, egoísta = selfish. "Well educated" matches none of them; "educado" means polite.

questions.stem: Which adjectives have the same form for a man and a woman? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in -e ("amable", "alegre") and in -ista ("egoísta") don't change for gender. "Trabajador" becomes "trabajadora", and "tímido" becomes "tímida".

questions.stem: Complete with the present of "medir": "Mi hermana ___ un metro sesenta."
questions.explanation: "Medir" changes e to i in the present: mido, mides, mide. "Mi hermana mide un metro sesenta" (1.60 m).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: He has brown eyes and a beard.
questions.explanation: "Tener" + the article for the eyes ("los ojos cafés") and no article for a beard ("barba"). The two can go in either order: "Tiene los ojos cafés y barba" or "Tiene barba y los ojos cafés". "Es" doesn't work with features, and Spanish uses "los", not "sus", with body parts.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: You look a lot like your mom.
questions.explanation: "To look like" is "parecerse a": "Te pareces mucho a tu mamá" ("mucho" can also come at the end, and in speech "A tu mamá te pareces mucho" puts the person first). Without "te", "pareces" means "you seem", and "como" isn't used after "parecerse".

questions.stem: Complete: "Guadalajara tiene ___ un millón de habitantes."
questions.explanation: Before a number, "more than" is "más de": "más de un millón de habitantes". "Más que" compares two things ("más habitantes que Puebla").

questions.stem: Complete: "Chihuahua es el estado más grande ___ México."
questions.explanation: After a superlative, "in" is "de", not "en": "el estado más grande de México".

questions.stem: Complete: "Aquí no hay ___ carros como en el centro."
questions.explanation: Before a noun, "tanto" agrees with it: "carros" is masculine plural, so "tantos carros como". "Tan" goes with adjectives and adverbs ("tan grande como").

questions.stem: Which is the -ísimo form of "rico"?
questions.explanation: Drop the -o and add -ísimo; to keep the k sound, c becomes qu before i: "riquísimo". "Muy" isn't added, because -ísimo already means "very".

questions.stem: Look at the bar chart. Which sentence is true?

image.alt: Bar chart of population in 2020 in millions (INEGI): Estado de México 17.0, Ciudad de México 9.2, Jalisco 8.3, Veracruz 8.1, Colima 0.7.

choices: Colima tiene más de un millón de habitantes.
Veracruz es el estado más poblado.
Jalisco tiene casi tantos habitantes como Veracruz.
La Ciudad de México tiene menos habitantes que Jalisco.
questions.explanation: Jalisco (8.3 million) and Veracruz (8.1 million) are almost equal: "casi tantos habitantes como". Colima has less than a million (0.7), the State of Mexico is the most populous, and Mexico City (9.2) has more than Jalisco.

questions.stem: How do you say "Ana is younger than me"?
choices: Ana es más menor que yo.
questions.explanation: For age, "younger" is "menor" (or "más joven"), followed by "que" and a subject pronoun: "menor que yo". "Menor" is already a comparative, so no "más".

questions.stem: "¿Estás seguro de que el hotel es aquí? — Sí, estoy seguro." What does "estoy seguro" mean here?
questions.explanation: With "estar" and "de que", "seguro" means sure: "Are you sure the hotel is here? — Yes, I'm sure." With "ser" it means safe: "Es un barrio seguro".

questions.stem: Name the numbered places on the map of Mexico.

image.alt: A simple map of Mexico with five numbered markers: in a sandy area in the north, in a green area in the far south, on a small lake west of Mexico City, on the Pacific coastline in the south, and on a small island off the Yucatán Peninsula.

questions.explanation: 1 el desierto (the deserts of the north), 2 la selva (the rainforest of the south), 3 el lago (Lake Chapala, the largest in Mexico), 4 la costa (the Pacific coast), 5 la isla (Cozumel, in the Caribbean). Mexico City sits in a valley, but there is no marker on it.

questions.stem: Type the -ísimo form of "largo" (very long).
questions.explanation: Drop the -o and add -ísimo; to keep the hard g sound, g becomes gu before i: "larguísimo" (larguísima for a feminine noun: una fila larguísima).

questions.stem: Match each sentence to its meaning.
left: Es la más alta de la clase.
choices: She's the tallest in the class.
questions.explanation: tan … como = as … as; más … que = more … than; la más … de = the most … in; -ísima = extremely. "Less tall than me" would be "menos alta que yo".

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Es la ciudad más bonita del país.
Tiene más que dos millones de habitantes.
Lo mejor del campo es la tranquilidad.
questions.explanation: The superlative takes "de" ("del país"), "tanto como" after a verb doesn't change, and "lo mejor" means "the best thing". Before a number it's "más de dos millones", and "riquísima" never takes "muy".

questions.stem: Put these states in order from the most populous to the least populous (INEGI census, 2020).
questions.explanation: State of Mexico 17.0 million, Jalisco 8.3, Veracruz 8.1, Colima 0.7. "El Estado de México es el estado más poblado; Colima es el menos poblado."

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Lake Chapala is the largest lake in Mexico.
questions.explanation: The superlative: article + noun + "más" + adjective + "de": "El lago de Chapala es el lago más grande de México" (or, the other way round, "El lago más grande de México es el lago de Chapala"). After a superlative, "in" is "de", not "en".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: There isn't as much traffic as yesterday.
questions.explanation: With a noun, "as much … as" is "tanto … como", and "tanto" agrees with "el tráfico": "No hay tanto tráfico como ayer." "Tan" is for adjectives, and "que" goes with más and menos.

questions.stem: Complete: "¿Hay ___ elevador en el edificio?"
questions.explanation: Before a masculine singular noun, "alguno" drops its -o: "algún elevador". "Alguna" is feminine, and "ninguno" is the negative.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly says "Nobody came"?
questions.explanation: When the negative word comes after the verb, "no" goes before the verb: "No vino nadie." When it comes first, there's no "no": "Nadie vino." "Nadie no vino" mixes the two, and "Vino nadie" is missing "no".

questions.stem: Complete: "No tengo ___ problema."
questions.explanation: The negative before a masculine singular noun is "ningún": "No tengo ningún problema." "Ninguno" is used alone, and "algún" isn't used in this negative sentence.

questions.stem: Complete: "Puedes venir a ___ hora." (You can come at any time at all.)
questions.explanation: "Any at all, it doesn't matter which" before a noun is "cualquier", with the same form for both genders: "a cualquier hora". "Cualquiera" is used alone or after the noun, and "alguna" would be "some time".

questions.stem: Complete with the word for "too": "Las rentas aquí son ___ caras."
questions.explanation: Before an adjective, "demasiado" (too) never changes: "demasiado caras". It agrees only before a noun ("demasiadas escaleras"). "Muy" means "very", not "too".

questions.stem: Read the ad. If you pay the first month's rent and the deposit before you move in, how much do you pay?

image.alt: A rental ad: SE RENTA DEPARTAMENTO, Colonia Jardines; 2 recámaras, 1 baño; tercer piso con elevador; balcón con vista al parque; amueblado; área de lavado en la azotea; renta 9,500 MXN al mes, mantenimiento incluido; depósito: un mes; aval o póliza jurídica; sin mascotas.

questions.explanation: The rent is 9,500 pesos a month and the deposit is one month ("depósito: un mes"): 9,500 + 9,500 = 19,000 pesos.

questions.stem: In the ad, the washing area is "en la azotea". Where is that?
questions.explanation: "La azotea" is the flat roof you can walk on; in many Mexican buildings it has the water tank and a place to wash clothes. The ground floor is "la planta baja", and the balcony "el balcón".

questions.stem: Complete: "No conozco ___ en Monterrey."
questions.explanation: "Nadie" refers to a person, and a person as the object takes the personal "a": "No conozco a nadie." "Nada" is for things.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the building.

image.alt: The apartment building in cross-section without words, with five numbered markers: on the flat roof, on the washing machine on the roof, on the balcony on the right side, on the elevator cabin in the middle and on the ground floor at the bottom.

questions.explanation: 1 la azotea (the flat roof), 2 la lavadora (the washing machine, on the roof), 3 el balcón, 4 el elevador (in the middle of the building), 5 la planta baja (the ground floor). The building has no garden or stairs in the picture.

questions.stem: Make the sentence negative. "Siempre hay algo en el refri." → "Nunca hay ___ en el refri."
questions.explanation: The negative of "algo" is "nada". "Nunca" comes before the verb, so no extra "no" is needed: "Nunca hay nada en el refri."

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Nadie vive en la planta baja.
No vive nadie en la planta baja.
Nadie no vive en la planta baja.
questions.explanation: "Nadie vive" (negative word first, no "no") and "No vive nadie" (negative word after the verb, with "no") are both right, and so is "No hay ninguna lavadora". "Nadie no vive" mixes the two patterns, and "Hay nada" is missing "no".

questions.stem: Match each renting word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: el depósito = the deposit (often one month's rent), el aval = a guarantor who signs with you, el contrato = the lease, amueblado = furnished, la mudanza = the move (moving house). The landlord is "el dueño" or "la dueña".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Nobody lives on the ground floor.
questions.explanation: With the negative word first, there's no "no": "Nadie vive en la planta baja" (or, starting with the place, "En la planta baja nadie vive"). "Alguien" is "somebody", and "nada" is for things. (With "no" before the verb, "No vive nadie en la planta baja" is also correct.)

questions.stem: Build the question in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Is there a washing machine? (any washing machine at all)
questions.explanation: "La lavadora" is feminine, so "alguna": "¿Hay alguna lavadora?" "Algún" is for masculine nouns, and "ninguna" is the negative. (A simple "¿Hay lavadora?" is also natural.)

questions.stem: According to the lesson, in which year did the Mexican mural movement formally begin, with government commissions under José Vasconcelos?
questions.explanation: In 1921 José Vasconcelos became Secretary of Public Education and the government began commissioning murals. 1910 is the start of the Revolution, 1954 the year Frida Kahlo died, and 1997 the year the Hospicio Cabañas became a World Heritage Site.

questions.stem: Where is José Clemente Orozco's "El hombre de fuego" (The Man of Fire)?
choices: in the National Palace, Mexico City
at the Detroit Institute of Arts
questions.explanation: Orozco painted 57 frescoes in the Hospicio Cabañas in Guadalajara in the late 1930s, with "El hombre de fuego" in the dome. The National Palace and Detroit murals are Rivera's, and the Casa Azul is Kahlo's house.

questions.stem: How do you say "a painting by Rivera"?
questions.explanation: The artist is introduced with "de": "un cuadro de Rivera". "Por" only works with the participle: "pintado por Rivera".

questions.stem: Complete: "El cuadro representa ___ dos mujeres."
questions.explanation: People as the direct object take the personal "a", even in a painting: "Representa a dos mujeres."

questions.stem: A guide says: "Fíjate en los colores vivos." What should you notice?
questions.explanation: "Colores vivos" are bright, vivid colors. "Vivo" also means "alive", but with colors it means bright.

questions.stem: Look at the mural sketch. What are the two men in the center doing?

image.alt: A mural sketch: a snow-capped volcano and a big sun in the background, a cornfield in the middle, and in the foreground a teacher with two children on the left, two farmers in straw hats carrying a basket of corn in the center, and a woman with white flowers on the right.

choices: Están cargando una canasta de maíz.
questions.explanation: The two farmers ("campesinos") are carrying a basket of corn between them: "Están cargando una canasta de maíz." The woman on the right has the flowers.

questions.stem: Where was Frida Kahlo born?
questions.explanation: Frida Kahlo was born in 1907 in the Casa Azul in Coyoacán, Mexico City, today the Museo Frida Kahlo. Rivera was born in Guanajuato and Siqueiros in Chihuahua.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in the mural sketch.

image.alt: The mural sketch with four numbered markers: on the volcano in the background, on the sun at the top right, on the teacher on the left and on the white flowers on the right.

questions.explanation: 1 el volcán (al fondo), 2 el sol (arriba, a la derecha), 3 la maestra (en primer plano, a la izquierda), 4 las flores (a la derecha). There is no river or horse in the sketch.

questions.stem: Match each artist to a place or fact from the lesson.
choices: the staircase murals of the National Palace
questions.explanation: Rivera began the National Palace staircase in 1929; Orozco's best-known murals are in the Hospicio Cabañas; Kahlo was born in the Casa Azul; Siqueiros was born in Chihuahua in 1896. None of the four was born in Oaxaca.

questions.stem: Put the steps for describing a painting in the order the lesson recommends.
choices: the people and what they are doing
questions.explanation: The lesson's method goes from the outside in and ends with you: facts, scene, positions (al fondo, en primer plano), people (estar + gerund), colors, and finally your opinion and a comparison.

questions.stem: Type the Spanish for "self-portrait", with its article.
questions.explanation: "El autorretrato": auto- (self) + retrato (portrait). After the prefix the r is doubled to keep the trilled sound.

questions.stem: Which sentences correctly describe the portrait sketch? Select all that apply.

image.alt: A portrait sketch: a woman with dark braided hair and three flowers in it, strong dark eyebrows, a serious mouth, yellow earrings and a white blouse with an embroidered neckline, against green leaves.

questions.explanation: She isn't smiling (her gaze is serious), she has flowers in her hair, and there are green leaves in the background. She is not lying down, and she doesn't wear glasses.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: It's a painting by Frida Kahlo.
questions.explanation: "Es un cuadro de Frida Kahlo": "ser" says what something is, and "de" gives the artist. "Está" is for location or states, and "por" needs a participle (pintado por).

questions.stem: A friend in Mexico says about your new apartment: "¡Está bien bonito!" What does she mean?
questions.explanation: Before an adjective, "bien" means "very" in informal Mexican speech: "bien bonito" = really pretty. On its own after "estar", "bien" means fine ("Estoy bien").

questions.stem: Which spelling follows the standard Spanish spelling rules?
questions.explanation: The spelling rules treat super- as a prefix and join it without a hyphen or accent: "superfácil". "Súper fácil" written apart is very common in chats and informal writing; alone, "súper" has an accent ("¡Estuvo súper!").

questions.stem: Complete in standard Spanish: "Estoy ___ cansada." (I'm kind of tired.)
questions.explanation: Before an adjective, "medio" is an adverb and doesn't change: "medio cansada". "Media cansada" is heard but considered incorrect.

questions.stem: Which sentence is best in careful written Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Excelente", "pésimo" and -ísimo forms already mean "very good / very bad", so careful Spanish doesn't add "muy".

questions.stem: What does "Espérame tantito" mean?
choices: Wait for me for a long time.
questions.explanation: "Tantito" (from "tanto") is Mexican for "a little, a bit": "Espérame tantito" = wait a moment for me.

questions.stem: What is the -ísimo form of "amable"?
questions.explanation: Adjectives in -ble become -bilísimo: "amable → amabilísimo". The stress and the accent fall on the í of -ísimo.

questions.stem: What does "Lo bueno es que el hotel está cerquita" mean?
choices: The good one is that the hotel is close.
The good thing is that the hotel is really close.
The hotel is good because it is close.
questions.explanation: "Lo" + adjective means "the … thing": "lo bueno" = the good thing. The diminutive "cerquita" intensifies here: really close.

questions.stem: When is "¡Qué chido!" a good thing to say?
choices: in a letter to your bank
chatting with a friend about a concert
at the start of an exam essay
questions.explanation: "Chido" is very informal Mexican slang for "cool". It fits a chat with friends; in an interview, a letter or an exam, choose neutral words such as "excelente" or "muy bueno".

questions.stem: Type the strongest single word for "muy antiguo".
questions.explanation: "Antiguo" ends in -guo; to keep the sound, it becomes -quísimo: "antiquísimo" (una casa antiquísima).

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: "Padre" as an adjective is Mexican for cool; "un montón" is loads; "tantito" is a little bit; "pésimo" is terrible; "precioso" is beautiful. "Boring" would be "aburrido". (Careful: for "valuable", say "valioso"; "precioso" means valuable only in set phrases like "piedras preciosas".)

questions.stem: Put these from the weakest to the strongest.
questions.explanation: "Nada" (not at all), "un poco" (a bit), "muy" (very), and -ísimo (extremely) is the strongest.

questions.stem: Which of these are informal? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Padre" (cool), "bien" + adjective and "un montón" belong to informal speech. "Muy bonito" and "excelente" are neutral and fine anywhere.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The good thing is that the hotel is really close.
questions.explanation: "Lo bueno es que el hotel está cerquita." The neuter "lo" makes "the good thing"; location takes "estar". "Lo bueno es que está cerquita el hotel" is also possible.

questions.stem: What is the yo form of "tener" in the future?
questions.explanation: Tener is one of the verbs whose future stem changes: a d takes the place of the vowel, tendr- + -é = "tendré". "Teneré" adds the ending to the whole infinitive, which only regular verbs do; "tendría" is the conditional (would have); "tenré" leaves out the d.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly says "There will be a lot of people at the party"?
choices: Habrá mucha gente en la fiesta.
Habrán mucha gente en la fiesta.
Habré mucha gente en la fiesta.
Hay a haber mucha gente en la fiesta.
questions.explanation: "Habrá" is the future of "hay" (there is, there are) and, like "hay", it stays singular. "Habrán" is a plural that standard Spanish doesn't use for "there will be", "habré" is the yo form, and "hay a haber" mixes up "va a haber" (there is going to be).

questions.stem: Complete: "Si ___ tiempo, te ayudaré con la mudanza."
questions.explanation: After "si" in a sentence about a real possibility, Spanish uses the present, never the future: "Si tengo tiempo, te ayudaré." English does the same ("if I have time", not "if I will have time"). "Tendría" (would have) and "tuviera" belong to other kinds of "if" sentences that you will learn at B1.

questions.stem: A TV presenter says: "Mañana lloverá en el norte del país." What kind of statement is this, the typical home of the simple future?
questions.explanation: "Lloverá" (it will rain) is a prediction about tomorrow's weather, exactly where the simple future is most at home: forecasts, predictions, promises and formal plans. In conversation about personal plans, Mexicans usually prefer "ir a" + infinitive.

questions.stem: What does "Seguramente lloverá por la tarde" mean?
choices: It will very probably rain in the afternoon.
It will certainly rain in the afternoon.
It surely rained in the afternoon.
It will rain safely in the afternoon.
questions.explanation: "Seguramente" looks like "surely", but it usually means "very probably": the speaker expects rain but isn't certain. For certainty, Spanish says "seguro que" or "sin duda". "Lloverá" is future, so "rained" is wrong.

questions.stem: In the lesson's weather forecast, where will it rain in the afternoon?
questions.explanation: The presenter says: "En la Ciudad de México lloverá por la tarde, como es normal en la temporada de lluvias." Monterrey will be clear, dry and hot (36 degrees), and Guadalajara will have some clouds but be sunny most of the day.

questions.stem: Write the future of "salir": "Mañana el vuelo ___ a las siete." (Give only the verb.)
questions.explanation: Salir has the irregular future stem saldr- (a d takes the place of the i): saldré, saldrás, saldrá, saldremos, saldrán. "El vuelo" is él, so "saldrá". "Salirá" doesn't exist.

questions.stem: Complete with the yo form of "hacer" in the future: "¿Mis propósitos? Este año ___ más ejercicio." (Give only the verb.)
questions.explanation: Hacer shortens its future stem to har-: haré, harás, hará, haremos, harán. "Haceré" is a common mistake.

questions.stem: Match each infinitive to its yo form in the future.
questions.explanation: Three groups: the vowel drops (querr-, sabr-), a d takes its place (pondr-, vendr-), or the stem is shortened (dir-). "Poneré" and "deciré" add the ending to the whole infinitive, which these verbs don't do.

questions.stem: This is the forecast map from the lesson without the weather words. Choose the word for each numbered icon.

image.alt: The simplified map of Mexico with tomorrow's weather icons and temperatures but no weather words. Five icons are numbered: a sun near Monterrey, a cloud with rain near Mexico City, a dark cloud with lightning off Acapulco, a red spiral off the coast of Quintana Roo, and a gray cloud near Mérida.

questions.explanation: The sun means a sunny day (soleado); the cloud with drops is rain (lluvia); the dark cloud with lightning is a thunderstorm (tormenta, or tormenta eléctrica); the red spiral is the hurricane (huracán); the gray cloud alone means cloudy (nublado). There is no snow (nieve) or wind (viento) on the map.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Si llueve, no iremos a la playa.
Si lloverá, no iremos a la playa.
Te prometo que llegaré a tiempo.
Dentro de dos años tendré mi propio negocio.
questions.explanation: "Si llueve, no iremos" puts the present after si, as it should be; "Si lloverá" wrongly uses the future after si. "Te prometo que llegaré" is a promise with the future. "Habrán nubes" should be "Habrá nubes": the future of hay stays singular. "Dentro de dos años tendré…" is correct (tendr- + -é).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'll call you tomorrow.
questions.explanation: "Te" goes right before the conjugated verb: "te llamaré". The time word can start or end the sentence: "Mañana te llamaré" or "Te llamaré mañana". "Llamará" would mean "he/she will call".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Next year we'll travel to Peru.
questions.explanation: "Viajaremos" is the nosotros future (the whole infinitive + -emos, with no accent). The time phrase can go first, last, or right after the verb: "El año que viene viajaremos a Perú", "Viajaremos a Perú el año que viene", "Viajaremos el año que viene a Perú". "Viajarán" means "they will travel".

questions.stem: Complete: "Gracias ___ tu ayuda."
questions.explanation: After "gracias", Spanish always uses "por": you thank someone because of what they did (a cause). "Gracias para" is a typical English-speaker mistake.

questions.stem: Complete: "Estudio español ___ viajar por Latinoamérica."
questions.explanation: Purpose ("in order to") is "para" + infinitive: "Estudio español para viajar." "Por" would give a cause, not a goal. The second gap in the sentence, "por Latinoamérica", is "por" because it means "around, through" a region.

questions.stem: Complete: "La habitación cuesta 900 pesos ___ noche."
questions.explanation: A rate ("per") is "por": 900 pesos por noche, dos veces por semana, 100 kilómetros por hora. "A noche" copies English "a night" and isn't Spanish; "en noche" and "para noche" aren't either.

questions.stem: Complete: "Necesito los boletos ___ el viernes." (They must be ready by Friday.)
questions.explanation: A deadline is "para": "para el viernes" = by Friday. "Hasta el viernes" means "until Friday" (a period ending then), and "por el viernes" would suggest "around Friday" or "because of Friday".

questions.stem: What does "Trabajo por mi papá" mean?
choices: I work for my dad (he's my boss).
I work for my dad's sake (or in his place).
I work until my dad arrives.
questions.explanation: "Por" gives the reason or the person you act on behalf of: for his sake, because of him, or instead of him. If your dad is your employer, say "Trabajo para mi papá".

questions.stem: In the dialogue at the airline counter, why does Lucía ask for a window seat?
choices: She wants to sleep during the flight.
The aisle seats are all taken.
It's her first time in Yucatán and she wants to see the sea.
She gets nervous when she flies.
questions.explanation: Lucía says: "Ventanilla, por favor. Es mi primera vez en Yucatán y quiero ver el mar." The other reasons are not in the dialogue.

questions.stem: Which verb do people in Mexico usually use for checking a suitcase in at the airport?
questions.explanation: "Documentar" is the Mexican word: "Voy a documentar una maleta." Spain says "facturar". "Abordar" (Mexico) and "embarcar" (Spain) mean to board the plane.

questions.stem: Write por or para: "Cancelaron el vuelo ___ la tormenta."
questions.explanation: The storm is the cause of the cancellation, and cause is "por": "por la tormenta" = because of the storm. "Para la tormenta" would mean the flight was canceled for the storm's benefit.

questions.stem: Write the Mexican term for "boarding pass": "Tenga su ___ en la mano, por favor."
questions.explanation: In Mexico it's "el pase de abordar" (from abordar, to board). Spain says "la tarjeta de embarque". The pass shows your flight, seat and gate.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to the use of por or para in it.
questions.explanation: Por: price and exchange (por 500 pesos), movement through or around a place (por el centro). Para: the person who receives something (para ti), a destination (para Mérida), a purpose with an infinitive (para viajar). None of these sentences gives a cause (por la lluvia) or a deadline (para el lunes).

questions.stem: Five field names are missing from this boarding pass. Choose the name for each numbered field.

image.alt: The invented boarding pass from the lesson with five field names removed. Numbered values: Mérida (MID), CB 584, 07:45, 23 and 14A. The fields Pasajero, De and Fecha still have their names.

questions.explanation: Mérida is where Lucía is going (el destino); CB 584 is the flight number (el vuelo); 07:45 is the departure time (la salida, here departure, not exit); 23 is the gate (la puerta); 14A is the seat (el asiento), a window seat. A boarding pass doesn't show customs, and this flight has no stopover (escala).

questions.stem: Which sentences use por or para correctly? Select all that apply.
choices: Fui a la agencia para comprar los boletos.
Para mí, Oaxaca es el mejor destino.
questions.explanation: "Por internet" is a means (por). "Para comprar" is a purpose (para + infinitive). "Para mí" gives an opinion. "Gracias para todo" should be "Gracias por todo", and a price takes por: "Lo compré por 2,000 pesos".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I bought the ticket for 2,300 pesos.
questions.explanation: A price or exchange takes "por": "Compré el boleto por 2,300 pesos." Putting the price first ("Por 2,300 pesos compré el boleto") stresses the amount and is also correct. "Para 2,300 pesos" is wrong for a price.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Thanks for the invitation!
questions.explanation: "Gracias por" + what you are thankful for: "¡Gracias por la invitación!" "Para" is never used after gracias.

questions.stem: What does "Acabo de comprar los boletos" mean?
