choices: I'm going to buy the tickets.
questions.explanation: "Acabar de" + infinitive in the present means "to have just done": the action happened a moment ago. "Dejar de" is to stop, "voy a" is going to, and "acabar" alone is to finish.

questions.stem: How do you say "I stopped smoking a year ago"?
choices: Acabé de fumar hace un año.
Dejé de fumar hace un año.
Dejé a fumar hace un año.
questions.explanation: "Dejar de" + infinitive means to stop doing something, and it needs "de". "Dejé fumar" is missing it, "dejé a fumar" has the wrong preposition, and "acabé de fumar" means "I finished smoking" (that cigarette).

questions.stem: Complete: "¿Qué tal si ___ al cine el viernes?"
questions.explanation: After "¿Qué tal si…?" (How about…?) use the present: "¿Qué tal si vamos al cine?" The infinitive is wrong here, and the future and the preterite don't fit a suggestion.

questions.stem: A friend invites you to a party, but you have to work. Which answer is the most natural and polite?
choices: Lo siento, es que tengo que trabajar. ¿Qué tal otro día?
No quiero ir a tu fiesta.
questions.explanation: A gentle no has three parts: an apology (Lo siento), a reason with "es que", and another option (¿Qué tal otro día?). A bare "No" or "No quiero ir" sounds cold, and "Rechazo tu invitación" is a formal description, not something you say to a friend.

questions.stem: What does "Quedamos de vernos a las seis" mean?
choices: We stayed to see each other at six.
We saw each other until six.
We agreed to meet at six.
We were left alone at six.
questions.explanation: "Quedar de" + infinitive (very common in Mexico) and "quedar en" both mean to agree to do something. "Quedamos de vernos" = we agreed to see each other, to meet.

questions.stem: Look at the poster. Which statement is true?

image.alt: The poster for the invented Festival de Jazz Los Fresnos: Saturday 14 and Sunday 15 March at the Foro del Lago, Parque Los Fresnos; Saturday 19:00 Trío Luna; Sunday 13:00 Big Band Universitaria, for the whole family; tickets 250 pesos at the box office or online; children under 12 free; there will be food and board games.

choices: The family concert is on Saturday evening.
Tickets cost 250 pesos, and children under 12 get in free.
Tickets are sold only at the box office.
The festival lasts a whole week.
questions.explanation: The poster says "Boletos: 250 pesos" and "Niños menores de 12: gratis". The family concert (Big Band Universitaria, para toda la familia) is on Sunday at 13:00; tickets are sold "en taquilla o por internet"; and the festival is only Saturday and Sunday.

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "Empecé ___ jugar ajedrez el año pasado."
questions.explanation: "Empezar a" + infinitive = to start doing: "Empecé a jugar." The same "a" appears in "volver a" (to do again) and "ponerse a".

questions.stem: Write the yo preterite of "rechazar": "___ la invitación porque tenía que trabajar." (Give only the verb.)
questions.explanation: In the yo preterite, -zar verbs write c before é: rechazar → rechacé (like empezar → empecé). The other forms keep the z: rechazaste, rechazó.

questions.stem: Match each phrase to its meaning.
questions.explanation: "To start doing" would be empezar a, and "to try to" is tratar de or intentar.

questions.stem: Put the lines of this phone call in order.
choices: ¿Qué tal si vamos al festival el sábado?
¡Qué lástima! Es que el sábado tengo un compromiso.
El domingo sí estoy libre. ¡Me late!
questions.explanation: First the invitation; then the gentle no with a reason (es que…); then a new suggestion (¿Y el domingo?); then the yes; and only then the arrangement of where to meet.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Tengo ganas de ir a la playa.
questions.explanation: "Pensar" + infinitive takes no preposition, "volver a" and "tener ganas de" have theirs. "Dejé fumar" needs "de" (dejé de fumar), and "Empecé estudiar" needs "a" (empecé a estudiar).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I feel like going to the fair.
questions.explanation: "Tener ganas de" + infinitive: "Tengo ganas de ir a la feria." Putting "a la feria" first adds emphasis (it's the fair I feel like going to) and is also correct. "Voy" doesn't fit: "tengo ganas de" needs the infinitive "ir".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish, the Mexican way.
questions.prompt: We agreed to meet at six.
questions.explanation: "Quedar de" + infinitive is the Mexican way to say "agree to": "Quedamos de vernos a las seis." The time can also come first. "Vemos" is a conjugated verb; after "de" Spanish needs the infinitive "vernos".

questions.stem: Replace "la cebolla" with a pronoun: "Corta la cebolla."
questions.explanation: The pronoun goes on the end of an affirmative command, and the stress stays on cor-, now three syllables from the end, so it needs a written accent: "Córtala". "La corta" means "He cuts it", and "córtalo" is masculine, but "la cebolla" is feminine.

questions.stem: How do you tell a friend "Give it to me" (la cuchara)?
questions.explanation: Affirmative command + indirect pronoun (me) + direct pronoun (la), all one word: "Dámela". With two pronouns added, "da" is now stressed three syllables from the end, so it needs the accent. The pronouns can't go before an affirmative command, and the indirect one always comes first.

questions.stem: Which command does NOT need a written accent?
questions.explanation: "Pon" + "lo" makes a two-syllable word stressed on the first syllable (PON-lo), which is the normal stress, so no accent. "Dí-me-lo", "sír-ve-lo" and "cór-ta-la" are stressed three syllables from the end and must carry one.

questions.stem: A waiter is told (usted): "Sirva la sopa a los señores." How do you say it with two pronouns?
questions.explanation: "La sopa" becomes "la", and "a los señores" becomes "les", which changes to "se" before la: "Sírvasela". "Les" can never stand right before lo or la, and "a ella" would point to one woman, not to the gentlemen.

questions.stem: How do you tell a friend "Don't worry"?
questions.explanation: Negative commands use a different form, which you learn as a phrase for now: "No te preocupes" (tú), "No se preocupe" (usted). "No te preocupas" is a statement (You don't worry), and the pronoun can't be attached after "no".

questions.stem: Look at the recipe card. What do you do right after frying the rice?

image.alt: The arroz rojo recipe card: ingredients and seven numbered steps: 1 wash and drain the rice; 2 blend the tomatoes, onion and garlic with half a cup of broth; 3 heat the oil and fry the rice until golden; 4 add the sauce and mix; 5 add the rest of the broth and the salt, and boil; 6 cover and cook on low heat for about 15 minutes; 7 let it rest 10 minutes and serve.

questions.explanation: Step 3 is "Calentar el aceite y freír el arroz hasta dorarlo" and step 4 is "Agregar la salsa y mezclar". Washing the rice and blending the tomatoes come before; resting is the last step.

questions.stem: Write the tú command of "pelar" with the pronoun for "las papas": "___ y córtalas." (One word.)
questions.explanation: Pela + las = "pélalas". The stress stays on pe-, now three syllables from the end, so it needs a written accent, just like córtalas.

questions.stem: Write the usted command of "traer" with "me" and "lo": "Bring it to me, please." → "___, por favor." (One word.)
questions.explanation: The usted command of traer is "traiga" (from the yo form traigo). Add the indirect pronoun first, then the direct: traiga + me + lo = "tráigamelo", with an accent on the first a to keep the stress.

questions.stem: Match each command to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Pícala: pica + la. Dámelo: da + me + lo. Sírvesela: sirve + se (for le, to her) + la. Lávate: a reflexive command. No lo toques: a negative command learned as a phrase. "Don't forget" would be No te olvides, and "Cut them" córtalos or córtalas.

questions.stem: Name the numbered kitchen utensils.

image.alt: A kitchen counter with seven utensils and no labels. Six are numbered: a large pot with two handles and a lid, a frying pan with a long handle, a knife, a spoon, a fork and a drinking glass. A mug on the right has no number.

questions.explanation: 1 is the pot (la olla), 2 the frying pan (el sartén; la sartén in Spain), 3 the knife (el cuchillo), 4 the spoon (la cuchara), 5 the fork (el tenedor), 6 the glass (el vaso). The mug (la taza) isn't numbered, and there is no oven or plate in the picture.

questions.stem: Which commands are spelled correctly? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Córtala" and "dímelo" are stressed three syllables from the end, so they carry an accent. "Hazlo" has two syllables with normal stress and needs none. "Pónlo" shouldn't have one (ponlo), and "sirvelo" is missing it (sírvelo).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Wash your hands and sit down.
questions.explanation: Reflexive commands attach the pronoun: lávate, siéntate. With body parts Spanish uses "las manos", not "tus manos". The two commands can also come in the other order. "Te lava" means "he/she washes you".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Chop the onion and add it to the rice.
questions.explanation: "Agrégala" = agrega + la (the onion), with an accent because the stress is now three syllables from the end. "La agrega" isn't a command: it means "he/she adds it".

questions.stem: On a Mexican highway sign, what is "la cuota"?
questions.explanation: "La cuota" (la carretera de cuota) is the toll road: you pay at the caseta. The free road is "la libre", a speed bump is "un tope" and a detour is "una desviación".

questions.stem: What does a sign saying "PROHIBIDO REBASAR" tell drivers?
questions.explanation: "Rebasar" (Mexico; Spain adelantar) means to pass or overtake, and "prohibido" means forbidden: no passing. (Some painted signs say "No rebase", a negative command with the same meaning.) No parking is "No estacionarse"; reduce your speed is "Disminuya su velocidad".

questions.stem: Look at the toll receipt. How did the driver pay?

image.alt: The invented toll receipt: Autopista del Valle, Caseta Los Pinos; date 08/05, time 07:12; class: automóvil; form of payment: efectivo; rate: 173.00 pesos; ¡Buen viaje! Conserve su comprobante.

choices: they didn't pay: it was free
questions.explanation: The receipt says "Forma de pago: Efectivo", and "en efectivo" means in cash. The rate (tarifa) was 173 pesos.

questions.stem: Where would you say "Lleno, por favor"?
questions.explanation: "Lleno, por favor" (full, please) asks the attendant to fill the tank, so you say it at a gas station (la gasolinera). "Lleno" is masculine because it refers to el tanque.

questions.stem: In Valeria's blog, why did her brother drive slowly on the curves?
choices: because it was raining a little
because there was a speed bump
questions.explanation: The blog says "Mi hermano manejaba muy despacio en las curvas, porque llovía un poco." The detour came later, near Oaxaca.

questions.stem: Which verb from the blog sets the scene (imperfect) rather than moving the story forward?
questions.explanation: "Llovía" (it was raining) describes the background, so it is imperfect. "Salimos, pagamos, llegamos" are single events that move the story on, so they are preterite.

questions.stem: According to the lesson (2026), which number do you dial for the Ángeles Verdes, the free roadside help on federal highways?
questions.explanation: The Ángeles Verdes answer at 078. 074 is CAPUFE, on the toll roads it runs, and 911 is for emergencies. Check numbers before a trip: they can change.

questions.stem: Complete the itinerary: "El viernes saldremos ___ Oaxaca y pasaremos ___ Puebla."
questions.explanation: "Salir para" + place gives the destination (para), and "pasar por" + place is the route, through a place (por).

questions.stem: Write the Mexican word for "speed bump": "Cuidado, hay un ___ a la entrada del pueblo."
questions.explanation: In Mexico a speed bump is "un tope". Spain says "un resalto" or "un badén", and other countries have their own words.

questions.stem: Write the usted command of "poner" with the pronoun "le": "___ quinientos pesos de Magna, por favor." (One word.)
questions.explanation: The usted command of poner is "ponga" (from pongo). Adding "le" puts the stress three syllables from the end: "póngale", with an accent.

questions.stem: What does each numbered sign mean?

image.alt: Six road signs: a yellow diamond with a bump and the word TOPE; a white sign with VELOCIDAD MÁXIMA 110 km/h; a white sign with PROHIBIDO REBASAR; a white sign with NO ESTACIONARSE; an orange sign with DESVIACIÓN and an arrow; a green sign with CASETA DE COBRO 2 km.

questions.explanation: TOPE: a speed bump. VELOCIDAD MÁXIMA: the speed limit, 110 km/h. PROHIBIDO REBASAR: no passing. NO ESTACIONARSE: no parking (No + infinitive). DESVIACIÓN: a detour. CASETA DE COBRO 2 km: a toll booth in two kilometers.

questions.stem: Match each Mexican word to the word used in Spain.
questions.explanation: Mexico pays at la caseta, Spain at el peaje; rebasar = adelantar; la llanta = el neumático; estacionarse = aparcar; la licencia de manejo = el carné (or carnet) de conducir. El visado (la visa) and facturar (documentar) belong to air travel.

questions.stem: Put the events of Valeria's trip in the order of the blog.
choices: Paramos en una gasolinera en Puebla.
Encontramos una desviación cerca de Oaxaca.
questions.explanation: They rented the car and left; paid two tolls before Puebla; stopped for gas in Puebla; met a detour near Oaxaca; and finally parked in front of the hotel.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: We'll take the toll road to get there faster.
questions.explanation: Purpose is "para" + infinitive: "Tomaremos la cuota para llegar más rápido." The purpose can also come first ("Para llegar más rápido, tomaremos la cuota"). "Por llegar" would give a cause, not a goal.

questions.stem: Ana is late and doesn't answer her phone. Her friend says: "¿Dónde estará Ana?" What does this mean?
questions.explanation: With no future time word, the future here is a guess about the present: "Where can Ana be? I wonder where she is."

questions.stem: What does "Tendrá unos treinta años" mean?
questions.explanation: The future of probability makes a guess about now: "He must be about thirty, he is probably around thirty". "Unos" = about. "Next year" would need a time word.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a guess about the present?
choices: Ana no contesta; estará en el metro.
El vuelo saldrá a las ocho.
questions.explanation: Ana isn't answering now, so "estará en el metro" guesses where she is now (she's probably on the metro). The other three talk about the future: mañana, a scheduled flight, a promise.

questions.stem: What does "Debe de tener frío" mean?
questions.explanation: "Deber de" + infinitive is a guess: "He must be cold" (that's probably why he's shivering). Obligation would be "deber" + infinitive without de.

questions.stem: Which sentence expresses an obligation, as careful Spanish writes it?
questions.explanation: "Deber" + infinitive (no de) is the careful way to express obligation: you should, you must study more. "Debes de estudiar" is used for obligation in speech but careful Spanish keeps "deber de" for guesses. "Estudiarías" means "you would study", and "a lo mejor" means maybe.

questions.stem: Someone says "Dicen que mañana no habrá clases." You answer "Mmm… ¿será?" What do you mean?
questions.explanation: "¿Será?" on its own is a common skeptical reaction: could that be true? I wonder. It uses the future of probability of ser.

questions.stem: In the Mexico City study described in the lesson, about how many of the simple futures expressed doubts, guesses or estimates?
questions.explanation: Lastra and Martín Butragueño (2008) classed about 150 of the 243 simple futures they found as modal (doubts, guesses, estimates): roughly six in ten.

questions.stem: In the mini mystery, who probably ate the cake?
questions.explanation: Aunt Carmen is in the patio with an empty plate and chocolate on her face, and the crumbs lead there. Luisito guessed the dog ("Será el perro"), but Mom points out that the dog doesn't use a spoon.

questions.stem: Turn the fact into a guess with the future: "Son las tres." → "___ las tres." (One word.)
questions.explanation: Ser in the future is regular: será, serán. "Serán las tres" = it must be about three o'clock.

questions.stem: Turn the fact into a guess with the future: "Él tiene hambre." → "Él ___ hambre." (One word.)
questions.explanation: Tener has the irregular future stem tendr-: "Tendrá hambre" = he must be hungry, he's probably hungry.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to how sure the speaker is.
left: A lo mejor está en casa.
questions.explanation: The present states a fact; deber de (like the future of probability) is a confident guess; a lo mejor means maybe; and no sé says you have no idea. None of them is a promise.

questions.stem: Which sentences are guesses about the present? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "¿Qué hora será?" and "Estará en el tráfico" use the future of probability, and "A lo mejor está dormido" guesses with a lo mejor + present. "Mañana iremos" is a plan for tomorrow, and "Ya son las siete" is a fact.

questions.stem: Put these sentences in order, from the most sure to the least sure.
choices: A lo mejor está en casa.
questions.explanation: A fact in the present is the surest; deber de is a confident guess; a lo mejor is only maybe; no sé dónde está means you have no idea.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I wonder where my keys are.
questions.explanation: The future of probability turns the question into wondering: "¿Dónde estarán mis llaves?" In speech you can also put the topic first: "¿Mis llaves dónde estarán?" "Estarás" is the tú form and doesn't agree with "mis llaves".

questions.stem: Complete the sign in standard Spanish: "Se ___ departamentos."
questions.explanation: With the impersonal (passive) se, the verb agrees with the noun after it. Departamentos is plural, so: Se rentan departamentos. Se renta departamentos is sometimes seen on signs, but the plural is the standard form (the RAE's Diccionario panhispánico de dudas advises agreement). Rento and rentamos name a subject (I, we), which this kind of sign leaves out.

questions.stem: A sign on a shop door says "Aquí se habla inglés." What does it mean?
questions.explanation: Se + habla says that English is spoken here, without saying who speaks it. It isn't about one man (that would be Él habla inglés), it isn't a command (Hable inglés) and it says nothing about an obligation (Hay que hablar inglés).

questions.stem: Look at the job ad. Which shift is the job?

image.alt: The invented job ad from Clínica Santa Fe in Puebla: SE SOLICITA ENFERMERO O ENFERMERA. Requisitos: licenciatura en Enfermería, dos años de experiencia, disponibilidad para turno de noche. Ofrecemos: empleo de tiempo completo, sueldo de 14,000 pesos al mes, prestaciones de ley, capacitación. Interesados: enviar currículum por correo o presentarse de lunes a viernes de 9 a 14 h.

questions.explanation: The requirements say "Disponibilidad para turno de noche": the candidate must be available for the night shift. Nothing in the ad mentions mornings, afternoons or weekends.

questions.stem: In an interview, you talk about a job you had from 2019 to 2021 (you don't work there now). Which sentence fits?
choices: Trabajaba dos años en una fábrica.
Trabajo dos años en una fábrica.
Voy a trabajar dos años en una fábrica.
Trabajé dos años en una fábrica.
questions.explanation: A finished job with a set length (dos años) takes the preterite: Trabajé dos años en una fábrica. The imperfect (trabajaba) describes background or habits, not a closed period; the present and ir a talk about now and the future.

questions.stem: What does "Lo despidieron en marzo" mean?
questions.explanation: Despedir (despidieron) = to fire. "He said goodbye" needs the reflexive despedirse (Se despidió); "he quit" is renunció; "they hired him" is lo contrataron.

questions.stem: Complete: "Renuncié ___ mi trabajo en mayo."
questions.explanation: With a noun, renunciar takes a: renunciar a un trabajo, renunciar a un puesto. On its own it needs nothing: Renuncié en mayo.

questions.stem: A colleague in a Mexican office texts you: "Estoy en una junta, te marco al rato." What is she doing?
choices: She's on a call with a client.
questions.explanation: In Mexican offices la junta is the everyday word for a meeting at work (la reunión is the general word). Te marco al rato = I'll call you in a while.

questions.stem: Write the sign "Programmers wanted" with buscar: Se ___ programadores.
questions.explanation: Programadores is plural, so the verb is plural: Se buscan programadores.

questions.stem: Write the feminine forms: el abogado → la ___; el programador → la ___.
questions.explanation: Nouns in -o change to -a (abogada); nouns ending in a consonant add -a (programadora), like contador → contadora.

questions.stem: Match each job to what the person does.
questions.explanation: el contador keeps the accounts, el mecánico fixes cars, el enfermero looks after patients, el abogado gives legal advice, el programador writes software. Teaching children is what a maestro does.

questions.stem: Which signs use the standard agreement? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: With a plural noun the verb is plural (Se venden casas, Se necesitan programadores); with a singular noun it is singular (Se renta departamento). Se busca meseros and Se vende tamales are seen on signs, but the RAE's Diccionario panhispánico de dudas advises the plural with a plural noun (of things, or of people with no a before them), so they aren't the standard form.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: English is spoken here.
questions.explanation: Se + habla, with no subject: Aquí se habla inglés. The place can also go at the end: Se habla inglés aquí. Está can't replace habla.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Waiters wanted. (standard agreement)
questions.explanation: Meseros is plural, so the standard form is Se buscan meseros. Se busca meseros is seen on signs, but the RAE's Diccionario panhispánico de dudas advises plural agreement here (meseros has no a before it), so learn and write the plural.

questions.stem: Complete: "Es la escuela ___ estudié la primaria."
questions.explanation: For a place, use donde: la escuela donde estudié. Que alone would need a preposition (la escuela en que / en la que estudié); quien is for people; lo que means "what, the thing that".

questions.stem: Complete: "La profesora ___ me enseñó inglés se jubiló."
questions.explanation: With no preposition before it, the relative word for a person is que: la profesora que me enseñó. Quien is used after a preposition (con quien, de quien). Lo que has no noun before it, and donde is for places.

questions.stem: Complete: "La amiga con ___ estudio vive cerca."
questions.explanation: After a preposition, a person takes quien: la amiga con quien estudio. Con que is not used for a person; you could also say con la que.

questions.stem: Complete: "No entiendo ___ dices."
questions.explanation: Lo que = what, the thing that: No entiendo lo que dices. (The question word qué would also work here as an indirect question, but it isn't among the choices.) Que without lo or an accent doesn't fit; quien and donde are for people and places.

questions.stem: How do you say "the book I read"?
questions.explanation: Spanish never drops que: el libro que leí. English can leave out "that", Spanish can't. Lo que has no noun before it, and quien is for people after a preposition.

questions.stem: In Mexico, after secundaria, students who continue usually go to…
questions.explanation: The order is primaria (6 years), secundaria (3), preparatoria or prepa (usually 3), then the licenciatura (bachelor's degree) and the maestría (master's).

questions.stem: A student in a Mexican secundaria says "Saqué 6 en química." Under the SEP rules described in the lesson, what happened?
choices: She passed, with the lowest passing grade.
questions.explanation: In secundaria the scale runs from 5 to 10, and 6 is the lowest pass. So she passed, just. The top grade is 10, and 5 is a fail.

questions.stem: Type the relative word: "Puebla es la ciudad ___ conocí a mi esposa." (where)
questions.explanation: For a place, donde: la ciudad donde conocí a mi esposa. En donde, en que, en la que and en la cual are also correct.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence: "___ más me gusta es la química." (What I like most…)
questions.explanation: At the start of a statement, "what" is lo que: Lo que más me gusta es la química. Qué is a question word.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: la beca = scholarship; la calificación = grade (Spain: la nota); los apuntes = notes taken in class; la materia = a school subject; reprobar = to fail. "To enroll" is inscribirse.

questions.stem: Name the numbered levels of the Mexican education ladder.

image.alt: The education ladder from the lesson without the level names. Preescolar is labeled at the bottom; the five higher steps are numbered 1 to 5 and show only their usual length: 6 años, 3 años, 3 años, 4 a 5 años, 2 años.

questions.explanation: From the bottom: primaria (6 years), secundaria (3), preparatoria (usually 3), licenciatura (usually 4 to 5) and maestría (usually 2). El semestre is half a school year and la beca is a scholarship.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The friend I study with lives nearby.
questions.explanation: The preposition goes before quien, never at the end: la amiga con quien estudio. Con que is not used for a person. The subject can also come after the verb: Vive cerca la amiga con quien estudio.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I don't understand what the teacher says.
questions.explanation: "What" in a statement is lo que: No entiendo lo que dice la profesora (or lo que la profesora dice). Quien is for people.

questions.stem: Make the request with the conditional (usted): "¿___ ayudarme, por favor?" (poder)
questions.explanation: The conditional of poder uses the irregular stem podr-: podría. Podía is the imperfect, podrá the future, and podería doesn't exist.

questions.stem: What is the conditional of hacer for nosotros?
questions.explanation: Hacer has the stem har- in the future and the conditional: haríamos. Haceríamos uses the regular stem by mistake; hacíamos is the imperfect and haremos the future.

questions.stem: Which is the most polite way to ask a bank clerk for a form?
choices: ¿Me podría dar el formulario, por favor?
questions.explanation: Going down the politeness ladder: a command (Deme) is the most direct, then a present question (¿Me da?, ¿Me puede dar?), and the conditional with por favor (¿Me podría dar…, por favor?) is the softest.

questions.stem: The clerk asks: "¿Le importaría esperar un momento?" You don't mind. What is the clearest answer?
questions.explanation: ¿Le importaría…? asks whether it would bother you. No, para nada (no, not at all) says it doesn't. Sí, me importa means you do mind; No, gracias refuses; Me gustaría doesn't answer the question.

questions.stem: How do you say "to withdraw money from the ATM"?
questions.explanation: Sacar dinero (del cajero) = to take money out. Depositar is to pay in; cobrar is to charge (or to get paid); transferir is to move money to another account.

questions.stem: At a Mexican post office you ask for "dos timbres". What do you want?
questions.explanation: In Mexico el timbre is a postage stamp (la estampilla in much of Latin America, el sello in Spain). An envelope is el sobre, a receipt el ticket or la factura, a package el paquete. (El timbre is also a doorbell, but not at a post office counter.)

questions.stem: In the dialogue, why did the bank's system show a fee on Laura's account?
choices: It recorded the ATM as another bank's.
questions.explanation: The officer says "Fue un cajero de otro banco, por eso se cobró la comisión". Laura explains that the ATM was in the bank's own branch, so it was an error and the fee is returned.

questions.stem: Type the conditional (tú) of decir: "¿Me ___ la hora, por favor?"
questions.explanation: Decir has the stem dir- in the future and the conditional: dirías. (Decirías is a common mistake.)

questions.stem: Complete with the conditional of gustar: "Me ___ abrir una cuenta."
questions.explanation: Me gustaría = I would like. With an infinitive, gustaría stays singular.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in this bank and post office scene.

image.alt: The bank and post office scene from the lesson without labels. Numbered: 1 an ATM, 2 a line of three people, 3 a service window with a clerk, 4 a package on the counter, 5 an envelope, 6 the stamp in the envelope's corner.

questions.explanation: In the bank: el cajero automático (ATM) and la fila (the line of people). At the post office: la ventanilla (the service window), el paquete (package), el sobre (envelope) and el timbre (the stamp in its corner). La factura is an invoice and el préstamo a loan; neither is shown.

questions.stem: Which sentences use the conditional? Select all that apply.
choices: Me gustaría hablar con el técnico.
questions.explanation: Podría, gustaría and sería are conditional forms (-ía added to the infinitive or the stem). Podía and quería are imperfects, polite in their own way but not conditional.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Could you fix the leak tomorrow? (to the plumber, usted)
questions.explanation: ¿Podría arreglar la fuga mañana? uses the conditional of poder, with the irregular stem podr-. The time can also come before the object or at the start. Podería doesn't exist: poder never keeps its e in the conditional.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'd like to make a transfer.
questions.explanation: Me gustaría + infinitive: Me gustaría hacer una transferencia. Gustarías would mean "you would please", which doesn't fit.

questions.stem: How do you say "I broke my arm"?
questions.explanation: For your own body, Spanish uses the reflexive pronoun and the article: Me rompí el brazo. The pronoun already says whose arm it is, so mi is not used; se doesn't go with the yo form rompí.

questions.stem: The doctor asks "¿Desde cuándo le duele?" Which answer is correct?
questions.explanation: For a period up to now, use desde hace + time: Desde hace tres días. Desde alone goes with a point in time (desde el sábado).

questions.stem: Which is the softest advice?
questions.explanation: The conditional deberías is the softest and most polite. Tener que and deber in the present are firmer, and hay que states a general rule.

questions.stem: Complete in the standard pattern: "Yo que tú, ___ al dentista hoy."
questions.explanation: Yo que tú (if I were you) is followed by the conditional: iría. Iba is the imperfect, iré the future and fui the preterite.

questions.stem: What does "Me duele una muela" mean?
questions.explanation: La muela is a back tooth (molar), so Me duele una muela is the usual way to say you have a toothache. Neck is el cuello, knee la rodilla, shoulder el hombro.

questions.stem: In Mexico, what does "Me lastimé el hombro" mean?
questions.explanation: Lastimarse is the usual Mexican verb for "to hurt oneself" (Spain: hacerse daño). Burned is me quemé; broke is me rompí.

questions.stem: In the dialogue, what does the doctor find after the X-ray?
choices: Diego's knee is broken and needs a cast.
The bone isn't broken: it's a bad knock.
questions.explanation: The doctor says "el hueso no está roto. Es un golpe fuerte, no es nada grave". She tells him to rest for a week, so he can't play this Saturday.

questions.stem: Type the preterite: "Ayer mi hermana se ___ la mano con el sartén." (quemar)
questions.explanation: Quemarse in the preterite, ella: se quemó. With a body part, the article (la mano), not su.

questions.stem: Type the conditional (tú) of deber for soft advice: "___ dormir más."
questions.explanation: Deberías + infinitive is polite, soft advice: Deberías dormir más (You should sleep more).

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this picture.

image.alt: The person from the lesson without labels. Numbered: 1 a small bandage on the forehead, 2 the neck, 3 a shoulder, 4 a finger, 5 a knee, 6 a cast on one forearm.

questions.explanation: The bandage on the forehead covers la herida (wound); 2 is el cuello (neck), 3 el hombro (shoulder), 4 el dedo (finger), 5 la rodilla (knee) and 6 el yeso (the cast on the forearm). La muela and el hueso can't be seen.

questions.stem: Put Diego's story in order.
choices: La doctora me dio una receta.
questions.explanation: The background comes first in the imperfect (Estaba jugando futbol), then the events in the preterite: he fell, which hurt his knee, so he went to the clinic, where the doctor gave him a prescription.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: You should rest for a week. (soft advice, tú)
questions.explanation: Deber + infinitive, with no word in between: Deberías descansar una semana. Deberías a descansar is a common mistake.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: If I were you, I'd go to the doctor.
questions.explanation: Yo que tú + conditional: Yo que tú, iría al médico. Yo que tú can also come at the end. Iba (imperfect) doesn't give advice.

questions.stem: In which section of a Mexican CV do you list your bachelor's degree?
questions.explanation: Degrees and courses go under Formación académica. Experiencia laboral is for jobs, Datos personales for contact details, and Idiomas y habilidades for languages and skills.

questions.stem: One job on a CV says "Coordiné un equipo de cinco personas." Which next line keeps the same style?
questions.explanation: The first line uses a first-person preterite with no yo, so the next should too: Aumenté. Aumento de… is the noun style (fine, but not mixed with verbs), the infinitive isn't used, and the imperfect with yo breaks the pattern.

questions.stem: Which greeting follows the Spanish convention for a formal e-mail?
questions.explanation: Spanish puts a colon after the greeting of a letter or formal e-mail: Estimada Lic. Pérez: The comma is the English habit; querida is for people close to you; a semicolon isn't used.

questions.stem: Under the Ley Federal del Trabajo, when must the aguinaldo be paid?
choices: with the first paycheck of the year
questions.explanation: Article 87 says the aguinaldo (at least fifteen days' pay) must be paid before December 20.

questions.stem: Under article 133 of the Ley Federal del Trabajo, which of these may an employer NOT demand?
choices: a copy of the candidate's CV
a medical certificate showing that a woman is not pregnant
questions.explanation: Fraction XIV of article 133 forbids demanding a no-pregnancy certificate to hire, keep or promote someone. A CV, an ID and proof of a degree are normal parts of an application.

questions.stem: What does "Quedo a sus órdenes" mean at the end of a formal e-mail?
questions.explanation: A sus órdenes is a polite Mexican formula: "at your service". It isn't about orders in the literal sense.

questions.stem: The interviewer asks: "¿Por qué dejó su último empleo?" Which answer uses the past tenses correctly?
choices: Terminó mi contrato y quería un puesto con más responsabilidad.
Terminaba mi contrato y quise un puesto con más responsabilidad.
Termina mi contrato y quiero un puesto con más responsabilidad.
Ha terminado mi contrato y querré un puesto con más responsabilidad.
questions.explanation: The contract ending is a finished event (preterite: terminó); what you wanted at the time is a state in the background (imperfect: quería). The other options mix the tenses the wrong way round or use the present and future.

questions.stem: What does "Tengo disponibilidad inmediata" mean in a cover e-mail?
choices: I need an answer right away.
I'm available for an interview today only.
questions.explanation: La disponibilidad = availability; inmediata = immediate. It tells the employer you can start at once.

questions.stem: Write the preterite (yo) for a CV line: "___ a empleados nuevos." (capacitar)
questions.explanation: Capacitar is a regular -ar verb: capacité (I trained). The written accent is on the final é.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: la vacante = job opening; las prestaciones = employment benefits; el logro = achievement; la habilidad = skill; el aguinaldo = year-end bonus. A recruiter is el reclutador.

questions.stem: Name the numbered section headings of this Mexican CV.

image.alt: The invented CV of Ana Sofía Ruiz Castro without its five section headings, numbered 1 to 5. Under 1: a phone number, an e-mail and Guadalajara, Jalisco. Under 2: one sentence about the job she wants. Under 3: two jobs with dates. Under 4: a degree from the Universidad de Guadalajara and a diploma course. Under 5: languages and computer skills.

questions.explanation: The usual order is Datos personales (contact details), Objetivo profesional (one sentence), Experiencia laboral (jobs, most recent first), Formación académica (degrees and courses) and Idiomas y habilidades. A cover letter is a separate document.

questions.stem: Which of these belong in a formal cover e-mail? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Le adjunto mi currículum, Quedo atento a su respuesta and a greeting like Estimado Ing. Garza: are all formal formulas with usted. ¿Qué onda? (What's up?) and Besos are for friends.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'm attaching my CV. (formal)
questions.explanation: Le adjunto mi currículum: le = to you (usted). Lo would mean "it" and can't sit next to mi currículum here.

questions.stem: Under the Ley Federal del Trabajo, how much paid vacation does a worker get after the first year?
questions.explanation: Article 76 gives at least 12 working days after one year, rising by two days a year up to 20. (Before the 2023 reform it was 6.)

questions.stem: The receptionist says "Permítame un momento." What should you do?
questions.explanation: Permítame un momento = One moment, please: she is asking you to hold.

questions.stem: What does "¿Me comunica con la licenciada Ríos?" mean?
choices: Could you put me through to Ms. Ríos?
Could you give Ms. Ríos a message?
Is Ms. Ríos in a meeting?
Could Ms. Ríos call me back?
questions.explanation: Comunicar con = to put through to. A message is un recado; "in a meeting" is en una junta; "call me back" is que me marque / ¿Podría decirle que me marque?

questions.stem: Your friend's voice stops in the middle of a call. When you call back, you say:
questions.explanation: Se cortó la llamada = the call got cut off. Se oye muy bien means the line is good; Le comunico is what an operator says; Deje su mensaje is the voicemail recording.

questions.stem: Which is the most polite way to ask to change an appointment?
questions.explanation: The conditional question ¿Sería posible…? is the softest. Cambie is a command, quiero is direct, and a bare infinitive sounds like a sign or a note.

questions.stem: In Sofía Treviño's voicemail, when will the order arrive?
questions.explanation: She says "va a llegar el jueves, no el miércoles": the new day comes after the correction, so Thursday. Listen for the word after no or sino.

questions.stem: Why is the order late, according to the voicemail?
questions.explanation: The message says "por la lluvia": because of the rain.

questions.stem: How do you read the sign _ in an e-mail address?
questions.explanation: _ is guion bajo (underscore). Punto is the dot, arroba is @, and guion is the hyphen.

questions.stem: Write the Spanish word for the sign @.
questions.explanation: The @ in an e-mail address is la arroba: luis arroba correo punto mx.

questions.stem: Complete the usual phone formula: "___ Paul Smith." (Paul Smith speaking.)
questions.explanation: On the phone, Habla + name says who is speaking: Habla Paul Smith (also Le habla Paul Smith). Soy Paul Smith is also heard and is correct.

questions.stem: Match each phrase to its meaning.
choices: Would you like to leave a message?
questions.explanation: Le comunico = I'll put you through; Le marco más tarde = I'll call you later; No se oye bien = I can't hear well; ¿Quiere dejarle un recado? = Would you like to leave a message? Permítame un momento = One moment, please. "Who's calling?" is ¿De parte de quién?

questions.stem: Put this voicemail in the order the lesson recommends.
choices: Hola, buenas tardes, habla Paul Smith.
Este mensaje es para la licenciada Ríos.
Le llamo por la cita del viernes.
Mi número otra vez: 55 47 12 30 89. Gracias, hasta luego.
questions.explanation: Name first, then who the message is for, the reason, the polite request with the number, and the number again with goodbye.

questions.stem: You are spelling a name with a v and want to be sure it isn't written with a b. What can you say? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Ve chica and ve de vaca both point to v. Be grande and be de burro point to b.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Could you put me through to sales? (usted)
questions.explanation: ¿Me comunica con ventas? uses the usted present of comunicar, the usual polite Mexican request. Comunico would mean "I put through".

questions.stem: Look at the message slip. Who called?

image.alt: The message slip from the lesson. RECADO. Para: Ing. Garza. De: Sofía Treviño, Transportes del Norte. Teléfono: 81 2345 0678, ext. 112. Mensaje: El pedido llega el jueves, no el miércoles (lluvia). Llamar para confirmar la hora. Recibió: Daniela, martes 4:15 p. m.

questions.explanation: De: (from) names the caller, Sofía Treviño. Para: is who the message is for (Ing. Garza), and Recibió: is who took the message (Daniela).

questions.stem: Your friend Ana calls and says: "Estoy en el tráfico." You pass it on to someone next to you right away. What do you say?
choices: Ana dice que estoy en el tráfico.
Ana dice que está en el tráfico.
Ana dice está en el tráfico.
Ana dice que estaba en el tráfico.
questions.explanation: With "dice que" the tense stays the same and the person changes: Ana's "estoy" (I am) becomes "está" (she is). "Dice que estoy" would mean that you are in traffic; "dice está" drops "que", which Spanish never leaves out; "estaba" puts it in the past, but she is in traffic now.

questions.stem: Your boss asks: "¿Vienes a la junta?" A coworker tells you what he asked. Which is correct?
choices: Pregunta que vienes a la junta.
Pregunta sí vienes a la junta.
Pregunta si vienes a la junta.
Pregunta cuándo vienes a la junta.
questions.explanation: A reported yes/no question takes "si" (whether), with no accent: "Pregunta si vienes a la junta." "Sí" with an accent means "yes"; "que" alone doesn't introduce a question; "cuándo" asks "when", which the boss didn't ask.

questions.stem: Yesterday Luis told you: "Estoy enfermo." Today he is fine again. How do you report what he said?
questions.explanation: A state at the time someone spoke goes into the imperfect after "dijo que": "Dijo que estaba enfermo." The present ("está") would mean he is still sick, which isn't true, and "dice" reports something he is saying now. The preterite "estuvo" presents the illness as a finished event, which is not what Luis said.

questions.stem: Marta told you this morning: "Perdí el vuelo." Complete the report: "Marta dijo que ___ el vuelo."
questions.explanation: A finished event that someone told about stays in the preterite, and the person changes from yo to ella: "Marta dijo que perdió el vuelo." "Perdí" keeps Marta's "I" (it would mean you missed it); "perdía" describes an ongoing or repeated situation; "pierde" is the present. (Careful writing may also use "había perdido", honors lesson 24h1.)

questions.stem: A journalist asks: "¿Cuándo es la elección?" Complete the report with one word: "La periodista pregunta ___ es la elección."
questions.explanation: Questions with a question word keep the word, and it keeps its written accent: "pregunta cuándo es la elección". Without the accent, "cuando" means "when" in a statement, not in a question.

questions.stem: Complete: "La ciudad tiene dos ___ de habitantes." (two million inhabitants)
questions.explanation: "El millón" is a noun with a plural, "los millones", and takes "de" before the noun: "dos millones de habitantes". The plural loses the written accent (mi-YO-nes ends in -s and keeps the stress on the second-to-last syllable). "Miles" means thousands.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: El titular is the headline, la encuesta a survey or poll, el periodista a journalist (also la periodista), la revista a magazine and el canal a TV channel. A newspaper is el periódico.

questions.stem: Which of these reported sentences are correct Spanish? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Dice que llega mañana" keeps que and the tense; "Pregunta dónde vives" keeps the question word with its accent; "Dijo que estaba en casa" uses the imperfect for a state. "Dice está cansada" drops "que", and "Pregunta sí…" puts an accent on "si" (whether), which then means "yes".

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this newspaper front page.

image.alt: The front page of an invented newspaper with five numbered parts: 1 the line with the day, 2 the large line of text at the top, 3 a picture of a fire truck, 4 the text in columns, 5 a small bar chart.

questions.explanation: 1 is la fecha (Martes 10 de marzo), 2 el titular (the headline), 3 la foto, 4 el artículo (the article that tells the story), and 5 la encuesta (a survey, shown as a chart). La revista is a magazine and el canal a TV channel.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: She said she was tired.
questions.explanation: "Dijo que estaba cansada": the imperfect "estaba" for her state at the time she spoke, and "que" is required. "Estuvo" presents the tiredness as a finished event, which is not what she said. The subject "ella" can be left out, as here.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: My grandfather is asking what channel it is.
questions.explanation: A reported question keeps the question word with its accent: "Mi abuelo pregunta qué canal es." Spanish also allows the subject after the verb: "Pregunta mi abuelo qué canal es." "Si" is only for yes/no questions.

questions.stem: Look at the survey chart. Which statement is true?

image.alt: A bar chart from an invented survey of young people about where they get their news: redes sociales 62 %, televisión 18 %, periódicos 13 %, radio 7 %.

choices: La mitad de los jóvenes escucha la radio.
Más de la mitad de los jóvenes se informa por redes sociales.
El 18 por ciento de los jóvenes lee periódicos.
questions.explanation: Social media has 62 %, which is more than half (la mitad). Only 7 % listen to the radio (not half, but not nobody either), and 18 % is television; newspapers have 13 %.

questions.stem: How do you say "40 percent of Mexicans" in Spanish?
choices: el 40 por ciento de los mexicanos
los 40 por ciento de los mexicanos
el 40 por cientos de los mexicanos
la 40 por ciento de los mexicanos
questions.explanation: A percentage usually takes the singular masculine article "el" (never "los" or "la"), and "por ciento" never takes a plural -s: "el 40 por ciento de los mexicanos" (written 40 %).

questions.stem: What does this news sentence mean? "Según los testigos, el ladrón se escapó en bicicleta."
choices: The witnesses say they saw the thief riding a bicycle.
The thief told the witnesses that he had a bicycle.
According to the witnesses, the thief escaped on a bicycle.
After the witnesses left, the thief took a bicycle.
questions.explanation: "Según" means "according to" and names the source of the information; "se escapó" is "escaped" (lesson 03). The other options add things the sentence doesn't say.

questions.stem: Your friend says: "Hay que reciclar más." You agree. What do you say?
questions.explanation: "Estar de acuerdo" uses estar, and "with you" is "contigo": "Estoy de acuerdo contigo." "Soy de acuerdo" and "Tengo de acuerdo" use the wrong verb, and "a ti" is the wrong preposition.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "You're right"?
questions.explanation: "To be right" is "tener razón": "Tienes razón." The other three translate English word for word with ser or estar.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ llovía, nos quedamos en casa." (Since it was raining, …)
questions.explanation: "Como" (since, as) gives the reason at the start of the sentence. "Por eso" and "así que" introduce a result, so they come after the reason; "pero" means "but".

questions.stem: "¿Por qué no fuiste a la fiesta?" — "___ estaba muy cansado."
questions.explanation: An answer to "¿por qué?" starts with "porque" (because). "Como" gives a reason only before the result in the same sentence, and "así que" and "por eso" introduce a consequence.

questions.stem: Complete: "Hacía mucho calor, ___ abrimos todas las ventanas."
questions.explanation: The heat is the cause and opening the windows the result, so you need a word for the consequence: "así que" (so). "Porque" would make the windows the reason for the heat; "como" goes at the start; "aunque" (although) gives a contrast.

questions.stem: Translate into Spanish: "I don't think so." (an answer to a yes/no question)
questions.explanation: "Creo que no" is the usual answer; "No creo" alone is also fine. "Pienso que no" and "Me parece que no" are correct too. Don't add a sentence after "No creo que…": that needs a B1 verb form.

questions.stem: Complete with proteger: "Yo ___ mis plantas del sol."
questions.explanation: Before o and a, the g of proteger is spelled j to keep the same sound: "protejo". "Protego" would be pronounced with a hard g; "proteje" is a misspelling of "protege" (él); "protegió" (with an accent) would be a preterite.

questions.stem: Match each phrase to what it does.
questions.explanation: "Yo no lo veo así" (I don't see it that way) is a soft way to disagree; "Tienes razón" agrees; "¿Qué opinas?" asks for an opinion; "por eso" introduces a result; "como" at the start of a sentence gives the reason. None of them is an apology.

questions.stem: Which kind of waste goes in each numbered bin? And what is item 4?

image.alt: Three trash bins with numbers 1 to 3. Bin 1 holds a banana peel and leaves; bin 2 holds a bottle, a can, a glass jar and a cardboard box; bin 3 holds a roll of toilet paper and a diaper. Number 4 is on the bottle.

questions.explanation: Food scraps and leaves are organic (orgánicos). The bottle, can, jar and cardboard can be recycled (inorgánicos reciclables). Used toilet paper and diapers can't (inorgánicos no reciclables). Item 4 is la botella.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Creo que es una buena solución.
questions.explanation: "Es importante" takes the infinitive directly, with no "de". "Creo que" takes the ordinary verb forms. "Planeta" is masculine, although it ends in -a: "el planeta", never "la planeta".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: In my opinion, it's necessary to protect the environment.
questions.explanation: "Es necesario" + infinitive, with no "de". "En mi opinión" can start or end the sentence or come in the middle between commas, and the infinitive phrase can also come first: "En mi opinión, proteger el medio ambiente es necesario."

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: There was a lot of traffic, so I took my bike.
questions.explanation: The reason comes first and "así que" introduces the result: "Había mucho tráfico, así que tomé la bici." The imperfect "había" describes the situation and the preterite "tomé" the single action. "Aunque" (although) would give a contrast, not a result.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, what has Mexico City required of households since 1 January 2026?
choices: To recycle only paper and glass
To buy bins of three official colors
To sort their trash into organic, recyclable and non-recyclable waste
To take their trash to a recycling center themselves
questions.explanation: Since 1 January 2026, sorting household waste is required in Mexico City, in three main groups: orgánicos, inorgánicos reciclables and inorgánicos no reciclables, collected on different days. The lesson doesn't give official colors, and rules can change.

questions.stem: Complete: "En el lago hay muchos ___." (fish, swimming in it)
questions.explanation: A living fish is "el pez", plural "los peces" (z changes to c before e). "El pescado" is fish as food.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I attended my cousin's wedding"?
choices: Ayudé a la boda de mi primo.
Asistí a la boda de mi primo.
Atendí la boda de mi primo.
Asistí la boda de mi primo.
questions.explanation: "Asistir a" means "to attend": "Asistí a la boda de mi primo." It's a false friend: "to help" is "ayudar". "Atender" is to serve or attend to (a customer), and "asistir" needs "a" before the event.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Although it rained, we went to the party"?
choices: Aunque llovió, pero fuimos a la fiesta.
Llovió, aunque fuimos a la fiesta.
Aunque llovió, fuimos a la fiesta.
Aunque llovió, sin embargo fuimos a la fiesta.
questions.explanation: "Aunque llovió, fuimos a la fiesta." After an "aunque" part, Spanish doesn't add "pero" or "sin embargo". "Llovió, aunque fuimos a la fiesta" puts "aunque" on the wrong part ("It rained, although we went").

questions.stem: You are writing to your landlord, señora Ruiz, whom you don't know well. Which opening fits?
choices: Estimada señora Ruiz: Le escribo para…
Estimada señora Ruiz: Te escribo para…
questions.explanation: A formal message uses a formal greeting and usted all the way through: "Estimada señora Ruiz: Le escribo para…" The third option mixes a formal greeting with tú ("te"); the others are informal.

questions.stem: Complete: "Te escribo ___ darte las gracias por el regalo."
questions.explanation: "Te escribo para…" + infinitive states the purpose of the message, and purpose is "para" (lesson 14). "Por darte las gracias" would mean "because of thanking you".

questions.stem: Write the Spanish connector for "however" that usually starts a sentence after a period: "El salón era pequeño. ___, todos bailamos."
questions.explanation: "Sin embargo" (however) contrasts with the sentence before; it usually follows a period or semicolon and is followed by a comma. ("No obstante" means the same, in a more formal style.)

questions.stem: Match each situation to the best message.
left: You arrived late to a dinner.
Your aunt sent you a present.
You want a friend to come over.
choices: Te pido una disculpa por llegar tarde.
¿Quieres venir a mi casa el sábado?
questions.explanation: Congratulate with "¡Felicidades por…!", apologize with "Te pido una disculpa por…" (Mexico), thank with "¡Muchas gracias por…!" and invite with "¿Quieres venir…?" "Lamento no poder asistir" declines an invitation, which none of the situations asks for.

questions.stem: Who or what is each numbered part of this invitation?

image.alt: An invitation card for a quince años party with four numbers: 1 beside Rosa y Ernesto Díaz, 2 beside the name Mariana in large letters, 3 beside Sábado 14 de marzo, 4 beside Av. Juárez 120, Puebla.

questions.explanation: Rosa and Ernesto Díaz invite the guests, so they are los anfitriones (the hosts). Mariana is la quinceañera, the girl turning fifteen. Sábado 14 de marzo is la fecha, and Av. Juárez 120 is la dirección (the address) of the party hall. El brindis (toast) and el pastel (cake) happen at the party, not on the card.

questions.stem: Which sentences use the past tenses correctly? Select all that apply.
choices: Daniela llevaba un vestido azul y estaba muy contenta.
Ayer fui a una boda y bailé mucho.
Cuando era niña, iba a muchas fiestas.
Cuando tuve diez años, mi familia se mudó.
questions.explanation: Description in the imperfect (llevaba, estaba), events in the preterite (fui, bailé), childhood habits in the imperfect (era, iba) and an experience up to now in the perfect (nunca he bailado) are all right. Age in the past is background, so it needs the imperfect: "Cuando tenía diez años…".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'm writing to thank you for the invitation.
questions.explanation: "Te escribo para…" + infinitive gives the purpose; "por" goes with the reason for thanking: "darte las gracias por la invitación". "Te escribo" opens the message, so it comes first.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Although she was tired, she went to the party.
questions.explanation: "Aunque" + the ordinary verb forms: "Aunque estaba cansada, fue a la fiesta" (or "Fue a la fiesta aunque estaba cansada"). The imperfect "estaba" describes how she felt; the preterite "fue" is what she did. "Fui" is "I went".

questions.stem: At a party, who is "la anfitriona"?
choices: The woman who gives the party
The woman who makes the toast
questions.explanation: El anfitrión / la anfitriona is the host or hostess. A woman who was invited is "una invitada", the fifteen-year-old is "la quinceañera", and anyone can make "el brindis".

questions.stem: Read: "Hola, Pablo: ¡Felicidades por tu graduación! Te escribo para disculparme: el viernes no puedo ir a la ceremonia. Sin embargo, el sábado regreso, así que te invito a cenar." What will the writer do on Saturday?
questions.explanation: He can't go to the ceremony on Friday ("no puedo ir"), but he gets back on Saturday, "así que te invito a cenar": so he invites Pablo to dinner.

questions.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: El salón era pequeño sin embargo todos bailamos.
El salón era pequeño, sin embargo todos, bailamos.
El salón era pequeño. Sin, embargo todos bailamos.
El salón era pequeño. Sin embargo, todos bailamos.
questions.explanation: "Sin embargo" usually follows a period (or a semicolon) and is followed by a comma: "El salón era pequeño. Sin embargo, todos bailamos."

questions.stem: How long is the reading test (Comprensión de lectura) of the DELE A2?
questions.explanation: Reading takes 60 minutes. Writing takes 45, listening 40, and the speaking test 12 minutes after 12 minutes of preparation.

questions.stem: A candidate scores reading 20, writing 14, listening 18 and speaking 11. What is the result?
choices: No apto: group 2 has only 29 points
Apto: every test has at least 10
No apto: group 1 has fewer than 35
questions.explanation: Group 1 (reading + writing) is 20 + 14 = 34; group 2 (listening + speaking) is 18 + 11 = 29. Each group needs at least 30, so the result is No apto, whatever the total.

questions.stem: Which statements about the DELE A2 match the official exam guide? Select all that apply.
choices: Each listening recording is played twice.
Wrong answers in the reading test lose points.
In the second writing task you choose one of two options.
Answers in Latin American Spanish are accepted.
The speaking test has no preparation time.
questions.explanation: Recordings are played twice, the second writing task offers two options, and any standard variety of Spanish used consistently is accepted. Wrong answers in reading cost nothing, and the speaking test has 12 minutes of preparation.

questions.stem: Match each DELE A2 test to its length.
questions.explanation: Reading 60, listening 40, writing 45 minutes; speaking lasts 12 minutes after 12 minutes of preparation. No test lasts 25 minutes.

questions.stem: Complete with the present of corregir: "Yo siempre ___ mis errores."
questions.explanation: "Corregir" changes e → i like pedir, and spells the g sound with j before o: "corrijo" (yo), "corriges", "corrige".

questions.stem: Choose the form a Mexican speaker would use: "Ayer ___ al cine con mis primos."
questions.explanation: A finished event at a finished time (ayer) takes the preterite: "fui". The perfect "he ido" doesn't go with "ayer"; "iba" describes a habit or background; "voy" is the present.

questions.stem: "¿Le diste el libro a Ana?" — "Sí, ___."
questions.explanation: Indirect before direct, and "le" becomes "se" before "lo": "Sí, se lo di." "Le lo" is never used, "lo le" has the wrong order, and "se le" is missing the direct object "lo".

questions.stem: You ask a stranger for directions. Which is the most polite?
choices: ¿Me podría decir dónde está la estación?
questions.explanation: The conditional question "¿Me podría decir…?" is the most polite (lesson 19). "Dime" is a direct tú command, "¿Me dices…?" is friendly and informal, and "Dígame" is a direct usted command.

questions.stem: Complete: "Este regalo es ___ ti."
questions.explanation: A recipient takes "para": "para ti" (lesson 14). "Por ti" means "because of you" or "for your sake", which doesn't fit a present.

questions.stem: Complete: "No hay ___ problema."
questions.explanation: After "no" + verb, use the negative "ningún" before a masculine singular noun: "No hay ningún problema" (double negative, lesson 12). "Algún" is positive, and "nada" and "nadie" don't go before a noun.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I have never been to Oaxaca.
questions.explanation: An experience up to now takes the perfect: "Nunca he estado en Oaxaca." "Nunca" goes before the verb (no "no" needed when it comes first); "en Oaxaca" can also come first. "Ha estado" is the wrong person.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: He asked me if I had time.
questions.explanation: A reported yes/no question takes "si" (whether) with no accent, and the past report puts "tienes" into the imperfect: "Me preguntó si tenía tiempo." "Sí" with an accent means "yes".

questions.stem: What does this instruction ask you to do? "Indique si la frase es verdadera o falsa."
choices: Write one true sentence and one false one.
Say whether the sentence is true or false.
questions.explanation: "Indique" is an usted command (indicate, say), "si" means "whether", and "verdadera o falsa" is "true or false".

questions.stem: Write the Spanish for "to make a mistake" (with cometer).
questions.explanation: "Cometer un error" is the usual phrase; "hacer un error" is an English-style mistake.

questions.stem: Last week Raúl said: "Te llamaré mañana." Report it in careful written Spanish: "Raúl dijo que me ___ al día siguiente."
questions.explanation: After a past reporting verb, the future becomes the conditional: "llamaré" → "llamaría" (he said he would call me the next day). "Llamaré" keeps Raúl's "I"; "llamó" says he did call, which isn't what he said; "llamaste" is "you called".

questions.stem: In careful writing, how do you report "He terminado el informe"? "Dijo que ___ el informe."
questions.explanation: The present perfect shifts to the pluperfect: "había terminado" (had finished). "Terminaría" and "habría terminado" are conditional forms (would finish, would have finished); "terminaba" means was finishing.

questions.stem: Last year Carla told you: "Vivo en Mérida." She has since moved to Cancún. Which report is right?
choices: Carla dijo que vive en Mérida.
Carla dijo que viviría en Mérida.
Carla dijo que vivía en Mérida.
Carla dijo que vivió en Mérida.
questions.explanation: The present shifts to the imperfect: "vivía". Keeping "vive" would mean she still lives there, which isn't true now. "Viviría" is a conditional, and "vivió" presents her life there as a finished event, which isn't what she said.

questions.stem: Pedro told you: "Mañana voy al dentista." A week later you tell someone. Which report fits?
choices: Pedro dijo que al día siguiente iba al dentista.
Pedro dijo que mañana iba al dentista.
Pedro dijo que el día anterior iba al dentista.
Pedro dijo que ese día fue al dentista.
questions.explanation: A week later, Pedro's "mañana" is no longer tomorrow, so it becomes "al día siguiente" (the next day), and "voy" becomes "iba". "El día anterior" is the day before; the last option changes what Pedro said.

questions.stem: "¿Dónde has dejado las llaves?" → "Me preguntó ___"
questions.explanation: Keep the question word with its accent and shift the perfect to the pluperfect: "dónde había dejado las llaves". "Si" is only for yes/no questions; "donde he dejado" has neither the accent nor the shift; "qué" asks something else.

questions.stem: What does this mean? "El vocero negó la noticia."
questions.explanation: "Negar" (niego, negó) is "to deny", and "el vocero" is the spokesperson (Mexico; Spain says "el portavoz"). "To announce" is "anunciar" and "to confirm" "confirmar".

questions.stem: What does "Me dijo que lo llamara" mean?
choices: He told me he would call me.
He told me that I called him.
He told me he had called.
He told me to call him.
questions.explanation: "Llamara" is a B1 form (past subjunctive) used to report a command: "Llámame" → "Me dijo que lo llamara" (he told me to call him). Recognize the -ara / -iera ending.

questions.stem: Which sentence reports the command "Llámame" without the new -ara form?
choices: Me dijo que tenía que llamarlo.
questions.explanation: "Tener que" + infinitive reports the command with forms you know: "Me dijo que tenía que llamarlo" (he told me I had to call him). "Lo llamaba" means I was calling him; a command form can't follow "que" in a report; "lo llamaré" keeps a future that doesn't fit.

questions.stem: Report with the conditional: "Vendré el lunes." → "Dijo que ___ el lunes."
questions.explanation: Venir has the irregular stem vendr- in the future and the conditional: vendré → vendría.

questions.stem: Match each original form to how it is reported after "dijo que" in careful Spanish.
questions.explanation: Present → imperfect (estaba), future → conditional (vendría), present perfect → pluperfect (había comido), ir a in the present → ir a in the imperfect (iba a salir). "Estuve" is a preterite and isn't the shifted form of anything here.

questions.stem: Which tenses usually stay the same after "dijo que"? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Estaba cansada" → Dijo que estaba cansada; "Me gustaría ir" → Dijo que le gustaría ir. The future shifts to the conditional, and the present to the imperfect (unless it is still true now).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: She asked me if I would come.
questions.explanation: A reported yes/no question takes "si", and a future in the original ("¿Vendrás?") becomes the conditional: "Me preguntó si vendría." "Vendré" doesn't shift.

questions.stem: In the retold museum report, what did the spokesperson clarify ("aclaró")?
choices: That the museum would close in January
That the works would cause problems
That the shop was still open
That the discount ended the next day
questions.explanation: "El vocero del museo aclaró que la tienda seguía abierta": he clarified that the shop was still open. The director announced the closing, the works caused no problems, and the discount ended that same day.

questions.stem: In the first draft of Example 1, why is "es cerca del centro" wrong?
choices: It should be "es lejos del centro".
questions.explanation: Where something is uses estar: "está cerca del centro". Ser is for what something is like (es tranquila, es segura).

questions.stem: Which correction fixes "Mi primer trabajo fue en una cafetería, cuando tuve diecisiete años"?
questions.explanation: Age in the past is background, so it takes the imperfect: "cuando tenía diecisiete años". The perfect, the conditional and the present don't fit a past setting.

questions.stem: Valeria asked about a neighborhood and about transport. A reply that only says "¡Qué buena noticia! Te veo el sábado. Un abrazo" would lose points mainly because…
choices: it uses tú with a friend
it is far too short and misses points of the task
it is in Latin American Spanish
questions.explanation: The task asked for a neighborhood, an answer about transport and a day to meet, in 60–70 words. A missing point costs more than a small grammar mistake. Using tú with a friend is right, and Latin American Spanish is accepted.

questions.stem: Which of these take a capital letter in Spanish? Select all that apply.
choices: the first word of a sentence
questions.explanation: Sentences, names of people and names of places start with a capital. Months, days of the week and nationalities don't: en mayo, el lunes, una amiga mexicana.

questions.stem: Write the word with its missing written accent: "transporte publico" → "transporte ___"
questions.explanation: Público is stressed on the third syllable from the end (PÚ-bli-co), and every word stressed there carries a written accent (la tilde).

questions.stem: Match each phrase to its meaning.
questions.explanation: "O sea" rephrases informally, "es decir" does the same more carefully, "en cuanto a" moves to a new point, and "por otro lado" adds a different idea. "However" is "sin embargo".

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in this picture of a bus terminal.

image.alt: A drawing of a bus terminal with six numbers: 1 on the ticket window on the left, 2 on the clock on the wall, 3 on the bus seen through the window at the back, 4 on the bench in the foreground, 5 on the big suitcase, 6 on what the older man on the right is reading.

questions.explanation: 1 la ventanilla (the ticket window), 2 el reloj (the clock, showing a quarter past ten), 3 el autobús, 4 la banca (bench), 5 la maleta (suitcase), 6 el periódico. There is no fountain (la fuente) or balloon (el globo) in the picture.

questions.stem: In the model photo description, what is the girl doing?
questions.explanation: "La niña está comiendo una manzana y la mamá está mirando su celular." The young man is buying a ticket and the older man is reading the newspaper.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: In the foreground, a girl is eating an apple.
questions.explanation: Estar + gerund for what is happening in the picture: "En primer plano, una niña está comiendo una manzana." The position phrase can also go at the end. "Es comiendo" is not Spanish.

questions.stem: Why does the lesson suggest moving through present, past and future in the prepared talk?
choices: Because the exam requires exactly three tenses
Because examiners only grade the future
It shows your range of grammar on topics you choose
questions.explanation: You choose what to say, so you can show the present, the past tenses and the future safely. The guide doesn't require a set number of tenses.

questions.stem: At the ticket window you didn't catch the departure time. What do you say?
questions.explanation: Asking for repetition is part of a real conversation: "Perdón, ¿puede repetir?" The others close a conversation or a talk, or offer to pay.

questions.stem: Which sentence describes what is happening in the photo right now?
choices: La mamá está mirando su celular.
La mamá mira su celular todos los días.
La mamá miró su celular ayer.
La mamá va a mirar su celular.
questions.explanation: Estar + gerund describes what is happening in the picture: "está mirando". The other sentences describe a habit, a past event and a plan.

questions.stem: Which is true about "o sea"?
choices: It is formal and best in writing.
It is used only in Spain.
It is informal and very common in Mexico; don't overuse it.
questions.explanation: "O sea" (I mean) rephrases what you just said. It is informal and very common in Mexico, so once or twice in a talk sounds natural; too many sound nervous. "However" is "sin embargo".

cards.front: Three strategies for a long text
cards.back: Use cognates (el mecanismo, perfecta), guess from context, and skip words the sentence doesn't need. Look up only what blocks the story.

cards.front: Imperfect or preterite in a story?
cards.back: Imperfect = the scene and repeated actions (había un reloj, yo lo ayudaba). Preterite = events that move the story (Toqué. Nadie abrió.). Follow the preterites to find the plot.
A note, a sign or a book "says": El cuaderno decía: «aquí». = The notebook said: "here".

cards.front: Guessing a word from context: the steps
cards.back: What kind of word is it? What does it do in the sentence? Make a guess, then read on and check it. (las manecillas marcaban las cuatro → the hands)
A conclusion the text supports but doesn't state. Ya es hora: it's time for the clock, and don Ernesto, to move on. Every "why" answer needs a line from the text.
An earlier event told later. Rebuild the real order from time clues: hace treinta años, ese día, dos meses después, hoy.
Find what each replaces: La buscamos = buscamos la llave; me la dio = me dio la pieza; se lo llevó al hospital = she took him to the hospital.
to wind up a clock (la cuerda = the spring, also rope)
It's time. / It's about time.
Skimming: fast reading for the main idea (title, first lines). Scanning: hunting for one detail (a number, a name, a date).
a small black coffee. Everywhere, vino tinto = red wine.
avocado in Peru, Chile, Argentina and Uruguay (from Quechua). Mexico: el aguacate (from Nahuatl).
the city bus; the subway. Mexico: el camión / el autobús; el metro.
Great! Cool! (Venezuela, Colombia, the Caribbean, parts of Peru and Ecuador). Mexico: ¡Qué padre!
Stress on the ending, no stem change: vos sos (tú eres), vos querés (quieres), vos tenés (tienes), vos podés (puedes).
Infinitive without -r, stressed on the last vowel: mirá, tomá, vení, decí (tú: mira, toma, ven, di). With a pronoun: mirame, contame.
Reversed: in Buenos Aires or Santiago, July is winter (pleno invierno) and December is summer.

cards.front: Bogotá, Lima, Buenos Aires: one fact each
cards.back: Bogotá: about 2,600 m up, cool all year (14 °C average). Lima: on the Pacific, gray in winter, very little rain. Buenos Aires: on the Río de la Plata; Latin America's first subway (1913).
Mexico (like the US) writes 2,600; Colombia and Argentina usually write 2.600. Same number.

cards.front: The order of a short biography
cards.back: Birth and childhood → studies → work and main achievement → later life → death → why the person matters today.
en 1943 (no article); el 19 de marzo de 1943; a los quince años; en los años setenta; a partir de 1932; desde 1973.
The present for past events: nace en 1889, gana un concurso, recibe el Nobel. Common in biographies and timelines; read it as the past (usually the preterite).
convertir A en B = to turn A into B (convirtió un baño en un laboratorio). convertirse en = to become (se convirtió en un héroe).
Spanish uses the active verb nacer: nació, nacieron.
After el primero / la primera: que + verb (que ganó) or en + infinitive (en ganar).
Mexican chemist. 1974: CFCs destroy the ozone layer (with F. S. Rowland). 1995: Nobel Prize in Chemistry, the first Mexican to win it.
Chilean teacher and poet (born Lucila Godoy Alcayaga). Worked in Mexico from 1922 with Vasconcelos. 1945: the first Latin American Nobel Prize in Literature.
Baseball player from Puerto Rico, Pittsburgh Pirates 1955–1972, 3,000 hits. Died on 31 December 1972 flying aid to Nicaragua after an earthquake. Hall of Fame 1973.
A written biography says murió; se murió is everyday speech.
Predict the words → listen for the gist (who, where, why) → listen for key words and numbers → check with the transcript → replay what you missed.
going to, bound for / coming from, arriving from. Pasajeros con destino a Cancún…; el vuelo procedente de Bogotá…
please … (polite instruction in Mexico and other parts of Latin America): Favor de abordar. Favor de no fumar.
final call (at an airport)
16:45 = 4:45 p.m. Announcements use the 24-hour clock.
el locutor / la locutora (announcer), los oyentes (listeners), la emisora (station), el boletín (bulletin), el noticiero (news program, Mexico), transmitir en vivo (to broadcast live).
podcast: written with an accent in Spanish; plural los pódcast. Podcasts have episodios, and you se suscribe (subscribe).
para, para el (casual speech). Write para.
cansado, usted, verdad: the d of -ado and a final d weaken or drop in relaxed speech. Recognize them; keep the d yourself.
Radio phrases: "… here with you" (Les saluda Andrea Ruiz); "talk to you next time" (Nos escuchamos la próxima semana).
-ar: é, aste, ó, amos, aron. -er/-ir: í, iste, ió, imos, ieron. Pronouns stay in front: me casé, se graduó.
-e, -iste, -o, -imos, -ieron, with no written accents: anduve, anduviste, anduvo, anduvimos, anduvieron
andar anduv-, estar estuv-, tener tuv-, poder pud-, poner pus-, saber sup-
venir vin-, querer quis-, hacer hic- (él: hizo)
decir dij-, traer traj-, conducir conduj-. The ellos ending is -eron: dijeron, trajeron, condujeron.
anduve, anduviste, anduvo, anduvimos, anduvieron (not andé)
there was / there were, for an event: Hubo una fiesta. Never plural: Hubo dos bodas.
Between vowels in él and ellos: leyó, leyeron; oyó; creyó; cayó; construyó, construyeron
Only él and ellos, e → i or o → u: pidió, sintió, consiguió, durmió, murió, mintió; pidieron, durmieron
mil novecientos noventa y ocho (one number, never split in pairs)
a los 18 años: Se casó a los 25 años.
cumplir 30 años: Mañana cumplo 30.
en los años noventa / en la década de 1990
casarse con alguien: Se casó con Luis.
mudarse (a): Me mudé a Monterrey. (moverse = to move your body)
me gradúo, te gradúas, se gradúa, nos graduamos, se gradúan (written accent on the u)
la carrera = a university degree course (also career, race); el título = the degree you get at the end
aba, abas, aba, ábamos, aban: jugaba, jugábamos
ía, ías, ía, íamos, ían: tenía, vivíamos (accent on every í)
ser: era, eras, era, éramos, eran. ir: iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, iban. ver: veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veían.
None: quería, podía, dormía, pedía, jugaba.
there was / there were (background, what existed): Había un columpio. Never plural in this sense.
habits (Cada verano íbamos…), descriptions and feelings (era, tenía miedo), age and time (Tenía ocho años; Eran las tres)
the imperfect: Los domingos comíamos con mis abuelos. Or soler: solíamos comer.
suelo = I usually (present); solía = I used to (imperfect). Suelo levantarme temprano.
antes (adverb) = before, in the past: Antes vivía en Puebla. antes de + noun/infinitive: antes de comer.
ya no + verb: Ya no juego futbol.
de niño (de niña for a girl), en mi infancia
la primaria (six years), then la secundaria (three years); el recreo = recess; el patio = schoolyard

cards.front: Imperfect or preterite in a story?
cards.back: Imperfect = the scene (time, weather, descriptions, feelings), habits, actions in progress. Preterite = the events that move the story.
imperfect + cuando + preterite: Caminaba por el parque cuando vi a un hombre.
while; usually + imperfect: Mientras yo cocinaba, mi hermano ponía la mesa.
de repente, en ese momento, entonces, al final
conocí = I met (for the first time); conocía = I knew
supe = I found out; sabía = I knew
no quise = I refused; no quería = I didn't want to
pude = I managed to; podía = I was able to (in general)
tuve que = I had to (and did); tenía que = I was supposed to
¿Sabes qué me pasó? Te cuento… Resulta que…
¿En serio? ¡No me digas! ¡Qué susto! ¡Qué mala suerte! ¿Y luego?
Me robaron la cartera. (literally: they stole my wallet from me)
me caí, te caíste, se cayó, nos caímos, se cayeron
